title: Home › Format › Protect Sheet never offers Unprotect (re-protects instead); selectLockedCells ignored
author: oliverstreetcreative
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.7.0 (macOS 26.5)

> **Edited:** Earlier versions of this issue got the details wrong. Root cause below.

**File:** an `.xlsx` timesheet template, with its one sheet protected and **no password**:

```xml
<sheetProtection sheet="1" objects="1" scenarios="1" selectLockedCells="1"/>
```

Editing the unlocked fill-in cells (`locked="0"`) works. The problem is getting protection *off*.

## 1. Home › Format › "Protect Sheet…" never becomes "Unprotect Sheet…"

**Steps:** Open the protected sheet, choose Home › Format › Protect Sheet…, click OK, then try to edit a locked cell.

**Expected (Excel):** On a protected sheet, this menu item reads **Unprotect Sheet…** and removes protection. With no password, it does so without asking.

**Actual:** The item always opens the **Protect Sheet** dialog (password, "Allow all users of this sheet to…"). Clicking OK runs `review.protectSheet`, which replaces the existing protection with new options, so the sheet stays protected and nothing visibly changes.

**Cause:** `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` hard-codes `("Protect Sheet…", "dialog:protectSheet", …)` in the Home › Format menu. The keytips do the same: `HOP` and `RPS` in `keytips/keytip_table/generated.rs` both map to `Action::Dialog("protectSheet")`, and so does the keytip on the Review button (`control_keytip(app, ui, &__k, "dialog:protectSheet")`). The Review › Protect Sheet button and the sheet-tab context menu (`tabs.rs`) do check `is_protected()` and switch to Unprotect correctly. The other entry points should do the same.

## 2. `selectLockedCells="1"` is ignored

**Expected:** Locked cells can't be selected, so the cursor moves only among unlocked cells, as in Excel and LibreOffice.

**Actual:** GridCraft selects locked cells and refuses only on edit. The importer reads the flag (`sheet_read.rs`: `select_locked: !e.flag("selectLockedCells", false)`), so the selection code probably doesn't consult `select_locked`.

Related: `protect_sheet` in `review.r…

title: [Bug] Text format is lost when editing a cell containing a leading apostrophe
author: Gunz52
body:
Steps to reproduce on Gridcraft - Version 0.7.0 · Oct 14, 2026

Enter '00123 into a cell and press Enter.

Verify that the cell displays 00123 as text.

Reopen the cell for editing without changing its contents.

Press Enter to confirm the cell without making any changes.

Actual result:

The cell displays 123 instead of 00123. The leading apostrophe disappears when the cell enters edit mode, and the content is subsequently interpreted as a number, causing the leading zeros to be lost.

Expected result:

The cell should retain the text value 00123, even after being reopened and confirmed without any changes.

Additional details:

The initial entry is handled correctly, but the text format appears to be lost when the cell is reopened for editing. The issue seems to occur because the application removes the leading apostrophe without preserving the cell's original text type.

This causes an unintended conversion from text to a numeric value, even when the user has not modified the cell's contents.

title: fix(keyboard): on a Croatian or German keyboard, Ctrl+; (Ctrl+Shift+,) decreases the font size instead of inserting today’s date
author: vedran-dobos
body:
## Summary

Excel (English interface) reads shortcuts with punctuation by the character the keyboard layout types. On a Croatian or German layout `;` is Shift+, and `:` is Shift+., so Excel inserts today’s date with Ctrl+Shift+, and the time with Ctrl+Shift+.

GridCraft matches these keys by their position on a US keyboard instead. Ctrl+Shift+, is the US Ctrl+< (Decrease Font Size), and Ctrl+Shift+. the US Ctrl+> (Increase Font Size). The date is only reachable with Ctrl+Č / Ctrl+Ö, the key in the US `;` position.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows, keyboard layout Croatian (or German), GridCraft interface in English.
2. Select a cell and press Ctrl+Shift+, (the keys that type `;`).
3. Press Ctrl+Shift+. (the keys that type `:`).

## Expected behavior

Step 2 starts editing the cell with today’s date, step 3 with the current time, as Excel does with the same keyboard.

## Actual behavior

Step 2 decreases the font size, step 3 increases it. Ctrl+Č (Croatian) / Ctrl+Ö (German) inserts the date.

The same mix-up hits the other punctuation shortcuts on these layouts:
- Ctrl++ (`+` without Shift on both layouts) does nothing; on a US keyboard Ctrl+Shift+= (`+`) opens Insert.
- Ctrl+' (the US `-` key on Croatian, Shift+# on German) does nothing instead of copying the formula from the cell above.
- Ctrl+Shift+0 (it types `=` on both layouts) opens Insert instead of unhiding columns.

## Runtime or environment

GridCraft `main` at d9d09f0 (0.7.0), built from source on Windows 11 with Rust 1.99.0; Croatian keyboard layout.

## Additional context

- Cause: `keymap::lookup` matches non-navigation keys by `physical_key` (the US position), while `ribbon::shortcut` gets the logical key; for Ctrl+Shift+, egui reports `key: Semicolon, physical_key: Comma`, and `lookup` sees Ctrl+Shift+Comma first. Ctrl+Shift+0 on these layouts goes the other way: `lookup` sees the digit, but `ribbon::shortcut` gets `=` with Shift and opens Insert.
- Digits are a different case and should keep thei…

title: fix(format): Decrease Font Size jumps from 8 pt straight to 1 pt, and Increase Font Size goes past 72 to 96 and 409
author: vedran-dobos
body:
## Summary

Home › Decrease Font Size (Ctrl+Shift+<) steps 11 → 10 → 9 → 8 and then jumps straight to 1 pt,
which makes the text practically invisible. Increase Font Size (Ctrl+Shift+>) from 1 pt jumps back
to 8. Going up, the shortcut skips 22 and 26 (which the ribbon's Font Size list has) and goes on
past 72 to 96 and then 409.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New workbook, select A1 (11 pt) and type some text.
2. Press Ctrl+Shift+< (or click Home › Font › Decrease Font Size) repeatedly: 10, 9, 8, **1**.
3. Press Ctrl+Shift+> once: **8**.
4. Keep pressing Ctrl+Shift+>: 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 36, 48, 72, **96, 409**.

## Expected behavior

Excel (Microsoft 365, Windows, observed) steps along its Font Size list, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16,
18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 36, 48, 72, and stops at both ends: Decrease does nothing at 8 and Increase
does nothing at 72. Presumably this keeps text from shrinking to an unreadable size by accident.
Smaller and larger sizes are typed into the Font Size box.

A gentler alternative to Excel's stop at 8 would be one point at a time below 8 (8 → 7 → … → 1 and
back up 1 → 2 → … → 8), so the shortcut can still reach small sizes without the jump.

## Actual behavior

Decrease goes from 8 to 1 in one step, Increase from 1 to 8; Increase skips 22 and 26 and
continues past 72 to 96 and 409.

## Runtime or environment

GridCraft `main` at d9d09f0 (0.7.0), built from source on Windows 11 with Rust 1.99.0.

## Additional context

The steps come from `SIZES` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` (`step_font`):
`[8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 36, 48, 72, 96, 409]`, with 1 as the fallback below
the first entry. The ribbon's size list (`size_combo` in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`) already
has 22 and 26 and ends at 72. A PR will follow.

title: Feature Request: Change font family and size using the mouse wheel
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
This is a feature request, not a bug report: GridCraft does not currently support this, and as far as I can see it was never implemented.

### Use case

On the Home tab, the Font Family and Font Size boxes can only be changed by clicking them, then picking from the list or typing a value. The mouse wheel does nothing over either box, so comparing a few fonts or sizes on the same cells takes a click and a pick each time.

### Proposed behavior

- **Font Family:** with the pointer over the box, each wheel notch applies the previous or next font in the Font list straight to the selected cells.
- **Font Size:** with the pointer over the box, each notch makes the selected cells' font larger or smaller, for example in the same steps as Increase/Decrease Font Size.
- Each box shows the new value as soon as it changes.
- **Priority over ribbon tab switching:** #897 / PR #899 propose that the wheel over the ribbon switches tabs. Over these two boxes, the wheel should change the font or size instead. Everywhere else on the ribbon it would still switch tabs as that PR proposes.

### Current behavior (steps)

1. Open a new workbook and select A1 (Calibri 11).
2. On the Home tab, hover over the Font Family box and turn the wheel up and down.
3. Do the same over the Font Size box.

A1 stays Calibri 11, and so do both boxes.

### Environment

- GridCraft 0.7.0, Flatpak, Linux (CachyOS)
- Also checked against the `v0.7.0` source (see below)

### Technical findings

- `font_combo` and `size_combo` in `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` are plain buttons that open `editable_combo`. Nothing in that path reads wheel input, so the Number Format box doesn't respond either.
- I wrote an `egui_kittest` probe, using the same harness as `tests/wheel_zoom.rs`, that sends wheel notches (line and point units, both directions) over each box on `v0.7.0`. The cell stays Calibri 11. In the same harness, `home.increaseFontSize` changes it to 12.

title: Feature request: Excel-style in-cell lists and nested arrays (Compatibility Version 3)
author: zenogrid-law80
body:
## Summary

Please add support for Excel's new in-cell lists, array-valued cells, and nested arrays, announced for the Windows/Mac Beta Channels on September 24, 2026:

[Microsoft: Put multiple values in one cell with lists and arrays in Excel](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft365insiderblog/put-multiple-values-in-one-cell-with-lists-and-arrays-in-excel/4559395).

The goal is to keep related values together as structured data, rather than comma-separated text or a mandatory spill range. Example use cases include several owners per task and a variable number of split times per run.

## Requested behavior

- Create, inspect, and edit a list in one cell; filter by individual list items. Excel exposes Insert > List / Ctrl+J and editing through F2.
- Keep a formula's array result in one cell with an outer brace wrapper, e.g. `={{1;2;3}}`. Referencing a list cell should expose its values for calculations or spilling.
- Preserve arrays inside arrays, e.g. `={{1,2,3};{4,5,6}}`, including nested results from supported formulas, without silently taking only the first item.
- Add `FLATTEN(array, [pad_value], [levels])`, `HAS(array, value)`, `HASANY(array, values)`, and `HASALL(array, values)`.
- Provide workbook-level calculation compatibility: Microsoft requires Compatibility Version 3 for most nested-array calculations and retains versions 1/2 for older behavior. The announced feature is still a preview.

This could be delivered in stages: value/parser/evaluator support and functions, then cell UI/filtering and file interoperability. Add regression coverage for mixed item types, unequal inner lengths, empty/error values, and bounded nesting/work. Preserve existing workbook behavior unless the new calculation mode is selected; document any XLSX limitations explicitly.

title: Show a scrolled-away table's header names and filter buttons in the column headings (Excel Tables; WPS also for AutoFilter ranges)
author: tisca26
body:
When a filtered table or range is scrolled so its header row is off screen, show the header names and their filter buttons in the column headings (where A, B, C… are), so you can filter without scrolling back to the top.

## What Excel does (Tables only)

Observed in Excel for Mac 16.114. Select a cell inside a Table (Insert › Table, ⌘T) and scroll down until the table's header row is off screen. The column letters over the table's columns are replaced by the header names, and each one shows its filter button, which opens the usual AutoFilter dropdown.

```
Scrolled to row 480, header row (3) off screen:

     │ A │ Bank ▾ │ Date ▾ │ Type ▾ │ Amount ▾ │ Ref ▾ │ J │
─────┼───┼────────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────┼───┤
 480 │   │ …      │ …      │ …      │ …        │ …     │   │
```

Columns outside the table keep their letters. GridCraft doesn't do this yet: the column letters stay, and filtering means scrolling back up to the header row.

## Going one step further: plain AutoFilter ranges

Excel only does this for Tables. A range filtered with Data › Filter (`<autoFilter>` on the sheet, no Table) keeps its letters. Many everyday workbooks are exactly that: a header row and Data › Filter, never converted to a Table. WPS Spreadsheets shows the header names and filter buttons in the column headings for plain AutoFilter ranges too, and in daily use it's a big time saver. In long lists, the filter is the thing you reach for most, and it's always the farthest away.

So the proposal:
1. **Excel parity:** Tables show their header names and filter buttons in the column headings when the header row is scrolled out of view.
2. **Beyond Excel (optional, maybe a setting):** the same for a sheet's AutoFilter range.

## Details worth deciding

- **When it shows:** in Excel I observed it with a cell inside the table selected. Whether it also shows with the selection outside the table is worth checking before implementing.

title: Keyboard: no Show Outline Symbols (Ctrl+8) and no Next Corner of Selection (Ctrl+.)
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel has two keyboard features, in every language, that GridCraft has no command for. Ctrl+8 shows and hides the outline symbols (the band with the group brackets and level buttons), and Ctrl+. moves the active cell to the next corner of the selection. In GridCraft both keys do nothing. The outline setting is also saved per sheet, and GridCraft drops it when it opens and saves a file.

## Measured

| Feature | English Excel (Microsoft's list) | German Excel (measured) | GridCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Show / hide the outline symbols | Ctrl+8 | Strg+7 | no command; Ctrl+8 does nothing |
| Move the active cell to the next corner of the selection | Ctrl+. | Strg+' (Strg+Umschalt+#) | no command; Ctrl+. does nothing |

Excel for Microsoft 365 with a German interface and keyboard, B2:C3 selected, B2 active:
- **Strg+7** turns the outline symbols off, and the second press turns them on again (`Window.DisplayOutline`). The outline itself stays.
- **Strg+Umschalt+#** moves the active cell B2 → C2 → C3 → B3 → B2 (clockwise). The selection stays.

## Steps to reproduce

```
$ gridcraft-cli commands --search corner
0 commands
$ gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'view.outlineSymbols={}' --quiet
gridcraft-cli: step 1 (--cmd, view.outlineSymbols): unknown command `view.outlineSymbols`
```

The file setting is lost: a workbook whose `sheet1.xml` has `<sheetView showOutlineSymbols="0" workbookViewId="0"/>` and rows 2:3 at `outlineLevel="1"`, run through `gridcraft-cli convert outline.xlsx out.xlsx`, comes back with `<sheetView tabSelected="1" workbookViewId="0">`. The outline band shows again in Excel.

In the app: group rows 2:3 (Data › Group), select B2:C3 and press Ctrl+8 or Ctrl+.: nothing happens.

title: Keyboard: Ctrl+Q closes GridCraft at once on Windows and Linux, and unsaved work is lost
author: iluebbe
body:
On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Q closes the GridCraft window immediately. Nothing asks to save, so unsaved work is gone. Ctrl+Shift+Q and Ctrl+Alt+Q do the same. In Excel for Windows, Ctrl+Q is Quick Analysis (#791) and never quits. On a German keyboard, AltGr+Q types `@` and Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so typing an e-mail address may close the window too.

## Observed

| Keys | Excel for Windows | GridCraft 0.7.0 (Windows, Linux) |
|---|---|---|
| Ctrl+Q | Quick Analysis | closes the window, no save prompt |
| Ctrl+Shift+Q, Ctrl+Alt+Q | — | closes the window, no save prompt |
| AltGr+Q on a German keyboard (`@`) | types `@` | Ctrl+Alt+Q, see above (checked in the egui test harness, not with a German keyboard in the running app) |
| Cmd+Q on macOS | Quit (menu bar) | closes the window (stays: it is the app's Quit there) |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start GridCraft on Windows or Linux and type something into a cell.
2. Press Ctrl+Q: the window closes. Restart: the input is gone.

## Cause

- egui closes the root viewport on `Options::quit_shortcuts`, which defaults to Command+Q, i.e. Ctrl+Q on Windows/Linux (egui 0.36.2, `memory/mod.rs`). `Context::end_pass` consumes it with `consume_shortcut`, which matches modifiers logically: extra Shift and Alt are ignored. Then it sends `ViewportCommand::Close`.
- GridCraft turns off egui's other built-in keys (`zoom_with_keyboard`, [lib.rs L1048–1052](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b349708ab4978cb3f061f6bd6ecbc25667cb/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1048-L1052)) but leaves `quit_shortcuts` at the default. Neither `keymap::lookup` nor `ribbon::shortcut` binds Ctrl+Q, so the key reaches `end_pass`.
- The app cancels a close request only while printing ([apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs L44–46](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b349708ab4978cb3f061f6bd6ecbc25667cb/apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs#L44-L46)). Closing the window never asks to save (#694, #1172, #1410).

title: XLSX: What-If scenarios are dropped on open, and scenarios made in GridCraft are invisible to Excel
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel keeps Scenario Manager scenarios in the worksheet XML as `<scenarios>` on the sheet that holds their changing cells. GridCraft doesn't read or write that element:

- **Opening an Excel file drops its scenarios.** `data.scenarioManager` lists none, and the next save writes the file without them. A model with Base / Bull / Bear cases loses them silently.
- **Scenarios added in GridCraft are invisible to Excel.** They are stored in a hidden workbook-scope defined name `_sc_scenarios` whose formula is a quoted JSON string. Excel's Scenario Manager shows nothing, and the file carries a long string name that no other tool understands.

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 writes, after Data › What-If Analysis › Scenario Manager:

```xml
<scenarios current="1" show="1" sqref="C28:C32">
  <scenario name="Base" locked="1" count="1" user="Analyst" comment="Base case">
    <inputCells r="C4" val="Base"/>
  </scenario>
  ...
</scenarios>
```

- `current`: the scenario selected in the manager; `show`: the scenario last shown (0-based); `sqref`: the result cells of the last Summary.
- `locked="1"` is Excel's default for a new scenario (Prevent changes); `hidden="1"` when Hide is checked.
- `val` holds the value as it would be typed: `100`, `3`, `0.085`, `Base` (no trailing `.0`).
- The element sits after `<protectedRanges>` and before `<autoFilter>` (ECMA-376 `CT_Worksheet` order).

Excel reads `<scenarios>` written in this shape back: a copy of an Excel-made DCF workbook (Base / Bull / Bear on `$C$4`, results `C28:C32`), written with `<scenarios current="1" show="1" sqref="C28:C32">` and the three scenarios, opened in Excel, and Excel's Scenario Manager listed Base, Bull and Bear.

| | Excel | GridCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Open a file with three scenarios in `<scenarios>` | Scenario Manager lists them | `data.scenarioManager` → `{"scenarios":[]}` |
| Save that file again | `<scenarios>` kept | `<scenarios>` gone |
| Add a scenario, save | `<scenarios>` in the sheet | h…

title: UI: Data › What-If Analysis › Scenario Manager… opens no dialog
author: iluebbe
body:
In Excel, Data › What-If Analysis › Scenario Manager… opens a dialog where scenarios are listed, shown, added, edited, deleted and summarised. In GridCraft the menu item (and the key tip Alt, A, W, S) runs the `data.scenarioManager` list query, and its result goes nowhere: nothing visible happens. The engine already has every scenario command (`data.scenarioManager`, `data.scenarioAdd`, `data.scenarioShow`, `data.scenarioDelete`, `data.scenarioSummary`), but they are reachable only through the control channel, the CLI and MCP. `docs/ui-parity.md` lists the Scenario Manager among the dialogs that exist.

## Excel's dialogs

Excel for Microsoft 365:

- **Scenario Manager**: the active sheet's scenarios in a list. Below it, the selected scenario's changing cells and comment. Buttons: Show, Add…, Delete, Edit…, Merge…, Summary…, Close.
  - Show writes the scenario's values into its changing cells and leaves the dialog open. Double-clicking a scenario shows it too.
  - With no scenarios, the list shows a short hint to use Add.
  - Summary… asks for the result cells (default: the current selection), adds the report sheet and closes the manager.
- **Add Scenario / Edit Scenario**: scenario name, changing cells (e.g. `B2:B4`, `C4,D7`, `$C$4`; at most 32 cells), comment. OK opens the second step.
- **Scenario Values**: one field per changing cell, labelled with its absolute address. Add prefills them with the cells' current values; Edit prefills them with the scenario's own values. OK stores the scenario and returns to the Scenario Manager.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `gridcraft --sample sales`
2. Data › What-If Analysis › Scenario Manager… (or press Alt, A, W, S).
3. Nothing opens. The same happens on a sheet that has scenarios (added with `data.scenarioAdd` through the control channel).

## Cause

- The ribbon maps the menu item and its key tip to the engine query, not to a dialog: [`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs#L1963`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b34970…

title: CSV and text import: delimiter, `sep=` line, quotes, apostrophes and `1,5E3` are read unlike Excel
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel reads a CSV file the same way whether it is opened with File › Open or imported with Data › From Text/CSV: it detects the delimiter, honours a `sep=` first line, keeps field text as text and gives dates, percentages and currency their number formats. GridCraft has three separate tokenizers (File › Open, paste, Text to Columns) and a From Text/CSV command that does its own delimiter guess and then retypes every field through `range.setValues`. The result: a German `;` file imported with From Text/CSV splits at the decimal commas, `=1+1` becomes a live formula, apostrophes in Dutch place names disappear, a quote inside a field swallows the rest of the line in Text to Columns, and `1,5E3` (German for 1500) becomes 15000. Several of these change numbers without any warning.

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 on Windows (de-DE UI), through File › Open, Data › From Text/CSV, Text to Columns, NUMBERVALUE and TEXTSPLIT, with about 60 variant files: delimiters `,` `;` TAB `|`, quoting, line ends, BOMs, en-US / de-DE / fr / de-CH / en-IN / zh-CN numbers and dates, Windows-1252 / UTF-16 / GB18030. GridCraft column: 0.7.0 (`e6b6b34`) through `gridcraft-cli`.

title: PivotTables in XLSX: unopenable files, dropped fields and changed layouts after a GridCraft save
author: iluebbe
body:
PivotTables that GridCraft saves, or opens and saves again, don't survive in Excel. A TRUE/FALSE column anywhere in the source makes a file Excel can't open at all, not even with repair. title: Options: no way to set the user name, and a save doesn't record who saved the workbook or when
author: iluebbe
body:
In Excel, File › Options › General holds the user name. It signs new notes and comments, becomes the author of a new workbook, and is recorded as *Last Modified By* on every save, together with the save time. GridCraft has a user name (`Prefs::user_name`) that signs notes and comments, but it starts as `GridCraft User` and nothing in the desktop app or the command set changes it; only the web build's `?author=` does. A save records neither who saved nor when. Worse, `cp:lastModifiedBy`, `dcterms:created` and `dcterms:modified` are dropped when a file is opened, so an Excel file saved in GridCraft loses its *Last Modified By* and both dates.

## Excel's behaviour

From Excel's public documentation (not measured):

- File › Options › General › *Personalize your copy of Microsoft Office* › *User name*.
- The user name becomes the author of new workbooks and the *Last Modified By* of every save.
- `docProps/core.xml` holds `dc:creator`, `cp:lastModifiedBy`, `dcterms:created` and `dcterms:modified`; the dates are W3CDTF (`xsi:type="dcterms:W3CDTF"`, e.g. `2026-10-14T13:45:00Z`).
- File › Info lists *Related Dates* (Created, Last Modified) and *Related People* (Author, Last Modified By).

| | Excel | GridCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Set the user name | File › Options › General | no field in Options; `options.userName` doesn't exist; only `?author=` on the web |
| Author of a new note | the user name | `GridCraft User` |
| First save of a new workbook | Author, Last Modified By, Created, Modified set | `core.xml` has none of them |
| Open a file with Last Modified By and dates, save it | Last Modified By and Modified updated, Created kept | all three removed |
| File › Info | Created, Last Modified, Author, Last Modified By | Author (an editable field); no dates, no Last Modified By |

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'options.userName={"name":"Ann"}'
# gridcraft-cli: step 1 (--cmd, options.userName): unknown command `options.userName`

gridcraft-cli r…

title: Outline: Group never asks Rows or Columns, − / + leave the cell editor open, no-op steps in Undo
author: iluebbe
body:
Follow-up to #373. When the selection is a range of cells rather than whole rows or columns, Excel's Group and Ungroup ask whether to act on its rows or its columns. GridCraft's ribbon buttons, shortcuts, key tips and Data menu group or ungroup the rows without asking. Three smaller outline problems remain as well:

- Clicking − or + while a cell is being edited leaves the editor open over a hidden row.
- Show Detail, Hide Detail and Ungroup add an undo step when there is nothing to act on.
- Ungroup with a selection that ends on the summary row leaves that row marked collapsed in the saved file.

title: Number formats: CELL("format") and AutoFill misread codes like [Red]0 as scientific or as dates
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel reports a cell's number format through `CELL("format")`, `CELL("color")` and `CELL("parentheses")`, and AutoFill uses the format to decide whether a single number is a date. GridCraft decides both by searching the code text for letters. An `e` anywhere (with a `0` somewhere) makes a format scientific, and a `d` or `y` anywhere makes it a date, even inside a colour tag or a quoted literal (`0 "days"` is `D1`). So `[Red]0` (the "e" and "d" of "Red") is `S0` for CELL and a date for AutoFill. Dates are always `D1` and times with hours always `D9`, and `CELL("color")` and `CELL("parentheses")` always return 0. Formulas that test `CELL("format")` (for example to tell dates from numbers) give wrong answers, and filling a red-formatted number counts up instead of copying it.

## Measured

- Excel: a German Excel for Microsoft 365 computed `CELL("format")`, `CELL("color")` and `CELL("parentheses")` for 104 format codes in a workbook GridCraft wrote. Its codes map one-to-one to the English ones: S → G, `.` → `,`, W → C, E → S, U1–U4 → D6–D9. German Excel reports `$` formats with `.` (`,`) because `$` isn't its currency; for those rows the table shows C, the en-US letter from Microsoft's CELL documentation.
- GridCraft 0.7.0 (= `main` e6b6b34): 5 in A1 with the format, `=CELL("format",A1)` through `gridcraft-cli run`.

| Format code | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `General` | G | G ✓ |
| `[Red]General` | G | D1 |
| `@` | G | F0 |
| `0.00` | F2 | F2 ✓ |
| `0.0#` | F2 | F1 |
| `#.##` | F2 | F0 |
| `#,##0` | ,0 | ,0 ✓ |
| `#,##0.0#` | ,2 | ,1 |
| `$#,##0_);($#,##0)` | C0 | C0 ✓ |
| `$#,##0_);[Red]($#,##0)` | C0- | S0 |

title: Number formats: [Color1]–[Color56] paint black and [Green] paints dark green (008000)
author: iluebbe
body:
In Excel, a colour tag in a number format picks a colour from the legacy 56-colour palette. `[ColorN]` is palette colour N, and the eight named colours are its first eight entries, so `[Green]` is bright green 00FF00, the same as `[Color4]`. GridCraft paints every `[ColorN]` black, in the grid and in PDF export, and paints `[Green]` as 008000. A format like `0;[Color10]-0` (dark green negatives) shows black negatives, and `[Green]` text looks different from Excel's.

## Measured

- Excel for Microsoft 365: `Range.DisplayFormat.Font.Color` of a cell holding 5 with the format `<tag>0`.
- GridCraft 0.7.0 (= `main` e6b6b34): the same cells exported with `file.exportPdf`, read from the text colour (`rg`) in the page content. The grid uses an identical colour table (see Cause).

| Tag | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| `[Black]` | 000000 | 000000 ✓ |
| `[White]` | FFFFFF | FFFFFF ✓ |
| `[Red]` | FF0000 | FF0000 ✓ |
| `[Green]` | 00FF00 | 008000 |
| `[Blue]` | 0000FF | 0000FF ✓ |
| `[Yellow]` | FFFF00 | FFFF00 ✓ |
| `[Magenta]` | FF00FF | FF00FF ✓ |
| `[Cyan]` | 00FFFF | 00FFFF ✓ |
| `[Color1]` | 000000 | 000000 ✓ |
| `[Color3]` | FF0000 | 000000 |
| `[Color 3]` | FF0000 | 000000 |
| `[COLOR5]` | 0000FF | 000000 |
| `[Color10]` | 008000 | 000000 |
| `[Color17]` | 9999FF | 000000 |
| `[Color46]` | FF6600 | 000000 |
| `[Color56]` | 333333 | 000000 |

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1:A3","values":[[5],[6],[7]]}' \
  --cmd 'home.numberFormat={"range":"A1","code":"[Green]0"}' \
  --cmd 'home.numberFormat={"range":"A2","code":"[Color10]0"}' \
  --cmd 'home.numberFormat={"range":"A3","code":"[Color46]0"}' \
  --cmd 'file.exportPdf={"path":"colors.pdf"}'
```

The page content draws "5" after `0 0.502 0 rg` (008000), and "6" and "7" after `0 0 0 rg` (black). Excel paints 00FF00, 008000 and FF6600. The grid's colour table (see Cause) gives the same colours as the PDF.

title: Charts: box & whisker boxes use inclusive quartiles while the file says exclusive
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel's box & whisker chart has a quartile setting (Format Data Series › Quartile Calculation: Exclusive median, the default, or Inclusive median). It is saved per series as `cx:statistics@quartileMethod`. Excel draws the box from QUARTILE.EXC for Exclusive and from QUARTILE.INC for Inclusive. GridCraft always draws inclusive quartiles, but writes `quartileMethod="exclusive"` for every box & whisker chart. A chart made in GridCraft therefore shows a different box in Excel than in GridCraft. An inclusive chart from Excel is drawn correctly, but GridCraft saves it back as exclusive, so Excel then draws it differently.

## Measured

- Excel for Microsoft 365: charts exported as PNG, box edges converted to values, calibrated at the whisker caps (which sit at the minimum and maximum).
- GridCraft 0.7.0 (= `main` e6b6b34): a chart from `insert.chart {type: "boxWhisker"}`, exported with `file.exportPdf`; box edges read from the PDF's box rectangle against the axis gridlines.

Box edges, Q1 to Q3:

| Data | Excel, Exclusive (default) | Excel, Inclusive | GridCraft (always) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–5 | 1.5 to 4.5 | 2 to 4 | 2 to 4 |
| 1–6 | 1.75 to 5.25 | 2.25 to 4.75 | 2.25 to 4.75 |
| 1–7 | 2 to 6 | 2.5 to 5.5 | 2.5 to 5.5 |
| 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 | – | 1.25 to 4.5 | 1.25 to 4.5 |

Excel's values are QUARTILE.EXC and QUARTILE.INC of the data. GridCraft's worksheet functions already compute both: `=QUARTILE.EXC({1,2,3,4,5,6},1)` gives 1.75, `=QUARTILE.INC({1,2,3,4,5,6},1)` gives 2.25.

Files, values 1–6:

| `quartileMethod` in the file | Excel 365 draws | GridCraft draws | GridCraft saves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exclusive` (what GridCraft writes) | 1.75 to 5.25 | 2.25 to 4.75 | `exclusive` |
| `inclusive` | 2.25 to 4.75 | 2.25 to 4.75 | `exclusive` |

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1:A7","values":[["v"],[1],[2],[3],[4],[5],[6]]}' \
  --cmd 'insert.chart={"range":"A1:A7","type":"boxWhisker","at":"C2"}' \

title: Borders and validation: mediumDashDotDot becomes thin, unknown names are silently replaced
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel has 13 border line styles, named `thin` … `slantDashDot` in SpreadsheetML. GridCraft's model has all 13, and the xlsx reader and writer know them all. But the names of `BorderStyle`, `CfOperator` and `ValidationKind` are spelled out again in each command and dialog, and those copies disagree:

- `home.borders` doesn't know `mediumDashDotDot`. It draws a thin border instead and reports success. Any misspelt style does the same, also through the MCP tool `format_range`, whose `style` is a free string.
- `data.validation` turns an unknown operator into "between" and an unknown type into "Any value". A typo silently removes the check. `home.conditionalFormat` refuses an unknown operator.
- Format Cells › Border offers None and 6 of the 13 line styles. Hair and the dash-dot, dash-dot-dot, medium dashed and slanted styles are missing.

A command that gets a name it doesn't know should return an error, as `home.conditionalFormat` does, and not apply something else.

## Measured

GridCraft 0.7.0 (= `main` e6b6b34), through `gridcraft-cli run`:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `home.borders {"range": "B2", "preset": "bottom", "style": "mediumDashDotDot"}` | thin bottom border, saved as `style="thin"` |
| MCP `format_range {"range": "A1", "borders": {"preset": "bottom", "style": "mediumDashDotDot"}}` | thin bottom border, `isError: false` |
| `home.borders {"range": "B4", "preset": "bottom", "style": "wavy"}` | thin bottom border, no error |
| `home.borders {"range": "B2", "preset": "bogus"}` | nothing changes, no error |
| `data.validation {"type": "whole", "operator": "bigger", "formula1": "5"}` | a "between" rule with no upper bound: 7 is refused |
| `data.validation {"type": "integer", "operator": "greater", "formula1": "5"}` | saved as `type="none"` (Any value): "abc" is accepted |
| `home.conditionalFormat {"rule": {"type": "cellIs", "operator": "bigger", "value": "5"}}` | error: unknown operator `bigger` |

title: Wildcards: `~`, `İ` and Replace patterns differ from Excel in criteria, lookups, Find and filters
author: iluebbe
body:
GridCraft has two wildcard matchers:
- `crates/functions/src/criteria.rs` for COUNTIF and the other criteria functions, the D-functions, MATCH / VLOOKUP / XLOOKUP and SEARCH;
- a copy in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` (`edit::wildcard`) for Find & Replace, AutoFilter custom filters and Advanced Filter.

They disagree with each other, and each differs from Excel 365. Counts and lookups give other results than in Excel. Replace with a wildcard pattern reports a replacement but leaves the cell unchanged.

## Measured

The values `x~`, `y`, `ab`, `a~b`, `a*b`, `axb`, `İ`, `i`, `I`, `ı`, `ß`, `~`, `hello`, `HELLO`, `a?b`, `~x` and `xyz~` (A2:A18) were run in Excel 365 through:
- COUNTIF, MATCH, XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP and SEARCH;
- AutoFilter "equals";
- `Range.Find` (whole and part, with and without MatchCase);
- `Range.Replace`.

Excel ran with a German UI. GridCraft is 0.7.0 (`main` e6b6b34) through `gridcraft-cli run`.

| Case | Excel 365 | GridCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `=COUNTIF(A2:A18,"?~")` | 7: every one-character value (`y`, `İ`, `i`, `I`, `ı`, `ß`, `~`); the trailing `~` is dropped | 1 (`x~`) |
| AutoFilter equals `?~` or `?` | 7 rows shown | 6 (`İ` hidden) |
| `=MATCH("x~",A2:A18,0)` | `#N/A` (it looks for `x`) | 1 (`x~`) |
| `=COUNTIF(A5,"a~b")`, A5 = `a~b` | 1 (no `*` or `?`: compared as it is) | 0 |
| `=COUNTIF(A4,"a~b")`, A4 = `ab` | 0 | 1 |
| `=COUNTIF(A2:A18,"~~")` | 0 | 1 (`~`) |
| `=COUNTIF(A2:A18,"h~ello")` | 0 | 2 (`hello`, `HELLO`) |

| Find `a~b`, whole cell | finds `ab` | finds `a~b` |
| `=COUNTIF(A2:A18,"i")` | 2 (`i`, `I`) | 3 (also `İ`) |

| `=COUNTIF(A2:A18,"*~~")`, AutoFilter equals `*~~` | 3 | 3 ✓ |
| Replace `h*o` → `X` in `hello world` | `X world` | unchanged, reports 1 replaced |

title: GROUPBY / PIVOTBY: subtotals, sort orders, header rows and blank cells differ from Excel
author: iluebbe
body:
GROUPBY and PIVOTBY were compared with Excel 365 cell by cell, for every cell of every spill range of 271 formulas. The data had blanks, `""`, case variants, text numbers, `#N/A`, booleans, dates, negatives and duplicates. GridCraft matched 47 of the 271. The differences change totals, row order and the size of the spill range, so a report built on these functions looks different from Excel's and can push into neighbouring cells.

Sub-problems (each can be fixed and tested on its own):
- [ ] 1. A total depth of 2 or more adds no subtotals.
- [ ] 2. Sort orders: PIVOTBY ignores sorting by value. With several key columns, keys are sorted flat instead of within their groups. A list of sort columns uses only its first entry. `field_relationship` is ignored.
- [ ] 3. Header rows: detected headers are shown, PIVOTBY lacks the column-field row, an extra value-name row appears, and generated names are wrong.
- [ ] 4. Blanks: COUNTA skips blank values; a blank key shows blank instead of 0; cells laid out without a value are blank instead of empty text.
- [ ] 5. Several functions at once (`HSTACK(SUM,COUNT)`, `VSTACK(…)`) give `#NAME?`.
- [ ] 6. Arguments that Excel rejects with `#VALUE!` are accepted.
- [ ] 7. Case variants of one key are spelled differently on different lines.

## Measured

Excel 365 on Windows with a German UI. The labels below are English; see "Open questions" for the ones not checked in English Excel. GridCraft is 0.7.0 (`main` e6b6b34) through `gridcraft-cli eval`. `·` is an empty cell, `/` separates rows.

| same, depth `-2` | Grand Total · 6 / a · 3 / a x 1 / a y 2 / b · 3 / b x 3 | Total · 6 / a x 1 / a y 2 / b x 3 |

title: Financial functions: securities functions read dates as 1900 serials in a 1904 workbook
author: iluebbe
body:
In a workbook that uses the 1904 date system, Excel's securities functions read their date arguments in that system, as DATE and EOMONTH do. GridCraft's financial date helpers always use the 1900 system. A 1904 serial is therefore read 1,462 days (four years and a day) off, and day counts, coupon dates and year fractions come out wrong. Example: COUPNCD returns 30 May instead of 31 May, and ACCRINT accrues the wrong amount.

Affected:
- COUPPCD, COUPNCD, COUPDAYS, COUPDAYBS, COUPDAYSNC, COUPNUM;
- PRICE, YIELD, DURATION, MDURATION;
- DISC, PRICEDISC, YIELDDISC, INTRATE, RECEIVED;
- ACCRINT, ACCRINTM, PRICEMAT, YIELDMAT;
- ODDFPRICE, ODDFYIELD, ODDLPRICE, ODDLYIELD;
- TBILLPRICE, TBILLYIELD, TBILLEQ;
- AMORDEGRC, AMORLINC.

## Measured

Excel 365, a new workbook with `Date1904 = True`. GridCraft 0.7.0 (`main` e6b6b34), the same formulas evaluated with `gridcraft-cli eval --in` against a workbook with `<workbookPr date1904="1"/>`:

title: Sheet references: names like `.x`, `R1C1` or `A1` are left unquoted; Excel can't open the saved file
author: iluebbe
body:
Excel quotes a sheet name in a reference (`'My Sheet'!A1`) whenever the bare name could be read as something else. GridCraft quotes sheet names in three places with three different rules, and none matches Excel's:
- the formula printer;
- the engine's pivot code (also used by Solver);
- ADDRESS.

The worst case: a formula into a sheet whose name starts with `.` is saved as `.x!A1`, and Excel 365 can't open the file, not even with repair. The quotes are also taken off again in about eight places. The Name Box's copy doesn't read `''` as `'`.

## Measured

Excel 365's rule, from typing `='name'!A1` and reading `.Formula` back, and from `ADDRESS(1,1,1,TRUE,name)`. GridCraft is 0.7.0 (`main` e6b6b34): formulas through `cell.set` and the saved `<f>`, ADDRESS through `gridcraft-cli eval`.

| Sheet name | Excel formula | Excel ADDRESS | GridCraft formula | GridCraft ADDRESS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A1`, `XFD1`, `AB1048576` | quoted | quoted | quoted | **bare** |
| `XFE1`, `AB1048577` (off the sheet) | bare | bare | bare | bare |
| `R1`, `C1`, `RC1` (also A1 cells) | quoted | quoted | quoted | **bare** |
| `R`, `C`, `RC`, `R1C`, `R1C1`, `r2c3` | quoted | quoted | **bare** | **bare** |
| `.x` | quoted | quoted | **bare** | **bare** |
| `TRUE`, `false` | quoted | bare | quoted | bare |
| `Ärger`, `日本`, `Σ`, `Sheet.1`, `_x`, `A1A` | bare | bare | bare | bare |

So Excel quotes a name when:
- it starts with a digit or `.`;
- it holds anything other than letters (any script), digits, `_` and `.`;
- it reads as an A1 cell within the sheet's bounds;
- it reads as an R1C1 reference (`R`, `C`, `RC`, `R1`, `C1`, `R1C`, `RC1`, `R1C1`, in any case);
- it is a boolean. Excel's ADDRESS is the exception here and leaves `TRUE` / `FALSE` bare.

Effects in GridCraft 0.7.0:
- **Unreadable file:** `='.x'!A1` is saved as `<f>.x!A1</f>`. Excel 365 refuses to open the file, and its repair fails too. (`R1C1!A1` and `RC!A1` happen to be accepted by Excel.)
- **PivotTable source:** `insert.pivotTa…

title: Control channel: ui.dialog.confirm runs a dialog's command with the raw field values, not what OK sends
author: iluebbe
body:
Clicking OK in a dialog and confirming it over the control channel should run the same command with the same parameters. They don't. OK runs the command with `build_params(&d)`, which reshapes the field values for several dialogs. `ui.dialog.confirm` passes the raw field values instead. Agents and tests that drive dialogs through the control channel get different results from a user clicking OK, or an error.

## Affected dialogs

- **`cfQuick`** (Home › Conditional Formatting › Highlight Cells Rules): the values arrive without their `rule` wrapper. `home.conditionalFormat` sees no rule and asks for the `newFormattingRule` dialog again ([insert.rs L1340–1343](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b349708ab4978cb3f061f6bd6ecbc25667cb/crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L1340-L1343)), so no rule is added.
- **Every other dialog that `build_params` translates** gets its fields unconverted: Data Validation, Text to Columns, Remove Duplicates, Subtotal, Allow Edit Ranges, Zoom, Series and Define Name.

## Steps to reproduce

Over the control channel (`gridcraft --control 7979`):

1. `{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"range.setValues","params":{"range":"A1","values":[[1],[3]]}}}`
2. Select A1:A2 and open Home › Conditional Formatting › Highlight Cells Rules › Greater Than….
3. `{"id":2,"method":"ui.dialog.confirm","params":{}}`

No rule is added. Clicking OK in the same dialog adds the rule.

## Cause

- `ui.dialog.confirm` builds the parameters as `Json::Object(d.values.clone())` ([control.rs L255](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b349708ab4978cb3f061f6bd6ecbc25667cb/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L255)).
- OK uses `build_params(&d)` ([dialogs.rs L942](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/e6b6b349708ab4978cb3f061f6bd6ecbc25667cb/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L942)), which is private to `dialogs.rs`.

## Fix ideas

- Make `build_params` `pub(crate)` and call it from `ui.dialog.confirm`, so both paths send the same parameters.…

title: Feature Request – Italian Language Support (Localization)
author: Mike65-dot
body:
Hello GridCraft Development Team,

I am currently using GridCraft on Windows 11 and would like to suggest adding **Italian language support** to the application.

GridCraft is a promising alternative to Microsoft Excel, particularly for professional, technical and scientific applications.

However, the interface is currently available in English, which may limit its accessibility to Italian-speaking users.

1. Add Italian as a selectable interface language.
2. Translate menus, ribbon commands, dialog boxes, settings and chart formatting options.
3. Provide a language selection option under File → Options → Language.
4. Support Italian regional settings:
   - Date format: DD/MM/YYYY

Could you please confirm whether multilingual interface support is planned for a future GridCraft release?

Thank you for your continued development of GridCraft.

title: Printing / PDF export replaces Greek text with "?" (proposed fix attached)
author: plousbooks
body:
What happens
On Windows 11 (Greek), printing a sheet that contains Greek text turns every Greek letter into ?. Numbers and Latin text print fine. For example, a list of book titles prints as ????? ??????? while the ISBNs next to them come out correctly. PDF export does the same thing.

(Attach greek-before.png here.)

Why
crates/pdf sets all text in the 14 standard PDF fonts with WinAnsiEncoding. win_ansi() maps every character outside CP1252 to ?, so Greek, Cyrillic and other non-Latin text can't survive the print path. This is already listed as gap #5 in docs/gaps.md ("Text in non-Latin scripts doesn't render or export").

Proposed fix
A patch against e6b6b34 is attached (greek-printing.patch, apply with git apply). It keeps the PDF crate dependency-free:

crates/pdf/src/truetype.rs (new): a small, bounds-checked TrueType reader. It reads units per em, metrics, cmap format 4/12 and advance widths, and rejects CFF/.ttc files and fonts whose fsType forbids embedding.
crates/pdf/src/lib.rs: when a text run has characters WinAnsiEncoding can't carry and a fallback font is available, the run is set in an embedded CIDFontType2 font (Identity-H, CIDToGIDMap /Identity, a /W array of the glyphs used, and a ToUnicode CMap so the text stays searchable and copyable). Everything else is unchanged: Latin-only text still uses the standard fonts, and with no fallback font the output is the same ? as before. text_width measures those runs with the fallback font's real advances.
Fonts come from a loader the app registers with gridcraft_pdf::set_unicode_font_loader. It runs once, lazily, the first time a PDF needs it, and is re-exported as gridcraft_engine::pdf. Nothing is added to the repo, so this stays in line with the fonts standard.
crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs: pdf_unicode_fonts() picks the first regular/bold "cell" font candidate that parses and has Greek (Calibri/Arial on Windows and macOS, Liberation/DejaVu on Linux).
apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs: registers the loader at start…

title: XLSX save: a carriage return in cell text is written as a raw CR, so Excel (and GridCraft itself) reads it back as a line feed
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Summary.** Cell text that contains a carriage return (CR, U+000D) changes on save. Excel stores a CR in the shared strings as `_x000D_`; GridCraft decodes that correctly on open (`decode_xstring("a_x000D_b") == "a\rb"`), but writes the CR back as a raw character. XML end-of-line handling (XML 1.0 §2.11) turns every raw CR LF and every lone CR into a single LF before any application sees the text, so after a GridCraft save, Excel, openpyxl and GridCraft itself read `Line 1⏎Line 2` with LF only: the text is one character shorter, `LEN`, `FIND`, `SUBSTITUTE(…;CHAR(13);…)` and lookups on it give different results, and nothing reports the change. `gridcraft-cli check` sees it as a round-trip `values` difference.

Real files carry CR LF wherever text was pasted from other Windows programs (e-mail, PDF, ERP exports) or written by tools. In a corpus run over 400 real-world workbooks (see #891), `check` reports this round-trip change in 6 workbooks (30 cells: CR LF → LF in 4 workbooks, a lone CR → LF in 2); 4 more workbooks with `_x000D_` in their shared strings are among the 5 that GridCraft could not open within the 180 s limit of the run.

**Steps to reproduce.** Fixture `gc_text_cr.xlsx` (KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures, `gridcraft/`; written by `make_gc_scoreboard_fixtures.py`, standard library only, nothing created by Excel): sheet `Text`, A1 `Line 1` CR LF `Line 2`, A2 `Part A` CR `Part B`, A3 `Item 3` LF `Item 4` (control), stored as Excel stores them; B = `LEN(A)`, C = `CODE(MID(A,7,1))`.

```
gridcraft-cli run --in gc_text_cr.xlsx --out saved.xlsx
gridcraft-cli check gc_text_cr.xlsx --json
```
then open `saved.xlsx` in Excel and recalculate (Ctrl+Alt+F9).

**Expected** (Excel for Microsoft 365, de-DE, measured via COM, original and after a save by Excel): B1 14 · B2 13 · B3 13 · C1 13 · C2 13 · C3 10.

**Actual** (GridCraft 0.7.0). `saved.xlsx` holds `<t>Line 1` CR LF `Line 2</t>` with a raw CR byte; Excel reads A1 with 13 characters and LF only, A2 with LF instead of…

title: Calc: CELL("filename") is always empty and German info types ("dateiname", "adresse", …) give #VALUE!, so the sheet-name formula of German workbooks fails
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Summary.** Two gaps in `CELL`, both visible in real German workbooks:

1. `CELL("filename", ref)` returns an empty string even for a workbook opened from disk. Excel returns `<folder>\[<file>]<sheet>` once the workbook has been saved, and the classic formula for the sheet name, `=MID(CELL("filename",A1),FIND("]",CELL("filename",A1))+1,31)`, depends on it. In GridCraft it gives `#VALUE!` (FIND finds no `]`).
2. A German Excel writes the info type into the file as the user typed it: `ZELLE("Dateiname";A1)` is saved as `CELL("Dateiname",A1)`, `ZELLE("Adresse";A1)` as `CELL("Adresse",A1)` (the info type is a string, it is not translated like the function name). GridCraft only knows the English names, so every German info type is `#VALUE!`.

In a corpus run over 400 real-world workbooks from a German office (see #891), **83 workbooks (21 %) use `CELL` with a German info type** (6,931 calls, shared formulas counted once; almost all `"dateiname"` in the sheet-name formula), and 2 more workbooks use English ones (1,048 calls). `check` reports 1,197 mismatching cells with `CELL` in 80 of the 83 workbooks; the English case does not show up there, because `check` treats `CELL("filename")` as volatile.

title: XLSX save: line breaks and spaces inside formulas are removed (every formula is re-printed in compact form)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Summary.** Excel keeps a formula exactly as it was typed, including line breaks (Alt+Enter) and spaces, and people use that to make long formulas readable: one `IF` branch per line, `LET` with one name per line, spaces around operators. GridCraft parses the formula on open and writes it back from the parse tree on save, so every line break and every space outside string literals is gone after a save: `=IF(A1>0,⏎  "positive",⏎  "not positive")` becomes `=IF(A1>0,"positive","not positive")`. Results do not change, and `gridcraft-cli check` compares formulas in normalized form, so its round trip reports nothing; but the next person who opens the file in Excel finds a long formula collapsed into one line.

In a corpus run over 400 real-world workbooks (see #891), **109 workbooks (27 %) contain formulas with line breaks (197,815 formula cells, shared formulas counted once) and 97 contain formulas with runs of spaces**; after a GridCraft save none of them is left. In the same run, `roundtrip_formulas_kept` (formula text unchanged, `_xlfn.`/`_xlws.`/`_xlpm.` ignored) is below 1 for 105 of the 347 workbooks with formulas; all 105 contain such formulas (138,340 re-printed formula cells), the few other differences are cosmetic (the case of a user-defined function name, a redundant sheet prefix).

title: Calc: the spill operator on a dynamic-array formula that currently returns one value gives #REF! (ROWS(C1#), SUM(C1#))
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Summary.** In Excel a dynamic-array formula is always the anchor of a spill range, also while its result is a single value (a FILTER that currently matches one row, a SORT/UNIQUE over one item): `C1#` is then the 1 × 1 range C1, `ROWS(C1#)` is 1 and `SUM(C1#)` is the value. GridCraft returns `#REF!` for `C1#` in that case (and `COUNT(C1#)` gives 0), so every formula that counts or sums a filtered list breaks as soon as the list has exactly one entry. In a corpus run over 400 real-world workbooks (see #891) it shows up as `ROWS(…#)` → `#REF!` in 3 workbooks (12 cells); how often the single-value case occurs depends on the data on the day the file is opened.

**Steps to reproduce.** Fixture `gc_spill_single.xlsx` (KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures, `gridcraft/`; written by `make_gc_scoreboard_fixtures.py`, standard library only; dynamic-array cells stored as Excel 365 stores them, `cm="1"` + `xl/metadata.xml`): sheet `Spill`, A1:A5 = 1…5, B1:B5 = 7;
C1 `=FILTER(A1:A5,A1:A5>4)` (one value) · C3 `=SORT(FILTER(A1:A5,A1:A5=3))` (one value) · C5 `=UNIQUE(B1:B5)` (one value) · C9 `=FILTER(A1:A5,A1:A5>3)` (spills C9:C10, control);
E1 `=ROWS(C1#)` · E2 `=SUM(C1#)` · E3 `=ROWS(C3#)` · E5 `=COUNT(C5#)` · E9 `=ROWS(C9#)`.
```
gridcraft-cli check gc_spill_single.xlsx --json
```

**Expected** (Excel for Microsoft 365 de-DE, measured via COM; also after a GridCraft save): E1 1 · E2 5 · E3 1 · E5 1 · E9 2.

**Actual** (GridCraft 0.7.0): E1 `#REF!` · E2 `#REF!` · E3 `#REF!` · E5 0 · E9 2. `check --json`: 4 mismatches, signature `number → #REF!` (3) and `number → number` (1). The saved file keeps the dynamic-array flags, so Excel computes the right values again after a GridCraft save; GridCraft's own cached results in it are wrong until then.

title: XLSX save: a legacy INDEX(…, MATCH(…)) formula is written back as a dynamic-array formula (cm="1", t="array")
author: zengbo
body:
**Version:** gridcraft-cli 0.7.0 (release tarball `gridcraft-0.7.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`), Ubuntu, aarch64

**What happens**

A plain (pre-dynamic-array) formula that contains `INDEX(range, MATCH(...))` and returns a single value is written back as a dynamic-array formula on any `.xlsx` save: the cell gains `cm="1"`, the `<f>` gains `t="array" ref="<cell>"`, and `xl/metadata.xml` with `XLDAPR` is added. The source cell had no `cm`. The value is unchanged, but Excel 2019 and earlier now show the cell as a `{=…}` CSE array formula. Shared formulas (`t="shared" ref="F16:F39"`) are also split into one array formula per cell.

`VLOOKUP`, `SUM` and a bare `MATCH` on the same ranges are left as plain formulas, so the trigger looks like `INDEX` with a range argument being classified as possibly array-returning.

**Repro**

```python
# uv run --with openpyxl python repro.py
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); ws = wb.active
for i, (k, v) in enumerate([("a", 0.1), ("b", 0.4), ("c", 0.7)], start=1):
    ws[f"A{i}"], ws[f"B{i}"] = k, v
ws["D1"], ws["E1"] = "c", "x"
ws["F1"] = "=INDEX($B$1:$B$3,MATCH(D1,$A$1:$A$3,0))"
ws["F2"] = "=IFERROR(INDEX($B$1:$B$3,MATCH(D1,$A$1:$A$3,0)),0)"
ws["F3"] = '=IF(E1="","",INDEX($B$1:$B$3,MATCH(D1,$A$1:$A$3,0)))'
ws["F5"] = "=VLOOKUP(D1,$A$1:$B$3,2,FALSE)"
ws["F6"] = "=SUM($B$1:$B$3)"
ws["F7"] = "=MATCH(D1,$A$1:$A$3,0)"
wb.save("lookup.xlsx")
```

```sh
gridcraft-cli convert lookup.xlsx roundtrip.xlsx
unzip -p roundtrip.xlsx xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml | grep -o '<c r="F[0-9]"[^>]*><f[^>]*>'
```

**Expected:** all six formulas keep a plain `<f>` with no `cm`, as in the source.

**Actual:**

```
<c r="F1" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="F1">
<c r="F2" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="F2">
<c r="F3" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="F3">

<c r="F7"><f>
```

title: Bug: Filter Dropdown Loses Focus on Enter Key and Fails to Apply Filter
author: Lord-Taw
body:
## Summary

When using the filter dropdown, pressing the `Enter` key to apply a selected filter causes the dropdown component to lose focus unexpectedly. Instead of confirming and applying the selected filter, focus is transferred back to the spreadsheet/grid, causing subsequent keyboard interactions to affect the grid rather than the filter control.

## Current Behavior
1. Open a filter dropdown.
2. Navigate through filter options.
3. Select a filter value.
4. Press `Enter`.

### Result
- The dropdown loses focus.
- The filter is not applied.
- Keyboard focus returns to the grid/spreadsheet.
- Subsequent keyboard actions interact with the grid instead of the filter component.

## Expected Behavior
When the user presses `Enter` within an active filter dropdown:

- The currently selected filter option should be confirmed.
- The filter should be applied immediately.
- Focus must be transferred back to the spreadsheet.

## Technical Notes
The behavior suggests that the `Enter` key event is either:

- Not being correctly handled within the dropdown component.
- Bubbling to a parent grid handler.
- Triggering a focus restoration mechanism before the filter action is executed.
- Being intercepted by spreadsheet-level keyboard shortcuts or navigation listeners.

Recommended areas for investigation:

- Keyboard event propagation (`keydown`, `keyup`, `keypress`)
- Focus management between filter popover and grid
- Event cancellation (`preventDefault`, `stopPropagation`)
- Grid-level keyboard shortcuts bound to `Enter`
- Filter application lifecycle and state updates

title: Feature Request: Hierarchical Date Filtering for Date Columns
author: Lord-Taw
body:
## Summary

Implement hierarchical date filtering for columns containing date values, allowing users to navigate and filter dates through an expandable tree structure organized by **Year → Month → Day**.

This enhancement would improve usability when working with large datasets containing extensive date ranges and align the filtering experience with common spreadsheet and enterprise data grid solutions.

## Problem Statement

Currently, date values are presented as a flat list within the filter interface, making it difficult to locate specific dates in datasets spanning multiple months or years.

As the number of unique dates grows, filter navigation becomes increasingly inefficient and requires excessive scrolling.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a hierarchical filtering structure for date-based columns.

 │   ├─ 02

 │   └─ ...

```

title: [Audit] 5 defects with evidence and fix PRs: table filter criteria lost on save, printTitles wipes the other axis, cut leaves notes/merges behind, sort/dedupe orphan notes and links, NETWORKDAYS.INTL all-weekend string
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Round-4 audit: 5 defects on current `main` (e6b6b34), each with an independent fix PR carrying a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on the branch. (No crash findings this time — the engine crates are clean of `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` — these are silent data-loss and correctness defects.)

### 1. XLSX save drops a table's filter criteria: the rows stay hidden with no filter left — data loss
The engine's only live filter state is `sheet.autofilter` (a table's header dropdown installs it over the table's range); `Table::filter` is only filled by the reader. Writing suppressed the sheet `<autoFilter>` whenever a table intersected it and wrote the table part from the empty `Table::filter`, so a filtered table saved with rows hidden and no criteria anywhere; a slicer's selection was lost the same way.
**Fix:** #1531

### 2. `pageLayout.printTitles` wipes the axis it is not given — data loss
`print_titles` read both `rows`/`cols` as `Option`s and assigned both unconditionally, so `{"rows":"2:2"}` silently cleared the repeated columns. `pageLayout.pageSetup` already distinguishes "absent" from "empty"; the two commands disagreed about the same settings.
**Fix:** #1527

### 3. Cut + Paste leaves the source's notes, hyperlinks and merged areas behind — data corruption
One merged block became two (an empty one left behind) and a note ended up on both cells; hyperlinks were never transferred by paste at all. The cut now clears the source's comments/hyperlinks/merges and paste carries hyperlinks (new `What::Hyperlinks`, so `pasteSpecial {"what":"hyperlinks"}` works like `"comments"`).
**Fix:** #1534

### 4. Sort and Remove Duplicates leave the rows' notes and hyperlinks at their old cells — data corruption
A note describing one record annotated whatever landed on that row; a note on a removed row annotated blanks. Both maps now travel through the same permutation the cells use.
**Fix:** #1535

title: Feature Request: Hover Highlight & Cascading Context Menu Navigation
author: Lord-Taw
body:
## Summary

Improve the usability and discoverability of the context menu by:

1. Automatically highlighting the menu item currently under the mouse cursor.
2. Displaying submenu indicators for items that contain child actions.
3. Opening submenus in a cascading side-panel layout, similar to other desktop applications.

This enhancement aims to improve visual feedback, reduce navigation errors, and provide a more familiar user experience.

---

## Problem Statement

Currently, when the user opens the context menu (right-click), it can be difficult to quickly identify which option is being targeted, especially in menus with many entries.

Additionally, menu items that contain nested actions are not visually differentiated enough from regular actions, making submenu discovery less intuitive.

---

## Proposed Behavior

### 1. Hover State Highlighting

When the cursor moves over a menu item:

- Apply a distinct visual hover state.
- The hovered item should be immediately highlighted.
- Only one menu item can be highlighted at a time.
- The highlight should follow cursor movement without requiring a click.

#### Suggested UI States

| State | Visual Style |
|---------|------------|
| Default | Normal background |
| Hovered | Accent background + contrasting text |
| Disabled | Reduced opacity |
| Selected/Active | Persistent accent state |

---

### 2. Submenu Indicators

Menu items containing child actions should display a right-facing arrow indicator.

Example:
Export >
- PDF
- Excel >
  -   XLSX
  -   CSV
  -   ODS

title: Feature Request: Add Cascading Submenus and Visual Indicators for Nested Context Menu Actions
author: Lord-Taw
body:
## Summary

Improve submenu discoverability and navigation by visually distinguishing menu items that contain child actions and opening their submenus in a cascading layout.

Items with nested actions should display a right-facing arrow (`>`) and, when hovered, reveal their child menu to the side, following common desktop application conventions.

---

## Problem Statement

Currently, menu items that contain nested actions are not visually differentiated enough from regular actions, making submenu discovery less intuitive.

Additionally, nested options are not exposed in a way that clearly communicates hierarchy and navigation flow, forcing users to explore menu items through trial and error.

---

## Proposed Behavior

### Submenu Indicators

Menu items containing child actions should display a right-facing arrow indicator (`>`).

### Cascading Submenus

When a user hovers over an item containing child actions:

- Open the submenu automatically.
- Display the submenu to the right of the parent menu.
- Keep both parent and child menus visible simultaneously.
- Support multiple nesting levels.
- Close the submenu when the pointer leaves the menu hierarchy.

### Example

```text
Export >
 ├─ PDF
 └─ Excel >
     ├─ XLSX
     ├─ CSV
     └─ ODS

Settings >
 ├─ Appearance
 ├─ Shortcuts
 └─ Advanced >
     ├─ Logs
     └─ Diagnostics

title: Feature Request: Python macro projects with an editor and form controls (uv on desktop, Pyodide on the web)
author: faysou
body:
## Summary

Support Python macros in GridCraft, organized like a VBA project: a workbook holds several Python modules, an in-app
editor edits them, and form controls on the sheet (buttons, check boxes, combo boxes, ...) run them. The desktop app
runs macros with `uv run --script`, and `gridcraft-web` runs the same code with Pyodide in a Web Worker. The project
declares its dependencies (`numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, ...) in a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/) header,
so users never manage a virtualenv and GridCraft never embeds `libpython`.

This follows the suggestion in #1143 to open a separate issue for Python. Related: #356 (macros), #1123
(plugin host), and #1000 (script undo history).

## Why Python with uv and Pyodide

- Python with numpy, pandas, and scipy covers most analysis people move out of a spreadsheet today.
- uv resolves the interpreter and the dependencies, on Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD. It downloads a standalone
  Python when none is installed and caches environments, so later runs start fast.
- GridCraft's Rust binary stays as it is. It spawns a process and talks to it over the existing control protocol.
- Pyodide reads the same PEP 723 header on the web, so one project runs on both targets without changes.

## Example project

A workbook with two modules. `analysis` holds the macros, and `stats` holds shared code:

```python

def z_scores(data: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return (data - data.mean(axis=0)) / data.std(axis=0)

title: MEDIAN and AGGREGATE(12) return #NUM! when finite middle values overflow during addition
author: MMexicann
body:
On upstream main `79e85c1`, the even-length branch of `median` in `crates/functions/src/stat.rs` computes `(lo + hi) / 2`. Two finite middle values can overflow in the addition even when their midpoint is representable. The numeric result check then returns `#NUM!`.

Reproduction:
```sh
gridcraft-cli eval '=MEDIAN(1E308,1E308)'
gridcraft-cli eval '=MEDIAN(-1E308,-1E308)'
gridcraft-cli eval '=AGGREGATE(12,0,{1E308;1E308})'
```
Expected: `1E308`, `-1E308`, and `1E308`. These are mathematical expectations under [Microsoft's documented MEDIAN rule](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/functions/median-function), rather than observed desktop Excel results for these extreme inputs.

A new Rust regression through the registered MEDIAN function fails on unchanged production code: expected `1e308`, got `Value::Error(Num)`. A control test for ordinary, tiny and mixed-type inputs passes. AGGREGATE function number 12 uses the same helper.

An overflow-safe midpoint should preserve sorting, coercion, error propagation and empty-input behavior. Regression coverage should include both signs, opposite signs, finite extremes, tiny values and dependent recalculation.

Prepared on behalf of @MMexicann with AI assistance; a regression-tested fix is in progress.

author: davidum2
body:
### Summary
GridCraft’s pure-Rust architecture and agent-native foundation (via MCP and JSON-lines control channel) provide an excellent substrate for AI-driven spreadsheet manipulation.

However, having an external agent or script orchestrate multi-step procedural workflows (such as iterating over hundreds of rows, inserting rows, recalculating sequential control numbers, or aggregating cross-sheet tables) step-by-step over the socket has three major drawbacks:
1. **Excessive Token Consumption:** Micro-managing hundreds of row/cell edits through repeated JSON-RPC tool calls consumes tens of thousands of tokens per task.
2. **Network/Socket Latency:** Hundreds of sequential roundtrips over the control channel introduce significant execution delay compared to in-process execution.
3. **Fragility on Repetitive Logic:** Relying on LLM generation for deterministic, repetitive procedural steps introduces unnecessary failure points and costs.

### Proposed Solution
Integrate a lightweight, sandboxed embedded scripting engine into GridCraft—such as **[Rhai](https://rhai.rs/)** (pure Rust, zero external dependencies, sandboxed, fast, with Rust-like syntax) or a similar minimal scripting runtime:

1. **Compound Tools for AI Agents:**
   - Instead of an AI agent issuing 300 individual commands to process a dataset, the agent (or a human developer) authors a procedural script **once** and stores it in the workbook or user config.
   - The script registers as a first-class compound command (e.g. `s.execute("macro.run", {"name": "monthly_fleet_consolidation"})`).
   - The agent can then invoke the compound tool in a single turn, consuming **~20 tokens** instead of **20,000 tokens**.

2. **In-App Script/Macro Editor for Power Users:**
   - Provide an in-app editor dialog (similar to Excel’s macro window or OBS Studio’s script manager) accessible from the **Automate** ribbon tab.
   - Users can create, test, and bind custom scripts to keyboard shortcuts and ribbon buttons directly…

title: Column widths assume a 7 px digit regardless of the workbook's Normal font: with Malgun Gothic 12 (9 px) columns render 20 % narrower (######) and a save widens pictures by 27 % in Excel
author: kimjinha
body:
## What happens

GridCraft converts the stored column width (character units) to pixels with a constant 7 px digit, which is right for Calibri 11 but not for other Normal-style fonts. Excel's unit is the maximum digit width of the workbook's Normal font: Malgun Gothic 11 → 7 px, Malgun Gothic 12 → 9 px. Korean (and Japanese/Chinese) workbooks commonly use Malgun Gothic 12 as the Normal style, so every column is drawn about 20 % narrower than in Excel, and prices that fit in Excel show `######`.

The same constant is used when the writer turns a one-cell picture anchor into a two-cell anchor, so after a save Excel sizes the picture from a `to` marker that was computed with the wrong column width.

## Measurements

Workbook with Normal = Malgun Gothic 12 ([`repro_normalfont_excel.xlsx`](https://github.com/kimjinha/gridcraft-fidelity-repro/blob/main/repro/repro_normalfont_excel.xlsx), written by Excel):

| Column | Stored width | Excel | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|---|
| B, C | 15.31 | 104 pt = 139 px | 112 px (= 15.31 × 7 + 5) |
| D, E | 9.08 | 63.5 pt = 85 px | 69 px |

D2:E6 hold `2,870,000` / `5,166,000` (`#,##0`): Excel shows the numbers, GridCraft shows `######`.

![GridCraft shows ###### where Excel shows the prices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kimjinha/gridcraft-fidelity-repro/main/images/cmp_normalfont.png)

The GridCraft column width above is read from what GridCraft itself writes: after `gridcraft-cli run --in repro_normalfont_excel.xlsx --out repro_normalfont_gc.xlsx` ([`repro_normalfont_gc.xlsx`](https://github.com/kimjinha/gridcraft-fidelity-repro/blob/main/repro/repro_normalfont_gc.xlsx)) the drawing's first picture (100 × 100 px, `xdr:ext cx="1080000"`) has `from` col 1 off 184902 and `to` col 2 off 198102, i.e. the writer assumed column B is 1080000 − 198102 + 184902 = 1,066,800 EMU = 112 px. Excel then sizes that picture from the markers:

| | Excel-authored file | After GridCraft save |
|---|---|---|
| Picture 1 (B2, placement = move only) | 75 ×…

author: kimjinha
body:
## What happens

title: Windows: a cell's font family has no visible effect; every cell is drawn with the default face
author: kimjinha
body:
## What happens

[`repro_fonts_excel.xlsx`](https://github.com/kimjinha/gridcraft-fidelity-repro/blob/main/repro/repro_fonts_excel.xlsx) has one cell per family: Noto Sans KR Medium, Noto Sans KR, 맑은 고딕, Malgun Gothic, Arial, Arial Black (all installed; Noto Sans CJK KR Medium/Regular .otf and NotoSansKR-VF.ttf are in C:\Windows\Fonts). Excel draws each in its own face; GridCraft draws all six identically (Arial Black isn't even bold), still 25 s after opening. author: kimjinha
body:
Found by diffing Excel-written files against `gridcraft-cli run` output (scripts in https://github.com/kimjinha/gridcraft-fidelity-repro). None is visibly harmful on its own, listed so they can be picked off together:

1. Fonts lose `<family val="3"/>` (written as 2) and `<charset val="129"/>` (Hangul); Excel stores Korean fonts with charset 129.
2. Automatic font color (no `<color>`) is written as `<color theme="1"/>` (53 of 115 styled cells on one sheet changed).
3. `<sheetFormatPr customHeight="1">` is always written, even when the source had no custom default height.
4. Rows without a stored height get an `ht` (18.55 for Malgun Gothic 12 where Excel fits 17.5; 165 for a merged wrapped cell, see the merged-cell issue).
5. `<col style="…">` (the column's default style) is dropped; a price list lost `style="5"` on every column of four sheets.
6. Pictures sharing one media part are written once per picture: 79 pictures over 70 media parts became 79 parts, +12 % file size (#985 is the cross-sheet case).
7. Page margins are written from f32: `0.3` becomes `0.30000001192092896`.
8. `xl/calcChain.xml` is dropped (harmless, Excel rebuilds it) and a single-cell merge (`E1`) is dropped.

title: Enable Korean IME composition when typing into an idle selected cell
author: euisuh
body:
Korean can be pasted as text, but starting Korean composition from an idle selected cell is a different input path. The grid must enable the native IME before a cell editor exists.

At current main `f1894c6`, the idle grid starts editing from `egui::Event::Text`, but has no corresponding initial `ImeEvent::Preedit`/`Commit` activation path or idle-cell `IMEOutput`. In egui-winit 0.36, native IME activation follows whether `PlatformOutput.ime` is present. This can prevent a Korean IME from delivering the composition events needed to start editing in the first place.

Expected:

1. Select an ordinary cell while no text editor/dialog owns focus.
2. Use a Korean IME to compose `한글` from successive preedits such as `ㅎ`, `하`, `한`.
3. The composing text is shown once; the final syllables replace preedit text rather than append to it.
4. Commit or cancel behaves correctly, without changing other cells or interrupting the OS composition on a widget-focus handoff.
5. Paste, direct committed text, navigation and existing formula-bar input continue to work.

Implementation/testing is in progress with synthetic egui composition sequences and caret-output checks. These establish the application event-path regression, not a completed Windows/macOS hardware-IME verification.

Related, distinct report: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/142 concerns imported/rendered Chinese text. Existing suite-level Korean report https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/issues/2093 is closed; this issue isolates the idle grid activation path.

Prepared with Codex.

title: About: the contributor list hasn't been refreshed since 2026-10-10, so it shows 16 of at least 57 contributors
author: arcanii
body:
## What happens

Help ▸ About ▸ Contributors lists 16 people. `crates/ui-egui/build.rs` compiles the list from `contributors/contributors.json`, and that file was last generated at `90b3c41` (2026-10-10), when `main` had 148 commits. It hasn't been refreshed since:

- **281 pull requests have been merged since then**, by 50 people. 41 of them aren't in the file at all, so About shows 16 of at least 57 contributors.
- **10 of the 13 entries in `contributors/people.toml`** have no row in the JSON. The names those people chose for themselves aren't shown, since a name is used only when the JSON marks the entry as verified (`people_entry`).
- **0.6.0, 0.6.1 and 0.7.0 shipped with the 10 October list.** The last refreshes were in the 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 version bumps (`13664fe`, `9f896c1`).

## Cause

The file is a snapshot by design: `AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributors.md` say maintainers regenerate it with `python3 ../../craftrules/scripts/contributors.py .`, and it must never be hand-edited. Nothing runs that step regularly; it isn't part of the release steps in `docs/releasing.md` or `docs/release-playbook.md`.

## Suggestion

- Refresh it now.
- Add the refresh to the release steps, so every release credits everyone who worked on it.
- Optionally, a check in CI or in the release workflow that warns when the snapshot's `head` is far behind `main`.

Counts are from `upstream/main` at `f1894c6` (2026-10-15) and from `gh pr list --state merged --search "merged:>2026-10-10T19:59:42Z"`.
