title: Legacy implicit intersection produces #SPILL! errors and propagates through dependent formulas
author: NaviStorm
body:
GridCraft appears to evaluate some legacy Excel formulas as dynamic arrays instead of preserving their implicit intersection behavior.

For example, a regular formula in cell G4 contains:

=IF(ISBLANK(B:B),0,IF(B4="Thierry",C4,0))

Under legacy Excel implicit intersection rules, the whole-column reference B:B is evaluated at the formula’s row, effectively testing B4. GridCraft instead evaluates the entire column, producing an array that cannot spill and returns #SPILL!.

Replacing ISBLANK(B:B) with ISBLANK(B4) returns the expected result.

The error then propagates through dependent cells. In the affected workbook, this reaches summary formulas such as:

=SUM(D5:D1000)

The SUM formula is not the source of the error; it propagates an error from its input range. Multiple worksheets are affected.

Expected behavior:
Preserve legacy implicit intersection when importing older Excel formulas, while retaining dynamic-array behavior for formulas that intentionally return arrays.

Suggested investigation:
Check how the importer distinguishes legacy formulas from modern dynamic-array formulas and whether implicit intersection needs to be represented explicitly in the imported expressions.

title: Python cell formulas (PY) with a local worker
author: derechopiano
body:
# Python cell formulas (PY) with a local worker

## Feature

Support Python cell formulas: read workbook data through `xl()` and return results to cells and
spilled arrays, with a Python editing interface, diagnostics and cancellation.

This complements #1566's Python macros. Formulas return calculation results; macros perform
workbook actions. PR #1123 already proposes external functions and persistent process handling,
so the runtime/process interface should be shared where appropriate.

## Proposed behavior and architecture

- Follow Excel's sheet/row-major Python calculation order and shared-variable semantics. When
  a Python input changes, recalculate the ordered Python group; avoid unsafe per-cell caching.
- Use an optional, persistent background worker per enabled workbook. Keep packages and
  compiled code warm, batch requests and deduplicate input ranges. Normal UI editing must not
  wait for Python. Coalesce edits and discard replies from superseded calculation generations.
- Support manual calculation, cancellation, bounded input/output/log buffers, and worker crash
  recovery. Opening a workbook must never install packages or silently execute its Python.
- Native execution would initially require explicit trust. A process/venv is not a security
  sandbox and cannot be described as matching Excel's cloud isolation.
- Preserve code and cached results when execution is disabled/unavailable. Define Python-object
  outputs and XLSX Python script encoding explicitly before claiming Excel interoperability.
- Keep the WASM build valid and coordinate the web backend with the Pyodide proposal in #1566.

## Initial performance evidence

A trusted synthetic prototype on one Windows laptop, using CPython 3.11.3, NumPy 2.4.6 and
pandas 3.0.6 in an isolated environment, measured these medians:

- Fresh worker plus pandas import and small calculation: 1.32 s (3 samples).
- Warm tiny IPC calculation: 0.112 ms (100 samples).
- 100,000 numeric values transferred and summe…

title: Charts: insert.chart with a multi-area range ("A1:A5,E1:E5") silently uses only the first area, so a pie comes out empty
author: javierjrueda
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.7.0, macOS universal build (also checked against `main` at f1894c6)

### What happens
`insert.chart` with a multi-area range only uses the first area and drops the rest without saying so. A pie chart over a label column plus a value column comes out empty.

### Steps
Through the control port (or the MCP `insert_chart` tool):

```json
{"command": "range.setValues", "params": {"range": "A1", "values": [["Mes","x","y","z","Ventas"],["Ene",1,1,1,10],["Feb",1,1,1,20],["Mar",1,1,1,30],["Abr",1,1,1,40]]}}
{"command": "insert.chart", "params": {"range": "A1:A5,E1:E5", "type": "pie", "at": "G2"}}
```

### Expected
As in Excel: one series with values from `E2:E5`, categories from `A2:A5` and the name from `E1`.

### Actual
The command returns `{"chart": 1}`, so it looks like it worked, but the chart is empty. The title is "Mes" (the header of the first area), there is 1 series with no numbers, and the legend shows 1, 2, 3, 4 instead of the month names. `E1:E5` never gets used. A contiguous range such as `D1:E5` plots as expected.

### Where
`build_chart` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`) calls `block()`, which calls `target_range()` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub(crate) fn target_range(s: &Session, p: &Json) -> Result<RangeRef> {
    Ok(target_ranges(s, p)?.first().copied().unwrap_or_default())
}
```

`target_ranges` parses every comma-separated area, but `target_range` keeps only the first one. A Ctrl-selected multi-area selection with no `range` param may have the same problem (`block()` uses `selection.current()`).

### Suggestion
Build the series from every area in `insert.chart` / `insert.recommendedCharts`. Excel's rule: when the first area is text with the same height as the others, it holds the categories and each later area is a series. Until that works, return an error when there is more than one area instead of plotting the first one quietly. Other commands that go through `target_range` may also drop areas without warning…

title: Crash: a LAMBDA that calls itself without end overflows the stack and closes GridCraft, also on open
author: iluebbe
body:
When a recursive LAMBDA goes too deep, Excel shows `#NUM!` in the cell. GridCraft 0.7.0 on Windows runs out of stack on the main thread instead, and the process ends: unsaved work is lost. A workbook that contains such a formula can't be opened at all, though Excel opens it and shows `#NUM!`. Forgetting the base case is an easy mistake while writing a recursive LAMBDA.

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0, build 20430, through COM) against GridCraft 0.7.0 on Windows 11 (`gridcraft-cli.exe` and `gridcraft.exe` from the MSI).

| Formula | Excel | GridCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `=LET(f,LAMBDA(g,x,g(g,x)),f(f,1))` | `#NUM!` | stack overflow, the process ends |
| defined name `LOOP` = `=LAMBDA(n,LOOP(n))`, cell `=LOOP(1)` | `#NUM!` | stack overflow, the process ends |
| `=LET(F,LAMBDA(me,n,IF(n<=0,0,1+me(me,n-1))),F(F,1000))` | 1000 | `#CALC!` (#917) |
| the same with `F(F,5000)` | `#NUM!` | `#CALC!` |
| `=LET(F,LAMBDA(me,n,IF(n=0,0,me(me,n-1))),F(F,1000))` | 0 | `#CALC!` |
| the same with `F(F,10000)` | `#NUM!` | `#CALC!` |
| defined name `CNT` = `=LAMBDA(n,IF(n=0,0,1+CNT(n-1)))`, cell `=CNT(1000)` | 1000 | `#NAME?` |

How GridCraft ends:

| What | Result |
|---|---|
| `gridcraft-cli eval "=LET(f,LAMBDA(g,x,g(g,x)),f(f,1))"` | `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack`, exit code `0xC00000FD` |
| `gridcraft.exe --control`: `cell.set` A1 = `unsaved work`, then `cell.set` B1 = the formula | no reply; the app exits with `0xC000041D`; A1 is lost |
| An Excel-saved workbook with the formula in B1 (Excel shows `#NUM!`): `gridcraft-cli run --in loop.xlsx --print A1:B1` | stack overflow, exit code `0xC00000FD` |
| The same workbook through `file.open` in `gridcraft.exe` | the app exits with `0xC00000FD` |

```
> gridcraft-cli eval "=LET(f,LAMBDA(g,x,g(g,x)),f(f,1))"

thread 'main' (16472) has overflowed its stack
```

title: Charts: keep an unedited chart's XML from the file on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Charts opened from an `.xlsx` are rebuilt from the model on save, so anything the model doesn't hold is dropped. `docs/chart-parity.md` lists this as Work item 2 and the main reason charts are about 30% ready.

**How often it matters:** in a census of 243 real-world workbooks (counts only), 97 have charts (718 in total). Many carry settings GridCraft drops today: bar overlap in 328 charts, gap width in 268, date axes in 232, deleted axes in 134, waterfall charts in 29, text boxes inside charts in 25.

**What goes wrong:** I built six small charts in Excel and saved them with `gridcraft-cli run` on main. Excel opens all six without repair, but:
- data labels on one series turn on for every series;
- a date axis becomes a text axis (the time-scale settings are gone);
- a waterfall's "set as total" bar floats;
- a text box inside a chart, and labels taken from cells, disappear;
- gap width, overlap, axis bounds and formats, and a deleted axis are reset.

**Proposal:** on read, keep the chart part and its style, colour and shape parts. On save, if the chart still equals what was read and its sheets still exist, write the kept parts back. Otherwise use today's writer. This is what #727 does for chart sheets, applied to embedded charts. Any failure (size limit, XML that doesn't parse, a missing element) falls back to today's writer.

The other option I considered is modelling everything: a typed chart tree with a bag of unknown XML per node. It is cleaner in the end but a much bigger change, and it touches every open chart PR. Happy to go that way if you prefer.

Two follow-up tickets cover editing a kept chart (#1675) and references the model doesn't hold (#1676).

**Questions:**
1. Is extending #727's approach to embedded charts the direction you want?
2. Should the kept bytes live on `Chart`, or in `Sheet.preserved`?

I'm happy to implement this as a PR if the shape works for you.

title: [Feature Request] Select and copy filtered data
author: rogeriothe
body:
### Summary
Allow users to select and copy only the visible rows of a spreadsheet after a filter has been applied.

### Problem
When a filter is applied to a sheet, there is currently no reliable way to select the filtered results and copy them. Users who need to reuse a subset of data (e.g., paste it into another sheet, a document, or an email) have to copy rows manually or export the whole dataset and clean it up elsewhere.

### Proposed solution
- When a filter is active, selecting a range (or using Select All / Ctrl+A) should include **only the visible (filtered) rows**.
- Copying (Ctrl+C / Cmd+C or context menu → Copy) should place **only the visible rows** on the clipboard, preserving column order.
- Pasting into GridCraft or external apps (Excel, Google Sheets, text editors) should keep the tabular structure (tab-separated values / HTML table).
- Optionally, include the column headers in the copy (e.g., via a "Copy with headers" option in the context menu).

### Expected behavior
1. User applies a filter to one or more columns.
2. User selects the filtered range (or the whole visible table).
3. User copies the selection.
4. The clipboard contains only the rows that match the filter — hidden rows are excluded.

### Alternatives considered
- Exporting filtered data to CSV/XLSX: works, but adds extra steps for a quick copy-paste task.
- Copying row by row: impractical for large datasets.

### Additional context
This is standard behavior in most spreadsheet tools (e.g., Excel's "Visible cells only"), so users naturally expect it when working with filtered data.

title: Charts: patch only the edited fields when a chart with kept XML is edited
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Follows #1668, which keeps a chart's original XML when it is unedited. When a chart is edited, the kept part should be patched, not discarded.

**Proposal:** parse the kept part and change only the fields that were edited: titles, legend, data-label and gridline flags, style, series references, colour, smoothing and trendlines. For a chart type change, or added or removed series, fall back to today's writer with a warning. #1290, #1219 and #1088 would each add one patch rule.

**Risk:** elements must be inserted in schema order or Excel offers to repair the file. Each patch rule needs a unit test against Excel XML, and each saved fixture should be opened in Excel before merging.

Refreshing the kept series caches when cell values change is a separate question, tracked in #1677.

title: Charts: move cell references inside kept chart XML on row inserts, renames and deleted sheets
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Follows #1668. A kept chart part holds references the model doesn't: a title taken from a cell, data labels from a cell range, legend-entry and trendline-label references, and waterfall references. Row inserts, sheet renames and deleting a sheet today only adjust the series references the model holds. Without more work, a kept title or label would point at the wrong cell after a row insert, with no warning.

In a census of 243 real-world workbooks, titles from cells appear in 10 charts and data labels from cells in 113.

**Proposal:** collect those references on the chart behind one `Chart::refs_mut()` helper, and use it in the three loops that fix references (structural edits, rename, delete sheet).

**The alternative:** accept stale references at first, as chart sheets do today in #727, and say so in `docs/chart-parity.md`.

**Question:** which do you prefer?

title: Charts: refresh kept series caches when cell values change
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Follows #1668. A kept chart part holds a cache of values for each series (`numCache` and `strCache`). It goes stale when the cells change.

Excel usually redraws same-workbook series from the cells, but I haven't verified that for every case. Previews and simpler readers use the cache.

**Proposal:** refresh a series' cache only when its values differ from the cells, and leave it byte-identical when they don't. Unedited round trips then stay byte-equal whenever the cell values are unchanged.

**Caveat:** for a PivotChart the cache sometimes should win. #684 has a rule for that, and a refresh must not overwrite it.

**Question:** should kept series caches be refreshed when cell values change?

title: XLSX: chart series that refer to defined names as `[0]!Name` show `#NAME?` and no data (0.7.0)
author: bldred
body:
A chart whose series point at workbook-scoped defined names opens blank in GridCraft 0.7.0: the category axis shows a single `#NAME?` label and every series has one empty point. This is the usual way to build a chart over a dynamic range (an OFFSET name that grows with a table). Excel and ONLYOFFICE plot such charts.

**Why:** in `<c:f>`, Excel writes a workbook-scoped name with its "this workbook" prefix:

```xml
<c:cat><c:strRef><c:f>[0]!TaskNames</c:f></c:strRef></c:cat>
<c:val><c:numRef><c:f>[0]!TaskStart</c:f></c:numRef></c:val>
```

`crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs` (`data_ref`, `read_series`) keeps that text as is, and `gridcraft_chart::resolve` evaluates it. The lexer reads `[0]` as a structured reference, so `[0]!TaskNames` doesn't parse and evaluates to `#NAME?`. The names themselves are fine: with the repro below, `gridcraft-cli eval` gives the right values for `TaskNames` and `#NAME?` for `[0]!TaskNames`, and with `[0]!` removed from the chart part the chart plots every point.

**Repro (synthetic):**
1. A sheet with a table `Plan` (columns Task, Start, Done, Left) and a few rows.
2. Workbook-scoped names: `TaskNames = OFFSET(Plan[[#Headers],[Task]],1,0,COUNTA(Plan[Task]),1)`, `TaskStart = OFFSET(TaskNames,0,1)`, and so on.
3. A stacked bar chart whose series use `[0]!TaskNames` for categories and `[0]!TaskStart` / `[0]!TaskDone` / `[0]!TaskLeft` for values (the form Excel saves).
4. Open in GridCraft: one `#NAME?` category, no bars.

Saving has the matching gap: GridCraft writes a name in a chart reference without the prefix, and a series *name* that is a defined name is written as literal text.

**Proposed fix (PR to follow):** handle it at the XLSX boundary, as `fmla.rs` already does for other file-only syntax. On read, `[0]!Name` becomes `Name` in chart references (`cat`, `val`, `xVal`, `yVal`, `bubbleSize`, `tx`, and chartex `<cx:f>`). On write, a bare workbook-scoped name is written as `[0]!Name`. Only `[0]` is touched: external books (`[1]Sheet1!…`) keep …

title: Charts: category axis "Categories in reverse order" (`orientation="maxMin"`) is ignored
author: bldred
body:
A bar chart whose category axis has `<c:scaling><c:orientation val="maxMin"/>` (Excel's Format Axis ▸ Categories in reverse order) draws its categories bottom to top in GridCraft, so the first row of data ends up at the bottom. Excel draws the first category at the top. Horizontal bar charts over a list (task lists, rankings) usually turn this on.

- Read: `crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs` doesn't read `c:scaling/c:orientation` for either axis.
- Write: the axis writer always emits `<c:orientation val="minMax"/>`, so a save also drops the setting.
- Repro: a bar chart over `A1:B4` with the category axis's orientation set to `maxMin` in the chart part. GridCraft draws the A2 category at the bottom.

Likely shape: a `reverse` flag on the category axis (and value axis) in the model, read and written in `<c:scaling>`, honoured by the renderer, and exposed in the Format pane and `chart.set`. Related: #1290 (fixed bounds) touches the same `<c:scaling>` element.

Found while testing #1686.

title: Charts: bar/column value axis always starts at 0, even when the data sits far from 0
author: bldred
body:
`chart/src/axis.rs::nice_scale` is called with `force_zero` for column, bar and area charts, so the automatic value axis always includes 0 (lines and scatter already skip 0 when the minimum is at least ⅚ of the maximum). Excel's automatic axis for bars doesn't always start at 0: a stacked bar chart that plots dates (about 45,000 as serial numbers) plus durations of a few days therefore draws the bars as slivers at the far end of a 0–50,000 axis in GridCraft. In Excel, with no fixed bounds, the axis covers just the date range.

- Repro: a stacked bar chart, series 1 = `{45200,45207,45214}`, series 2 = `{5,10,3}`, no `<c:min>`/`<c:max>`. Excel's axis starts near 45,200; GridCraft's starts at 0.
- Not covered by #1290, which adds *fixed* bounds; this is about the automatic ones.

Needs a black-box check of Excel's automatic bar-axis rule (stacked and clustered, with and without negatives) before changing `force_zero`.

Found while testing #1686.

title: Charts: series that go through a defined name don't pick up their source number format
author: bldred
body:
`resolve.rs::ref_format` (and `category_texts`) read the number format from the first cell of a direct reference only (`parse_ref`). A series whose values are a defined name (`Dates` = `Sheet1!$B$2:$B$9`, or an OFFSET name) falls back to `General`. So a value axis with `<c:numFmt formatCode="m/d/yyyy" sourceLinked="1"/>` over date cells shows serial numbers (`45200`) instead of dates. The same series with `Sheet1!$B$2:$B$9` typed directly shows dates.

- Repro: dates in B2:B4 formatted `m/d/yyyy`, a name `Dates` = `Sheet1!$B$2:$B$4`, a bar chart with values `Dates`. The axis labels are numbers.
- Fix idea: when a series formula is a name (or evaluates to a reference), take the format from the cells the reference resolves to. Related: #1219 (typed axis formats; this is the linked-to-source path).

Found while testing #1686.

title: XLSX: chart series that refer to defined names are saved without `numCache`/`strCache`
author: bldred
body:
`xlsx/src/chart.rs::ref_values` writes cached points only for a plain reference (`Expr::Ref`). A series whose `<c:f>` is a defined name (`[0]!Dates`) is saved with no cache. Excel recalculates on open, but readers that only use the cache (viewers, previewers, some converters) show an empty series.

- Repro: a bar chart with values `Dates` (a workbook name); save; the `<c:numRef>` has a `<c:f>` but no `<c:numCache>`.
- Fix idea: evaluate the name to its reference (or values) when writing the cache. `xlsx` is L2 alongside `calc`, so check the layering rules before pulling in evaluation.

Found while testing #1686.

title: Linux (Fedora): cell fonts not found, so bold/italic are never shown; serif, mono, Thai and CJK fall back
author: ibakard
body:
**GridCraft:** 0.7.0 AppImage (`gridcraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`)
**OS:** Fedora 44, x86_64, Wayland

## Summary

On Fedora, cells formatted **bold** or *italic* are drawn as regular text. The Bold button shows as pressed and the style is saved to the .xlsx correctly, but nothing changes on screen and nothing is logged. A workbook made in Excel with bold headers and totals opens with no bold at all.

The cause is that the cell font roles look for font files at fixed Debian/Ubuntu/Arch paths (`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`, the `"cell" | "cell-bold" | …`, `"serif"` and `"mono"` arms, still the same on `main`). Fedora installs the same fonts in different folders and sometimes under different file names. No cell font is found, so every cell falls back to egui's built-in proportional font, which has a single weight and no italic.

This is not covered by #974, which starts the installed-font scan. Calibri cells only use a scanned font when a font named "Calibri" is installed. Carlito, the Calibri substitute on Linux, is named "Carlito", so those cells still go through the fixed-path `cell-*` roles.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fedora 44 with its default fonts (`google-carlito-fonts`, `liberation-*-fonts`, `google-noto-*-vf-fonts`, `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts`).
2. Start the GridCraft 0.7.0 AppImage and type text in A1.
3. Press Bold (or Italic).

**Expected:** bold (italic) text.
**Actual:** regular text in the fallback font. The Bold button shows as pressed.

Also: Cambria, Georgia, Times New Roman and Courier New cells render in the built-in fallback fonts, and Thai, Chinese, Japanese and Korean text displays as empty boxes.

## What GridCraft looks for vs. where Fedora has it

I traced the font files GridCraft 0.7.0 opens at startup with an `LD_PRELOAD` shim on `open64`.

| Role | File GridCraft looks for | Where Fedora has it |
|---|---|---|
| `cell`, `cell-bold`, `cell-italic`, `cell-bold-italic` | `Carlito-{Regular,Bold,Italic,BoldItalic}.ttf` in `<dir>/carli…

title: [Feature Request] [GridCraft] Spanish formulas with decimal point for es-HN, es-MX and other regions
author: fjruizhn
body:
### Description

In GridCraft, choosing **Español** under View → Interface language switches the formula language to Spanish with **decimal commas** and **semicolon arguments**, as described in `docs/formula-input.md`. That is the convention in Spain and much of South America, but **several Spanish-speaking countries use a decimal point and comma thousands separators**: Honduras (es-HN), Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and others. The system locale shows this too: `es_HN.UTF-8` has `decimal_point "."` and `thousands_sep ","`.

So today a user in Honduras has to choose between a Spanish interface with the wrong number format, or the right number format in English. We kept GridCraft in English for that reason.

**Request:** separate the number and argument separators from the formula and interface language, or offer regional variants (for example *Español (Honduras / México)*) that keep Spanish function names (`SUMA`, `SI`, `BUSCARV`) with a decimal point and comma arguments, ideally following the system locale.

Possibly related: #1702 (dot not accepted as the decimal separator).

**If you don't have time for it:** we'd be happy to implement it ourselves and send a PR. Could you tell us:
- where the formula-language table and the separator choice live (the editor boundary described in `docs/formula-input.md`);
- whether you'd prefer a regional variant per language or a separate "number format follows system locale" setting;
- what tests you'd expect?

### Operating system and version

Ubuntu (Linux x86_64), GridCraft 0.7.0 AppImage.

title: Bug: Clearing contents of PivotTable range does not delete the PivotTable or prevent partial deletions
author: sam-f-gh
body:
### Description
In Microsoft Excel, PivotTables have protected boundaries with well-defined deletion semantics:
1. Selecting the **entire PivotTable range** and pressing `Delete` completely deletes the PivotTable object from the sheet (clearing its layout, formatting, caches, and unregistering the PivotTable so the Fields side pane no longer opens).
2. Selecting a **partial range** (e.g., individual cells, row/column labels, or intersecting rows/columns) and pressing `Delete` is blocked with:
   > *"Cannot change part of a PivotTable report."*

In GridCraft, pressing `Delete` triggers `edit.clearContents`, which clears cell values directly without verifying PivotTable boundaries. This causes two issues:
* Clearing the entire PivotTable range leaves behind an orphaned PivotTable: the cell text is wiped, but the formatting remains, the PivotTable stays in `sheet.pivots`, and clicking any of those cells still opens the PivotTable Fields pane.
* Clearing a partial range or individual label cells wipes out the cell text, breaking the PivotTable's visual state while leaving the underlying report structure active.

---

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a PivotTable on a worksheet.
2. Select the entire cell range covering the PivotTable.
3. Press the `Delete` key.
4. Observe that while text is cleared, the table styling persists.
5. Click any cell within the cleared area and observe that the PivotTable Fields pane still opens.
6. (Alternatively) Select only a row label or a subset of cells in the PivotTable and press `Delete`. Observe that the cell text is wiped out instead of being blocked.

---

### Actual Behavior
* Deleting across the PivotTable range only clears cell values; the PivotTable object and cell styles remain.
* Deleting a subset of cells inside a PivotTable clears text instead of rejecting the change.

---

### Expected Behavior (Excel Parity)
* If the selection completely encloses a PivotTable, pressing `Delete` (`edit.clearContents` / `edit.clearAll`) shou…

title: PivotTable: support in-cell header renaming and protect report cells from direct editing
author: sam-f-gh
body:
### Description

In Microsoft Excel, PivotTable reports support in-cell editing for headers while protecting calculated data cells:

1. **Value Field Headers** (e.g. `"Sum of Sales"`):
   - Typing directly into a value header cell updates the custom name of that value field (`pt.values[i].name`), re-renders the report, and syncs the new name to the PivotTable Fields task pane.
   - Validations:
     - Cannot be blank (`"The name isn't valid."`).
     - Cannot match an underlying source data column name (`"PivotTable field name already exists."`).
     - Cannot duplicate another value field's custom name in the PivotTable (`"PivotTable field name already exists."`).

2. **Axis Header Captions** (`"Row Labels"` / `"Column Labels"`):
   - In compact layout, typing directly into `"Row Labels"` or `"Column Labels"` updates the axis header caption (`rowHeaderCaption` and `colHeaderCaption` in OpenXML).
   - Validations:
     - Cannot be blank (`"A PivotTable report field name cannot be blank."`).

3. **Data Cell Protection**:
   - Directly typing into calculated body data cells (or subtotal/grand total cells) is refused with:
     > `"Cannot change part of a PivotTable report."`

---

### Current Behavior in GridCraft

- Typing into any PivotTable cell triggers `cell.set`, which unconditionally overwrites the cell value in `sh.cells`.
- For value headers, the underlying `PivotTable` value field is unchanged, the PivotTable Fields task pane does not reflect the rename, and subsequent refreshes overwrite the cell.
- Axis header captions (`"Row Labels"`, `"Column Labels"`) cannot be customized or persisted in XLSX.
- Body/data cells are overwritten with static values without protection.

---

### Expected Behavior

- In-cell edits to value headers rename the value field, re-render the PivotTable, and update the task pane.
- In-cell edits to `"Row Labels"` / `"Column Labels"` update `row_header_caption` / `col_header_caption` and round-trip through `.xlsx`.
- Edits to calcula…

title: Dark mode keeps the cell canvas white — please add a "Dark Cells" view option (or Page Color)
author: Teejer
body:
Dark mode (`view.darkMode`) repaints the chrome beautifully — ribbon, headers, formula bar, menus, desk area — but the cell canvas itself stays white. The white grid is the majority of the screen, so it's the single biggest reason I can't use dark mode for long spreadsheet sessions.

**Where it lives in v0.7.0** (I read the source before writing this):

- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`: `Tokens::dark()` hardcodes `grid_bg: Color32::WHITE`, identical to `light()`; `gridline` is `#E1E1E1` in both palettes.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: `look()` resolves *automatic* font color to a hardcoded `Color32::BLACK`; un-filled merged cells paint `Color32::WHITE`; automatic border ink is hardcoded `Color32::BLACK`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/formula_bar.rs`: the in-cell editor paints `Color32::BLACK` when it targets the grid.

So "automatic vs explicit" ink currently collapses to one constant in three places — presumably why the canvas was left white.

**What I built locally to check it's tractable** (~60 implementation lines over 6 files): a view option, not a workbook property — `UiState.dark_cells` (persisted in `ui.json`), a `view.darkCells {on?: bool}` command, and a "Dark Cells" checkbox under the existing Display-theme menu. Since all canvas painting already reads through `Tokens::get(ctx)`, the flag is mirrored into `ctx.data()` from the update loop and applied there: `grid_bg` → black, `gridline` → `#3F3F3F`, plus a new `auto_text` token (`#E6E6E6`) replacing the three hardcoded automatic-ink constants.

Rules it follows:

- Only **automatic** ink flips; an explicit black font stays black (then invisibility is the user's stated choice, and the file round-trips unchanged for other Excel users).
- Automatic ink over an **explicit fill** picks black or near-white by the fill's luminance — I first shipped it without this and a white info block in the sales sample turned invisible-on-white. With the rule it matches Excel's dark canvas.
- Explicit fills and conditional-format sc…

title: PDF export replaces Serbian Latin characters (č, ć, đ) with question marks
author: slobeksila
body:
Description

When exporting an XLSX workbook to PDF, Serbian Latin characters such as č, ć, and đ are replaced with question marks. Their uppercase equivalents (Č, Ć, Đ) are affected as well.
The text is stored correctly in the XLSX file. The characters š, ž, Š, and Ž are exported correctly.

Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new workbook.
2. Enter the following text in a cell:
   č ć đ š ž Č Ć Đ Š Ž
3. Export the workbook to PDF.
4. Open the exported PDF.

Expected result

č ć đ š ž Č Ć Đ Š Ž
ctual result
? ? ? š ž ? ? ? Š Ž

Environment

- GridCraft version: 0.7.0
- Operating system: Linux (Bazzite)
- Package: gridcraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage

Additional information

The issue was reproduced using the gridcraft-cli binary included in the AppImage, with Calibri, DejaVu Sans, and Liberation Sans. Changing the font does not resolve it.

The generated PDF uses Helvetica / Helvetica-Bold with WinAnsiEncoding.

The likely cause is the Unicode-to-WinAnsi conversion in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`: the `win_ansi()` function replaces characters that cannot be represented in CP1252 with `?`.

This makes PDF export unsuitable for documents containing these Serbian Latin characters. Could the PDF exporter support them, ideally through Unicode text and embedded fonts?

- **Gridcraft Version:** 0.7.0

title: Thai text renders as tofu on ChromeOS/Crostini: script-fallback font paths omit `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos`
author: narithtyty
body:
**GridCraft:** 0.5.0 (`.deb`, `gridcraft-0.5.0-linux-x86_64.deb`, package `0.5.0-1`)
**OS:** ChromeOS Linux container (Crostini) — Debian 13 "trixie", x86_64, Wayland
**Still present on `main`:** yes (see line numbers below)

## Summary

Thai text in cells renders as tofu boxes (□□□) even though a Thai font is installed and the text is read correctly. The same workbook's Thai content is parsed and printed correctly by `gridcraft-cli`, and Thai sheet names appear correctly in the app's own UI — so the data is fine and only **glyph lookup** fails.

The cause is that the script-fallback lists in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` probe a **fixed set of Debian/Ubuntu/Arch directories** that does not include ChromeOS/Crostini's font location. Crostini's `cros-host-fonts` package installs every system font under `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos/`, so no Thai face is ever found and the whole Thai fallback chain is empty.

## Root cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`, `fn thai()`:

```rust
// v0.5.0, theme.rs:474-491  (same on main: theme.rs:580-597)
fn thai() -> Vec<(String, u32)> {
    ...
    let lin = ["/usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto",
               "/usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto",
               "/usr/share/fonts/truetype",
               "/usr/share/fonts"];           // <-- main theme.rs:584
    ...
    for d in lin {
        v.push((format!("{d}/NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf"), 0));
        v.push((format!("{d}/tlwg/Garuda.ttf"), 0));
        v.push((format!("{d}/garuda/Garuda.ttf"), 0));
    }
    v
}
```

On this machine the font is present, but at a path none of those `{d}` values produce:

```
$ ls /usr/share/fonts/*/noto/NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf
/usr/share/fonts/chromeos/noto/NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf
```

`load_fallback()` walks the candidate list and keeps the first entry that loads. With every candidate missing, `sys-thai` contributes nothing, so Thai falls through to egui's built-in fonts, which have **no coverage beyond Latin** — exactly the case the function's own doc c…

title: Ribbon layout: group captions, ordering and missing groups vs Excel on every tab
author: alosslessdev
body:
GridCraft's ribbon puts the right commands on the tabs, but the tabs don't *read* like Excel's. Comparing every tab side by side with Excel (Microsoft 365):

**Missing on every tab**

- No group captions under the clusters (the "Clipboard", "Font", "Alignment"… labels Excel draws along the bottom of each group). The groups exist in `catalog.rs` and in the code, but the ribbon shows only bare clusters — this is the same root cause as the group-titles half of #1655.
- No dialog launchers (the little box with the arrow in a group's bottom-right corner) where Excel has one and GridCraft has the dialog.
- Blank space inside the tab where a feature Excel has is missing. Excel packs groups left and keeps all the blank space at the right edge; when a function is missing its whole slot should collapse and everything after it should move left.

**Missing or misplaced groups and controls (all commands below already exist in `main`)**

| Tab | Gap |
|---|---|
| Home | no Add-ins group (`home.addIns`) |
| Insert | `Controls` sits after Sparklines instead of after Illustrations; no separate Recommended PivotTables or PivotChart buttons; Text Box and Header & Footer are two buttons where Excel folds them into one "Text" drop-down |
| Draw | no group captions (Drawing Tools, Convert) |

title: Sheet protection: Delete Rows and Delete Columns are refused even when the permission is granted
author: Hamza0101
body:
**Summary.** On a protected sheet, ticking **Delete rows** or **Delete columns** in Review ▸ Protect Sheet has no effect: the deletion is still refused. Insert rows and Insert columns do work when ticked, so the two halves of the dialog disagree.

**Steps to reproduce.** A sheet with values in A1:A3, protected with Delete rows and Insert rows both allowed:

```
review.protectSheet {}                      # then set delete_rows = insert_rows = true
home.insertRows {}   -> works
home.deleteRows {}   -> "The cell or chart you're trying to change is on a protected sheet."
home.deleteColumns {} -> the same
```

**Measured** on `main` @ f1894c6, with every permission ticked:

| action | result |
|---|---|
| `home.insertRows` | works |
| `home.insertColumns` | works |
| **`home.deleteRows`** | **refused** |
| **`home.deleteColumns`** | **refused** |

**Expected.** Excel's permission means what it says: with Delete rows ticked, a protected sheet's rows can be deleted, locked cells included — that is the point of granting it. (Sorting is the documented exception in the other direction: Excel refuses to sort ranges containing locked cells whatever the Sort box says.)

**Cause.** `check_protection` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` runs after every command and refuses when a locked cell's contents changed:

```rust
for c in sh.cells.diff(&after.cells) {
    if !same_content(sh.cell(c), after.cell(c))
        && old.styles.get(sh.style_id(c)).protection.locked
        && let Some(m) = locked_cell_error(sh, c, unlocked)
    { return Err(...) }
}
```

Deleting a row removes locked cells, so the diff sees their contents change and the guard fires before `delete_rows` is ever consulted. Inserting shifts cells without removing any, which is why Insert is unaffected.

**Fix shape.** The guard needs to know which operation produced the new workbook, so a permitted row or column deletion is not judged as an edit of the cells it removed — rather than exempting deletions from the guard, …

title: Draw: Ink to Shape parity (mode-before-draw and Excel's shape set)
author: alosslessdev
body:
# Draw: Ink to Shape parity (mode-before-draw and Excel's shape set)

GridCraft has `draw.inkToShape`, but it works after the fact on the last stroke and recognises only four outcomes (rectangle, ellipse, triangle, line) from bounding-box corner/apex tests. Excel's Ink to Shape is a **mode you turn on before drawing**: each shape drawn is converted automatically to the equivalent Office shape in the ink colour, and can then be styled from the Format tab.

## Excel behaviour (public documentation + black-box observation)

- Draw ▸ **Ink to Shape** turns the mode on; each drawn shape converts automatically. Selecting it again returns to plain inking.
- Converted shapes: rectangle, square, diamond, parallelogram, trapezoid, irregular quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, ellipse, circle, single-headed arrow, double-headed arrow, connector, right triangle, equilateral triangle, isosceles triangle, irregular triangle, block arrow (18 kinds).
- The resulting shape keeps the ink colour; fill, transparency and style are then available on the Format tab.

Reference: <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/convert-ink-to-shapes-in-office-8ca00db0-4342-4bde-bbb2-92d6cb5e2e45>

## Gap vs GridCraft (main, `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`)

- No mode: `draw.inkToShape` converts the last stroke (or `{id}`) on demand.
- Recognition: bounding-box corner/apex heuristics yield Rectangle / Ellipse / Triangle / Line only.
- Model: `ShapeKind` has Rectangle, RoundedRectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Line, Arrow, TextBox, Icon, Ink — no diamond, parallelogram, trapezoid, pentagon, hexagon, right triangle, block or double arrow, so XLSX saves of those shapes cannot round-trip either.

## Proposed PR

1. **Mode.** `draw.inkToShape` toggles a session mode (`{on?: bool}`), and `draw.stroke` converts each completed stroke while the mode is on. The explicit `{id}` conversion stays for programmatic use. One undo step per conversion.
2. **Shape kinds.** Add the DrawingML-preset kinds Excel's conversion…

title: Draw: Action Pen — handwriting recognition (ink to text)
author: alosslessdev
body:
# Draw: Action Pen — handwriting recognition (Ink to Text)

Excel's Draw tab (Microsoft 365, Windows) has an **Action Pen** in the Drawing Tools group: writing in cells with it is converted automatically to typed Excel data. GridCraft's Draw tab has pen, highlighter, eraser, lasso and Ink to Shape, but every stroke stays ink — there is no handwriting recognition.

## Update (2026-10-17): the recognizer must be cross-platform

Handwriting recognition **must be cross-platform**. An implementation that depends on a Windows-only service — Windows Ink / `Windows.UI.Input.Inking`, or any other Windows-specific handwriting feature — is not acceptable. The recognizer must be one implementation that builds and runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD; wasm may stay disabled with a clear message, but must not break the build. Recognition must stay offline: no Office component, no Microsoft cloud service and no network round-trip.

This supersedes the original Windows-only requirement below. **PR #1778 (Windows Ink) has been closed because it is not cross-platform; a new implementation is required.**

### What that implies

There is no OS-independent handwriting service: `Windows.UI.Input.Inking` has no macOS/Linux equivalent, macOS Vision is OCR and platform-specific, and Linux has no standard handwriting service. The only realistic cross-platform, offline design is a recognition model executed in-process:

1. Prefer a **pretrained model with clear, redistributable licence terms**. Creating or training a model is possible but is significant work, and needs its own plan (training data and its licence, conversion, accuracy validation). The options below explain why PdfCraft's pipeline was not adopted.
2. Run it with a **cross-platform inference engine**. RTen (`.rten`/ONNX) is the leading pure-Rust candidate and fits GridCraft; the Nemotron proposal would instead require a GGUF/GGML llama.cpp runtime, which does not exist yet (see below).

title: Ribbon: group captions, dialog launchers and content-sized groups
author: alosslessdev
body:
# Ribbon: group captions, dialog launchers and content-sized groups

Split from #1764 / #1767 (superseded), one PR per feature. Launchers and blank-slot collapse are properties of the group container, so they live in this first ribbon PR (GitHub cannot stack fork branches onto fork branches when the base repo is upstream).

## Currently (main)

The ribbon draws its controls as loose clusters separated by dividers. There are no group captions, no group containers, and no dialog launchers — tabs don't read like Excel's.

## Expected (Excel)

Each cluster is a group: controls packed top-left, the group's caption centred along the bottom of a caption band, and a small dialog-launcher box in the group's bottom-right corner wherever Excel has one and GridCraft has the dialog. - Dialog launchers in the group corner, opening the same dialogs as the related commands.
- Regression tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ribbon_groups.rs`): captions sit under their controls, groups pack left with no reserved space for missing features, and a launcher opens its dialog.

title: Commands that work on one block silently act on only the first area of a multi-area target
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.7.0, current `main` (8ffff19)

### What happens

A command that works on one block takes a comma-separated multi-area range and quietly keeps only its first area — the rest is dropped without a word. With no `range` param, `block()`'s selection fallback picks the selection's *last* area instead, equally silently.

### Steps

Through the control port:

```json
{"command": "range.setValues", "params": {"range": "A1:B1,C2:D2", "values": [["a","b"],["c","d"]]}}
```

The call reports success with `{"cells": 4}`, but the values land in `A1:B2` (grown from the first area's corner) and `C2:D2` is never touched. The same shape affects the rest of the single-block commands: `data.sort` with `"A1:B5,D1:E5"` sorts only `A1:B5`, `sheet.read` reads back only the first area, `pageLayout.printArea` sets the print area to the first area only.

### Where

`target_range()` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`) returned `target_ranges().first()`, and `block()` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`) falls back to `selection.current()` — the last area. Going through them: `range.setValues`; `edit.fillDown`/`fillUp`/`fillLeft`/`fillRight`; `edit.autoFill`; `edit.fillSeries`; `edit.flashFill`; `data.fromTableRange`; `formulas.autoSum` (explicit `range`); `formulas.createFromSelection`; `review.spelling` (explicit `range`); `data.sort`/`sortAscending`/`sortDescending`/`filter`/`removeDuplicates`/`subtotal` (explicit `range`); `data.textToColumns`; `insert.table`/`home.formatAsTable`; `sheet.read` (explicit `range`); `pageLayout.printArea`; `home.insertCells`/`home.deleteCells`. Commands that already walk every area (`range.fill`, the style/border/clear/merge family, `edit.copy`/`edit.cut`, conditional formats, `data.validation`, …) are not affected.

### Expected

Either act on every area like the multi-area commands do, or refuse with an explicit error — Excel shows "This action won't work on multiple selections." here, which `edit.copy` in this repo already uses for unlin…

title: CSV/TSV import: option to keep all fields as text (no type inference)
author: Cockainaa
body:
**Problem**
Opening a CSV always converts fields as if they were typed input (numbers, dates, booleans). That breaks identifier columns: barcodes (GTIN/EAN), SKUs, ZIP codes, phone numbers. A 13-digit GTIN like `8435392892278` becomes a number, leading zeros are dropped (`0123…`), and on *Save As CSV* the value is written as displayed, so it can come out in scientific notation. Round-tripping a product feed through GridCraft can corrupt it.

**Already in the code**
`CsvOptions` has `parse_values` ("otherwise keep text"), and `read_csv` honours it, but the app never exposes it. Both open paths use the defaults: `crates/engine/src/io.rs` (lines 156 and 164, `..Default::default()`, `parse_values: true`), and the same in `crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs`.

**Request**
One of these, in order of preference:
1. A preference such as "Open CSV/TSV as text" (persisted in `prefs.json`), applied to File > Open and to drag-and-drop.
2. An import dialog (like Excel's Text Import / LibreOffice's) with "all columns as text", or per-column type.
3. At least a CLI flag, e.g. `gridcraft --csv-as-text file.csv`.

**Expected**
With the option on, every field is a text cell, kept exactly as in the file, and written back unchanged on save.

title: About: the contributor list is stale and shows 16 of at least 57 contributors
author: arcanii
body:
Split from #1633.

## What happens

Help ▸ About ▸ Contributors lists 16 people. `crates/ui-egui/build.rs` compiles the list from `contributors/contributors.json`, and that file was last generated at `90b3c41` (2026-10-10), when `main` had 148 commits:

- **282 pull requests have been merged since then**, by 50 people. 41 of them aren't in the file at all, so About shows 16 of at least 57 contributors.
- **10 of the 13 entries in `contributors/people.toml`** have no row in the JSON. The names those people chose for themselves aren't shown, since a name is used only when the JSON marks the entry as verified (`people_entry`).

## Fix

Regenerate the snapshot the way `docs/contributors.md` describes, `python3 ../../craftrules/scripts/contributors.py .`, and commit the result. The file is never hand-edited.

Counts are from `upstream/main` at `8ffff19` (2026-10-17) and from `gh pr list --state merged --search "merged:>2026-10-10T19:59:42Z"`.

title: Releasing: refresh contributors/contributors.json as part of the release steps
author: arcanii
body:
Split from #1633.

## What happens

`contributors/contributors.json` is a snapshot by design: `AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributors.md` say maintainers regenerate it with `python3 ../../craftrules/scripts/contributors.py .`. Nothing runs that step regularly, and neither `docs/releasing.md` ("Cutting a release") nor `docs/release-playbook.md` mentions it.

The last refreshes were in the 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 version bumps (`13664fe`, `9f896c1`). 0.6.1 and 0.7.0 shipped with the list from 2026-10-10, so their About window credits 16 of at least 57 contributors.

## Suggestion

- **Add the refresh to the release steps**, next to step 1 ("Bump the version") in `docs/releasing.md`, so the version bump commits a fresh `contributors/contributors.json` and every release credits everyone who worked on it.

title: Insert Chart ignores all but one area of a non-contiguous range (empty or category-less chart)
author: andresilvareis
body:
### What happens

Excel's usual way to chart two separate columns is to select the labels column, Ctrl+select the values column, then Insert ▸ Chart. GridCraft only uses one of the areas:

| How the chart is inserted | Series written to the chart part | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `insert.chart {"range":"A1:A4,C1:C4","type":"pie"}` | name `Sheet1!$A$1`, values `Sheet1!$A$2:$A$4` | Only the **first** area is used. The labels become the "values", so the pie is empty and the legend shows 1, 2, 3 |
| `selection.set {"range":"A1:A4,C1:C4"}` then `insert.chart {"type":"pie"}` | name `Sheet1!$C$1`, values `Sheet1!$C$2:$C$4`, no categories | Only the **last** area is used. The pie has no category labels |
| Expected (as Excel does) | name `Sheet1!$C$1`, categories `Sheet1!$A$2:$A$4`, values `Sheet1!$C$2:$C$4` | |

### Repro (headless, GridCraft 0.7.0)

```sh
V='range.setValues={"range":"A1","values":[["Item","Qtd","Total"],["A",1,10],["B",2,20],["C",3,30]]}'
gridcraft-cli run --cmd "$V" --cmd 'insert.chart={"range":"A1:A4,C1:C4","type":"pie"}' --out multi.xlsx
unzip -p multi.xlsx 'xl/charts/chart*.xml' | grep -o '<c:f>[^<]*</c:f>'
```

The same happens in the desktop app over the control port. The workaround is `chart.selectData {"range":"Sheet1!C1:C4","categories":"Sheet1!A2:A4"}` after inserting.

### Suggested behaviour

Treat a multi-area range or selection the way Excel does: if the areas have the same row span, combine them as if they were adjacent. The first text column becomes the categories, and each further column becomes a series. `insert.chartRecommendations` should see the same combined shape.

### Environment

GridCraft 0.7.0 (AUR `gridcraft`, built from source), Arch Linux x86_64. Not touched by any commit on `main` since v0.7.0 as far as I can see.

title: XLSX: gradient cell fills are flattened to their first stop
author: alosslessdev
body:
## Summary

Excel supports gradient cell fills (`<gradientFill>` in `styles.xml`, Format Cells → Fill → Fill Effects). GridCraft currently:

- reads a gradient as a solid fill using only its first stop (`crates/xlsx/src/styles.rs`);
- writes only `patternFill`, so opening and saving a workbook destroys the gradient;
- has no gradient controls in Format Cells → Fill;
- paints only the solid/pattern approximation in the grid and PDF.

## Expected

- Read and write linear and path gradients with `degree`/convergence, every stop, stop positions, and theme/tint colours.
- Render them in the grid, the in-cell editor, and PDF export.
- Let Format Cells create/edit a gradient; switching to Solid clears the gradient; undo/redo works.

## Scope

Cell fills only. Data-bar gradients are covered by #781/#703; conditional-format colour scales are separate.

## Acceptance

- An Excel-authored workbook with a linear and a path gradient opens, renders, and saves without losing any gradient attribute.
- Round-trip tests compare the full `GradientFill` value, not just a colour.
- Existing solid/pattern fills are unchanged.

title: Charts: add a Pareto chart (sorted bars with cumulative percentage line)
author: alosslessdev
body:
GridCraft has Histogram but no Pareto chart. Excel's Pareto subtype sorts categories by value, draws columns, and overlays a cumulative-percentage line on a secondary 0-100% axis.

Scope: ChartKind::Pareto; renderer (stable descending sort, columns, cumulative line, right percentage axis, labels); insert.chart type pareto; ribbon/dialog/pane; chartex read/write; tests; docs.

Acceptance: insert.chart with type pareto shows sorted bars and the cumulative line; save/reopen keeps ChartKind::Pareto; docs no longer list Pareto as missing.

title: Charts: add a radial bar chart (concentric rings)
author: alosslessdev
body:
A radial bar chart places one category per concentric ring; each ring is an arc from 12 o'clock whose sweep is value / max.

Excel has no native radial bar type (Radar is the closest), so this is a GridCraft extension. It must survive save/reopen.

Scope: ChartKind::RadialBar; renderer (one ring per category, palette colour, track, labels, data labels); insert.chart type radial; ribbon/dialog/pane; XLSX doughnut fallback plus a GridCraft c:extLst marker read back as RadialBar; tests; docs.

Acceptance: insert.chart with type radial shows concentric rings; save/reopen keeps ChartKind::RadialBar; Excel opens the file as a doughnut fallback.

title: Charts: doughnut primitives for Excel parity (one ring per series, hole size, first slice angle)
author: alosslessdev
body:
Excel has no native radial bar chart; users build radial charts from a doughnut/multilayer doughnut, one data series per ring, with helper gap slices. GridCraft's Doughnut kind exists, but its renderer only draws the first series, so multi-ring doughnuts (and the radial templates built from them) do not display.

This issue tracks the Excel-compatible primitives, not a new radial chart type.

**Behaviour to match (Microsoft docs + Excel 365 observation)**
- Every data series is one concentric ring; the first series is outermost (Excel's order).
- Hole size 10–90% (Excel default 75%) and first slice angle 0–359° (default 0°).
- Multi-series legend names the series; a single-series doughnut names its slices.
- `c:holeSize` and `c:firstSliceAng` round-trip through XLSX.

**Scope**
- Renderer: all series as rings, per-point colours, data labels, first slice angle and hole size.
- Model: `hole_size` and `first_slice_angle` on `Chart` with serde defaults.
- XLSX: read/write both fields.
- `chart.set` `holeSize` / `firstSliceAngle`; Format Chart pane sliders.
- Tests: ring order, hole, angle, XLSX round-trip.
- Docs: `docs/chart-parity.md`, `docs/target-app-parity.md`, `docs/roadmap.md`.

**Acceptance**
- A doughnut chart with three series draws three concentric rings, first series outermost.
- Hole size and first slice angle are editable and survive save/reopen.
- The Excel-authored radial-bar template pattern (one ring per helper series) renders all rings.

title: Bug: formatting may not persist after save without format-specific feedback
author: earlvanze
body:
## Report

A community report says that GridCraft does not retain formatting after saving. The report does not specify the input/output format, GridCraft version, or formatting affected.

## Known format boundaries

- `.xlsx` is intended to preserve styles, number formats, fills, borders, alignment, conditional formatting, and related workbook formatting.
- `.xlsb` and `.ods` currently import values only, so formatting is not retained through those paths.
- CSV/TSV are data formats and do not retain spreadsheet formatting.
- Some `.xlsx` style fidelity gaps are already tracked in #1609 and #1818.

## Needed to reproduce

Please provide a minimal workbook, GridCraft version and OS, source and saved filename extensions, the exact formatting applied, and whether the loss occurs immediately after save/reopen or only when opened in another spreadsheet app.

## Expected

For supported `.xlsx` formatting, saving and reopening should preserve the applied formatting. Unsupported format paths should make their limitations clear rather than silently appearing to save formatting.

title: gridcraft-cli audit: report hidden information in .xlsx before sharing

body:
Spreadsheets routinely carry information the sender doesn't know is there: hidden rows and columns (the data stays in the file), hidden and very-hidden sheets, external workbook links in formulas, author names on comments, creator / last-modified-by in core properties, pivot caches carrying source data, hidden defined names. Proposal: `gridcraft-cli audit <file>` scans the raw OPC package, reports findings as machine-readable JSON with stable finding IDs, and exits nonzero when findings exist (CI-gate usable). v1 finding classes: hidden rows/columns, hidden + very-hidden sheets, external workbook links, author PII (comments, core/app properties), pivot caches with source data, hidden defined names.

Out of scope for v1: sanitizing (strip flagged content with a before/after report) — follow-up.

Fixtures will be synthetic, built from ECMA-376 (no Excel-produced files committed, per the clean-room rule).

title: Conditional formatting: colour scales with a formula in a Percent/Percentile stop, or with stops out of order, look different from Excel
author: iluebbe
body:
In two cases GridCraft draws a colour scale from an Excel workbook differently from Excel. In the first case, saving the workbook also changes the rule.

## 1. A Percent or Percentile stop with a formula becomes a Formula stop

Excel lets a Percent or Percentile stop take a formula as its value, e.g. `=$Z$1*10`. GridCraft's reader turns any non-numeric `val` of a `percent` or `percentile` `cfvo` into `CfValueKind::Formula` ([`sheet_read.rs` L568–L569](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/c30fa3f1cf324603f3bfc0171689b1d4083b40e5/crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs#L568-L569)). The model's `Percent(f64)` and `Percentile(f64)` can't hold a formula.

So GridCraft takes the formula's result (20) as the threshold itself, not as 20 % or the 20th percentile. Saving writes `type="formula"`, and from then on Excel shows the changed rule too. The New Formatting Rule editor in #1822 shows the stop as Formula.

A Number stop with a formula (`=$Z$2`) is read as a Formula stop as well. Its colours stay the same; after a save, Excel lists it as Formula instead of Number. Data bars and icon sets use the same `cfvo` reader; they weren't measured.

## 2. Stops that aren't in ascending order

`cf.rs` interpolates only when each threshold is higher than the one before it ([`cf.rs` L224–L230](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/c30fa3f1cf324603f3bfc0171689b1d4083b40e5/crates/engine/src/cf.rs#L224-L230)). Otherwise the position is 0 or 1, so the cells get one or two plain colours. Excel draws these rules as if the thresholds were sorted in ascending order, with the colours kept in stop order: the first stop's colour at the lowest threshold.

Excel's object model accepts such rules; the workbook below was made through it. `home.conditionalFormat` `stops` accepts them too, and so does #1822's dialog, whose Number fields don't check the order.

## Measured

- **Excel:** Excel for Microsoft 365, through COM. It made a workbook with the values 0…10 in A1:F11 (each column), Z1:Z3 = 2, …

title: Windows: GridCraft cannot be selected as default for .xlsx and .csv
author: earlvanze
body:
## Report

On Windows 11, GridCraft may appear in **Open with** but cannot be selected reliably as the default application for `.xlsx` and `.csv` through **Settings > Apps > Default apps**. The reporter suspects this began after a Windows update; the Windows version/build and GridCraft version still need confirmation.

## Expected

The GridCraft MSI should register its workbook and text-data ProgIDs and capabilities so Windows offers GridCraft as a selectable default for `.xlsx` and `.csv`.

## Current packaging intent

`packaging/windows/gridcraft.wxs` registers `GridCraft.Workbook` for `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` and `GridCraft.TextData` for `.csv`/`.tsv`, under `OpenWithProgids`, `Capabilities`, and `RegisteredApplications`. The installer intentionally must not silently change the user's defaults.

## Investigate

- Verify a released MSI on current Windows 11 can be selected for both `.xlsx` and `.csv` in Default apps.
- Record Windows build, GridCraft version, installer versus portable build, and any Settings error.
- Check whether registration is missing after install/upgrade or whether Windows rejects the user-selected association.

Related: <https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/1436> extends OS association coverage to `.xls`, but does not address the reported `.xlsx`/`.csv` default-selection failure.

title: Custom key bindings: a user keymap file for shortcuts and key-tip sequences
author: alt-t-u-t
body:
Follow-up to #110. PR #319 brought the built-in shortcuts close to Excel's published lists, and the key-tip table now covers the whole ribbon. Thank you for both. #110 also asked for "an ability to add them", and @vangel76 noted that custom key bindings were out of scope for #319. This issue covers that part.

**Who this is for:** finance and accounting modelers (banking, equity research, corporate finance) who work keyboard-only and have years of muscle memory, often including bindings from add-ins or their own macros. A tool's defaults never match everyone's habits, so the deciding factor is whether users can fix the gaps themselves.

**Request:** a user keymap file that is loaded at startup and overrides or extends the defaults, for:
1. **Direct shortcuts:** modifier + key → command id (for example `Ctrl+Shift+F` → `home.formatCells`).
2. **Key-tip sequences:** leader + letter sequence → command id (for example `W F F` → `view.freezePanes`), including Excel 2003 menu paths beyond the built-in ones (see #941).

Since every action is already a command id, the file could be very simple, for example `~/Library/Application Support/GridCraft/keymap.toml` (and the matching paths on other platforms):

```toml
[shortcuts]
"Ctrl+Shift+F" = "home.formatCells"

[keytips]
"W F F" = "view.freezePanes"
"T U T" = "formulas.tracePrecedents"
"D G G" = "data.group"
```

Nice to have:
- Unknown command ids and conflicts are reported in the log, not silently ignored.
- A way to export the current effective keymap as a starting point.
- Platform-specific sections (`[shortcuts.macos]`) for people who switch between Windows and Mac.

A Keyboard page in an Options dialog could come later. A plain file covers power users right away.

title: macOS: optional Windows keyboard layout (Ctrl as primary modifier, tapping Option starts key tips)
author: alt-t-u-t
body:
**Request:** an opt-in macOS setting that makes the keyboard behave like Excel for Windows, for people who move between a Windows desktop at work and a Mac, or who simply learned Excel on Windows.

What GridCraft does today (v0.7.0): Cmd is the primary modifier on macOS, which is the right default. Key tips start only with F10 (Fn+F10) on macOS, because Option is kept for accented characters.

What the setting would do when enabled (for example "Keyboard: Windows layout" in Options):
1. **Ctrl acts as the primary modifier.** Ctrl+C/V/Z/B, Ctrl+arrows, Ctrl+Shift+arrows, Ctrl+Page Up/Down, Ctrl+1 and so on behave exactly as on Windows. Cmd can keep its Mac meaning or be ignored.
2. **Tapping Option (press and release with no other key) starts key tips,** the same way tapping Alt does on Windows. Holding Option and typing a letter would still produce accented characters, so text entry is unaffected. The Alt-tap logic in `keytips.rs` already exists and is only gated off on macOS.
3. **Alt+key combinations** (for example Alt+= for AutoSum, Alt+Down to open a filter or validation drop-down) map to Option+key.

Notes:
- macOS reserves some Ctrl combinations by default (Ctrl+arrows switch Spaces, Ctrl+Up opens Mission Control). It would help if the setting's description, or the log, said that users may need to turn those off in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts.
- A keymap file (#1863) could cover this too, but an explicit, documented toggle is far easier for most people than writing one.

Why it matters: right now Windows-trained Mac users have to install Karabiner or Hammerspoon to get this behavior in Excel for Mac. A native GridCraft option would be a real reason for them to switch.

title: Formula auditing from the keyboard: Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+] and a precedent navigator
author: alt-t-u-t
body:
Keyboard formula auditing is one of the most-used workflows in financial models. Trace Precedents/Dependents arrows already exist (and are reachable through key tips), but there is no way to *move* to precedents or dependents from the keyboard.

**1. Excel parity: Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]** (they are not in `docs/ui-parity.md`, present or missing)

| Keys | Excel behavior |
|---|---|
| Ctrl+[ | Select the active cell's **direct precedents**. If they are on another sheet, activate that sheet and select them there. |
| Ctrl+Shift+[ (Ctrl+{ on a US layout) | Select **all** precedents (direct and indirect) |
| Ctrl+] | Select **direct dependents** |
| Ctrl+Shift+] (Ctrl+}) | Select **all** dependents |

Excel for Mac uses the same keys with Control. Repeated presses keep drilling from the new selection, and F5 then Enter returns to the cell you started from. This is how modelers trace a number back through a model.

**2. Beyond Excel: a precedent navigator**

Finance Excel add-ins (FactSet's, among others) offer an auditing mode that Excel lacks. From a formula cell you step through each reference in the formula one at a time, including references on other sheets and nested inside functions, with arrow keys or Tab. Each step jumps to and highlights that range, and Enter or Esc returns to the start.

A proposal for GridCraft, as a separate command (for example `formulas.navigatePrecedents`) with its own shortcut so Excel's Ctrl+Shift+[ meaning is kept:
- A small panel or popover lists every reference in the active cell's formula in order (sheet, range, current value).
- Down/Up or Tab/Shift+Tab moves through the list and selects each range live, switching sheets if needed.
- Right arrow drills into the selected precedent's own formula; Left arrow goes back up a level.
- Enter stays at the current location; Esc returns to the original cell.
- The same for dependents.

GridCraft's dependency graph and command model seem well suited to this, and it would be a real step beyond Exce…

title: Fonts: a cell font saved under its Korean name (e.g. Malgun Gothic as 맑은 고딕) is never matched
author: chessive
body:
Korean Excel often saves a cell's font under its Korean name, e.g. `<name val="맑은 고딕"/>` instead of `Malgun Gothic`. GridCraft doesn't match those names to the installed font, so the cell is drawn in the default face.

## Steps
I made a workbook that sets 맑은 고딕, 굴림, 굴림체, 돋움, 바탕 and 궁서 twice each: once by the English name (Malgun Gothic, Gulim, GulimChe, Dotum, Batang, Gungsuh) and once by the Korean name. Then I opened it in a build where the installed-font scan runs (#1179 merged on top of main, since on main the scan doesn't start, see #1573).

- English names: each row is drawn in its own face (Batang and Gungsuh are easy to tell apart).
- Korean names: every row is drawn in the default face.

The font box shows the right name for each cell, so the file is read correctly. Only the matching fails.

## Cause
`file_faces` in `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs` keeps one name per face (`english_or_first()`), so each face is cataloged under its English name only. A scan on Windows 11 finds `Batang` and `Gungsuh` in batang.ttc but nothing for `바탕` or `궁서`, even though the fonts' name tables include the Korean names.

One more thing for the fix: `font_definitions_with` in `theme.rs` binds a family under the catalog's name (`fnt:Malgun Gothic:nn`), but `cell_family` looks up the name stored in the cell (`fnt:맑은 고딕:nn`). So matching the Korean name alone won't be enough; the binding has to use the cell's name too.

This is close to the name ID 1 point in #1606 (`Noto Sans KR Medium`), which also comes from keeping one name per face. Opening it separately, as asked there. #931 doesn't change this.

## Possible fix
- Keep every family name a face has (all languages, name IDs 16 and 1) and match against any of them. Keep the English name for the font list.
- Bind under the name the workbook uses, so it matches what `cell_family` looks up.

I'd like to try a PR for this, if the approach sounds right.

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200), fonts that ship with Windows. Build: …

title: Wayland: window freezes (no repaint, no input, control/MCP requests stall) while a frame callback is pending, e.g. when the window is hidden or Parsec is running
author: code-reviewer-x
body:
# Wayland: window freezes (no repaint, no input, control/MCP requests stall) while a frame callback is pending, e.g. when the window is hidden or Parsec is running

## Summary

On Linux/Wayland, every control-channel request (and so every MCP tool call made through
`gridcraft-cli mcp --connect`) waits until the window is shown again when the GridCraft window is
fully covered by another window. Requests are only drained inside a UI pass
(`control::poll`, `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1058`), and on Wayland a UI pass only runs after the
compositor sends a frame callback, which GNOME does not send to windows it is not showing. After
60 s the client gets `timed out waiting for the UI (is the window minimised?)` although the window
is not minimised, only covered.

For an agent driving GridCraft through MCP this looks like random freezes, mostly "after a while
doing nothing": the user is looking at the agent's window, which covers GridCraft.

## Environment

- GridCraft 0.8.0 (AppImage) and a local build of `v0.8.0` (823c565) with debug line tables
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-38, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland session
- Hybrid graphics: Intel Arc (MTL, Mesa 26.0.8) + NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop (580.178.04); wgpu Vulkan
- eframe 0.36.2, winit 0.30.13

## Steps to reproduce

1. `gridcraft --control 7979` on a GNOME Wayland session.
2. Send requests in a loop, e.g. `{"id":1,"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}` every 2 s, or any
   `engine.execute`.
3. Cover the GridCraft window completely with another window.

Expected: requests keep being answered (the engine does not need the window to be visible).
Actual: requests block; after 60 s the reply is `timed out waiting for the UI (is the window
minimised?)`; the next request blocks until the window is uncovered.

Measured with a stress script (446 requests, charts/tables/formulas/screenshots, idle pauses):

| Time | Window | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 10:47:30 – 10:49:20 | visible | ~300 requests, all < 7 s |
| 10:51:30 | covered by the us…

title: A control request that timed out still runs later (reply discarded)
author: code-reviewer-x
body:
# A control request that timed out still runs later (reply discarded)

## Summary

When a control-channel request waits more than 60 s, the connection thread replies
`{"ok": false, "error": "timed out waiting for the UI …"}` but the request stays in the queue.
The next time the UI runs a pass, `control::poll` executes it anyway and drops the reply.

The client was told the command failed, yet it is applied. An MCP agent that retries after the
error runs the command twice (duplicate rows, charts, sheets…); a client that gives up leaves an
unexpected change in the workbook.

## Code (v0.8.0)

- `apps/gridcraft/src/control_server.rs:122-129`: `tx.send(req)`, then
  `rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))`, then the timeout reply. Nothing withdraws `req`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:391-407` (`poll`): `while let Ok(req) = rx.try_recv()` runs
  `handle(...)` for every queued request, then `let _ = req.reply.send(v);`, ignoring that the
  receiver is gone.

## Steps to reproduce

(Derived from the code above; observed so far only as the 60 s timeout itself, not yet as a
duplicated change.)

1. On Wayland, cover the GridCraft window (see #1913) or otherwise keep it from running UI passes.
2. Send `{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"cell.set","params":{"cell":"A1","input":"timed out"}}}`.
3. After 60 s the reply is the timeout error.
4. Uncover the window: A1 now contains `timed out`.

## Suggested fix

Withdraw requests whose client stopped waiting: e.g. an `Arc<AtomicBool>` (or a deadline) in
`ControlRequest`, set by the connection thread on timeout, checked by `poll` before `handle`.
Optionally reply `cancelled: timed out` in the journal so the behaviour is visible.

title: Desktop theme watcher opens a new D-Bus session connection every 4 seconds
author: code-reviewer-x
body:
# Desktop theme watcher opens a new D-Bus session connection every 4 seconds

## Summary

On Linux, `DesktopTheme::start` (`crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs`) polls the portal every
`POLL` = 4 s, and each `read()` calls `zbus::blocking::Connection::session()`: a new connection,
SASL handshake and `Hello` every 4 s for the whole life of the app (≈ 900 connections an hour).

With `RUST_LOG=info` the log fills with zbus handshake lines from the `gridcraft-desktop-theme`
thread (74 handshakes in the first 5 minutes of a session):

```
INFO [gridcraft-desktop-theme] zbus::connection::handshake::common: write_command; command=Auth(Some(External), …)
INFO [gridcraft-desktop-theme] zbus::connection::handshake::common: write_commands; commands=[NegotiateUnixFD, Begin] …
```

## Suggested fix

Open the connection once and keep it, or better subscribe to the portal's
`org.freedesktop.portal.Settings.SettingChanged` signal for `color-scheme` and stop polling.
At minimum, reuse the connection between polls.

Environment: GridCraft 0.8.0, Ubuntu 26.04.1, GNOME Shell 50.1 (Wayland).

Related: #530 (the same reader does not query `org.freedesktop.appearance`); PR #504 adds a second
portal watcher polling every 4 s, which would double this if it follows the same pattern.

title: fix(edit): Ctrl+Enter drops the automatic number format in cells that already hold a value
author: vedran-dobos
body:
## Summary

Typing `5%` into a General cell shows 5% (the input gets the automatic `0%` format). Entering the
same input in a selection with Ctrl+Enter (`range.fill`) gives that format only to the cells that
were empty. A cell that already held a value keeps General and shows 0.05. The same goes for every
automatic format: currency, dates, times and the date formulas (`=TODAY()`, `=DATE(…)`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Type `1` in A2.
2. Select A1:A2 (A1 active), type `5%` and press Ctrl+Enter.

The same thing happens through the control channel:
`range.setValues {"range":"A2","values":[[1]]}`, `selection.set {"range":"A1:A2","active":"A1"}`,
`range.fill {"input":"5%"}`.

## Expected behavior

Both cells show 5%, as typing `5%` into each of them does. Excel’s Ctrl+Enter does the same.

## Actual behavior

| Input | A1 (was empty) | A2 (held 1) |
|---|---|---|
| `5%` | 5% | 0.05 |
| `$5` | $5 | 5 |
| `3/4/2026` | 3/4/2026 | 46085 |
| `=DATE(2026,3,ROW())` | 3/1/2026 | 46083 |

A related case: an empty cell in a formatted column (say B:B is `0.00`) takes the *active* cell’s
format instead of its own, so `5%` filled over A1:B1 shows 5% in B1 rather than 0.05.

## Runtime or environment

GridCraft `main` at 66ce6be (0.8.0), built from source on Windows 11 with Rust 1.99.0.

## Additional context

`range_fill` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` parses the input once, at the active cell, with
`input_to_cell`, which also picks the automatic format. Then, for each target cell that already
holds a cell, it puts back that cell’s old style, which drops the format the input got. An empty
target keeps the active cell’s style, row and column formats included. A PR will follow.

title: XLSX: Excel linked data types (Currencies, Stocks) open as #VALUE!, =A1.Price doesn't calculate, and saving drops them
author: dsaiko
body:
## In short

In Excel you can turn a cell into a live record, for example a currency pair (Data › Currencies) or a stock (Data › Stocks). The cell then shows a small bank or stock icon and the name, such as `EUR/USD`, and other cells read its fields with formulas like `=A1.Price`. People use this to keep exchange rates and investment portfolios up to date.

GridCraft doesn't support these "linked data types" yet:

- **Opening:** the record cell shows `#VALUE!` instead of `EUR/USD`.
- **Calculating:** formulas such as `=A1.Price` can't be calculated.
- **Saving:** the file is written back without the records, so the data is lost for Excel users too.

This request asks GridCraft to keep these records, show their saved values, and later refresh them from a price source.

---

## Details

### How Excel stores a linked data type

A workbook made in Excel with `EUR/USD` in A1 converted through Data › Currencies, and `=A1.Price` in B1, contains:

**The record cell.** It holds an error as the fallback for apps that don't understand rich values, plus a value-metadata index:

```xml
<c r="A1" s="1" t="e" vm="1"><v>#VALUE!</v></c>
```

**The field formula.** `=A1.Price` is stored as `_FV(A1,"Price")`, the field-value form of `FIELDVALUE`. Excel marks it as an always-calculate array formula:

```xml
<c r="B1" cm="1"><f t="array" aca="1" ref="B1" ca="1">_FV(A1,"Price")</f><v>1.0842</v></c>
```

**`xl/metadata.xml`.** The `XLRICHVALUE` future metadata maps each `vm` index to a rich value (`<xlrd:rvb i="…"/>`). `XLDAPR` covers the dynamic-array `cm` of the formula cell.

**`xl/richData/rdrichvaluestructure.xml`** defines two structures:
- `_linkedentity`: a single key, `%cvi` (type `r`), pointing to the core value.
- `_linkedentitycore`: the record itself.
  - Display keys: `_Display`, `_DisplayString`, `_Flags`, `_Format`, `_Icon`, `_SubLabel`.
  - Entity keys: `%EntityCulture`, `%EntityId`, `%EntityServiceId`, `%IsRefreshable`, `%ProviderInfo`.
  - The data fields themselves, fo…

title: Wrap Text: the row grows too little and cuts off the last lines of the text
author: jcagudelo12
body:
**Environment:** Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland, built from source (main @ 66ce6be)

**Steps**
1. Make column A narrow (e.g. 12 characters).
2. Type a sentence in A1, e.g. "Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware across the solar system–on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space."
3. Turn on Wrap Text for A1.

**Expected:** the row grows to show every wrapped line, as in Excel.
**Actual:** the row is too short; the last lines are cut off and the row has to be resized by hand.

**Cause:** `auto_row_height` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`) counts a wrapped cell's lines as its
estimated text width over the column width, as if words could split anywhere. The grid wraps whole
words, so each line ends early and a narrow column needs more lines than counted. The per-character
width estimate also differs from the font that draws the text, so a word can move to its own line
where the estimate thought it fit.

title: Embedded hub: post gridcraft:opened after a hub-supplied document finishes loading
author: ChristianGrubbs
body:
## Summary
When GridCraft runs embedded in the SCC Space Creative Hub, the host has no signal that a document handed to the app has finished opening. The hub's host agent waits for an `gridcraft:opened` (or `gridcraft:loaded`) message and gives up after 5 s. The document is really open 1.8–2.4 s after it is handed over, so every launch with a file shows "Opening…" about 5 s longer than it needs to.

## Evidence
Measured on 2026-10-19 against the served build, headless Chromium, 3 cold and 3 warm launches per app across two runs:
- PdfCraft: `opened` reported at 7.4 s against a true delivery of 2.4 s.
- CADCraft: 6.9 s against 1.9 s.
- GridCraft: 6.7 s against 1.8 s.
- The gap was 5002–5003 ms in every one of the 36 runs.

## Request
The hub hands the file to the app with a `{ type: 'gridcraft:open', name, bytes }` message on `window.parent`. After the app has finished loading that document and is showing it, it should post one reply:

```js
window.parent.postMessage({ type: 'gridcraft:opened', name }, location.origin);
```

If the open fails, post `{ type: 'gridcraft:open-failed', name, error }` instead. The hub will treat that as a failed open rather than waiting out the timeout.

## Workaround on our side
Until this ships, the hub will resolve the open shortly after the hand-off. That works but can't detect a failed open.

body:
Hello GridCraft team,
I am writing to follow up on the Spanish formula localization work implemented in #45 and merged via #98 in v0.5.0.
