title: Test table_filter_autofit_works_through_command_and_header_double_click fails on Windows
author: iluebbe
body:
`table_filter_autofit_works_through_command_and_header_double_click` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/header_autofit.rs` fails on Windows. Checked on `main` at a1c84547, Windows 11:

```
heading overlaps filter: zoom=50, double_click=false
```

CI runs `cargo xtask ci` on Ubuntu only, so it stays green there. On Windows `cargo xtask ci` fails at this test. It also failed the same way in the checks of #942, #899, #2083 and other UI PRs merged into `main` locally.

**Cause:** the test expects the heading to take the width `approx_text_width` gives ([header_autofit.rs#L186-L187](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/a1c84547e3485606a5d8b6fab07dd3a072aa6c52/crates/ui-egui/tests/header_autofit.rs#L186-L187)). `home.autofitColumnWidth` doesn't use that estimate when `Session::text_width` is set: the UI sets it to measure with the installed font ([lib.rs#L1151](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/a1c84547e3485606a5d8b6fab07dd3a072aa6c52/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1151)). On Windows the heading's font, Calibri, is installed and measures narrower than the estimate:

| "Quarterly Revenue" in the heading's style | width |
|---|---|
| `approx_text_width` (what the test checks against) | 121.7 pt |
| `Session::text_width` (what AutoFit used) | 111.6 pt |

AutoFit makes column A 151 pt wide. At zoom 50 (scale 0.4), the estimated text plus the 2.5 pt gap ends at 78.69 px, while the filter button starts at 78.6 px, so the assertion fails by 0.09 px. The column fits the measured width, so this looks like a test problem, not a layout problem (not checked by eye in the app).

Measuring the expected width the same way AutoFit does (through `app.session.text_width` when it is set, otherwise `approx_text_width`) would make the test independent of the installed fonts.

title: Deleting many separate rows takes tens of seconds
author: iluebbe
body:
Deleting many separate rows at once (Ctrl-selected rows, or a Go To Special selection, then Delete Sheet Rows) takes tens of seconds on a sheet of moderate size. Deleting the same number of rows as one block takes well under a second.

**Checked:** `main` at a1c84547, release build of `gridcraft-cli`, Windows 11. Sheet with values in A1:C20000 (60,000 cells, no formulas), then `selection.set` with single-cell areas in every 10th row from row 2 and `home.deleteRows {}`. Times are for the whole `gridcraft-cli run` (opening the file alone takes about 0.3 s):

| Rows deleted | Time |
|---|---|
| 2,000 rows as one block (`A2:A2001`) | 0.4 s |
| 250 separate rows (rows 2, 12, …, 2492) | 12 s |
| 2,000 separate rows (rows 2, 12, …, 19992) | 37–46 s |
| 2,000 separate rows through `{"rows": "2:2,12:12,…"}` | 37 s |
| 200 separate rows on a 2,000-row sheet with one column | 0.4 s |

The result is right; only the time is the problem.

**Where:** `delete_lines` deletes the areas one at a time, last first. For each area it takes the cells, shifts every cell below it, shifts the sheet's features and rewrites the workbook's formulas ([sheet.rs#L351-L382](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/a1c84547e3485606a5d8b6fab07dd3a072aa6c52/crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs#L351-L382)). So the work grows with the number of areas times the size of the sheet. Removing all areas in one pass (one shift per cell, one formula rewrite with the full list of deleted lines) would make it about as fast as deleting one block. Deleting columns goes through the same loop.

Found while checking #1378 (for #1295), which lets Go To Special keep up to 65,536 areas, so selections like this get easier to make.

title: Security tracking: patch publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, then work through the robustness findings
author: Higgs32584
body:
Tracking issue for the security and robustness findings filed as #2157–#2183, plus related older issues (#777, #999, #1662). Sorted by **verified** impact, with the fix PR for each.

Every item was checked against a release build of `main` at d1db71d0 on Windows 11 x64 (details and measurements: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/2290#issuecomment-6349021426).

**Status:** ✅ reproduced · 🔍 confirmed in code, not run · ❌ not reproduced · ✔️ fixed on main

## Step 1 — Crash or hang when opening a small file

These are the most serious: a file of a few KB takes GridCraft down, and unsaved work in other workbooks is lost.

- [x] **#1662** ✅ Endless recursive LAMBDA overflows the 1 MB main-thread stack (`0xC00000FD`), also on open → #1809 (partial)
- [ ] **#2183** ✅ Range-operator chains make dependency extraction exponential (~4× per 2 operands; <500 chars ≈ days) → #2198
- [ ] **#2173** ✅ XLSX reader copies attacker-sized strings per cell or rule (a 2 KB file → 786 MB, growing linearly). Item (d) is smaller than first stated (~9 KB per cell) but slow to open (27 s per 10k cells) → #2197

## Step 2 — Local attack surface (opt-in or needs an existing foothold)

- [ ] **#2174** Medium ✅ Control channel accepts commands without a token. It's opt-in, and browser/HTTP requests are already rejected → #2205 (also closes the rest of #777)
- [ ] **#2176** Low ✅ Windows opener is resolved from the app folder. Defence in depth: the same folder can already plant DLLs that load at launch → #2204
- [ ] **#2181** Low ✅ `link.open` from `mcp --connect` / the control channel skips the confirmation. Scripts are already blocked (#2209) → #2203
- [ ] **#2172** Low–Medium ✅ MCP and control-channel file commands accept any path. Needs a design decision on MCP roots → no PR yet

## Step 3 — Resource limits (hardening)

- [ ] **#2157** ✅ No per-formula budget (`REPT(…)&SEQUENCE(n)`: ~315 MB per 10k rows) → needs a fix
- [ ] **#2162** ✅ REGEXREPLACE builds ~1.5 GB before its length c…

title: Incorrect Euro Currency Formatting for German Locale
author: BjoernD000
body:
Incorrect Euro Currency Formatting in the Latest Version

In the latest version of Gridcraft, Euro amounts appear to be formatted incorrectly when using the German locale.

For example, an amount is currently displayed as:

€ 500.00

This follows the English number format and does not match the standard German currency format.

Euro amounts should be displayed using the German format:

500,00 €

The formatting conventions should be:

- Decimal separator: Comma (,)
- Thousands separator: Period (.)
- Currency symbol: After the amount, separated by a space

Example for a larger amount: 1.500,00 €

In the latest version:

- The Euro symbol appears before the amount.
- A period is used as the decimal separator instead of a comma.

Please ensure that currency formatting respects the configured language or locale, so that Euro amounts follow German formatting conventions when the German locale is selected.

title: Format as Table inside an existing table fails instead of restyling it
author: dfendr
body:
Home > Format as Table with the active cell (or a selected range) inside an existing table fails with "A table can't overlap another table."

In Excel, picking a style from Format as Table while inside a table applies that style to the table. Microsoft's "Format an Excel table" support page describes this.

**Steps**
1. Put a few rows of data in A1:B3 and make it a table.
2. Select B2.
3. Home > Format as Table > pick any style.

**Expected:** the table takes the new style.
**Actual:** error "A table can't overlap another table."; the style is unchanged.

A range that crosses a table's edge should still be rejected.

Fix: #2295

title: Table styles don't look like Excel's: gallery rows look alike and the neutral band is invisible
author: dfendr
body:
The table styles don't look like Excel's.

1. **Rows of the gallery look the same.** Excel's Format as Table gallery has distinct layouts per row: Light 1-7 (rules only), 8-14 (solid header, ruled box), 15-21 (vertical grid); Medium 1-7 (solid header, frame), 8-14 (white tile gaps), 15-21 (black rules), 22-28 (tinted grid); Dark 1-7, 8 and 9-11 (two accents). GridCraft renders every row of a family from one template, so e.g. Light 8 and Light 15 look the same.
2. **The neutral band is invisible.** Column 1's band is white darkened about 3%, so Light 1 and Medium 1 look unbanded.
3. **The gallery swatches** draw only fills and one bottom line per row: no vertical lines, outer border or grid.

**Steps:** Insert a table, open Table Design > Table Styles (or Home > Format as Table) and compare rows of the gallery, or apply Light 8 and Light 15 and compare.

title: A chain of dynamic-array formulas reading each other's spill areas stays stale after the eight recalculation rounds
author: RedBearAK
body:
I ran into this while working on multi-threaded recalculation (#2319), and it is worth its own issue because it is a wrong result on current main, not a performance matter.

## What happens

When several dynamic-array formulas form a chain, and each one reads the *spilled cells* of the previous one rather than its anchor cell, the chain does not settle. After a full recalculation, the formulas near the end of the chain show values that are too small, and several of them show the same value.

## How to see it

Put `1` in `Z1`, then enter these formulas, in this order of columns from right to left:

| Cell | Formula |
|---|---|
| `K1` | `=SEQUENCE(600,1,Z1)` |
| `J1` | `=SEQUENCE(600,1,MAX(K2:K600))` |
| `I1` | `=SEQUENCE(600,1,MAX(J2:J600))` |
| ... | and so on, each column reading the one to its right |
| `A1` | `=SEQUENCE(600,1,MAX(B2:B600))` |

Each `SEQUENCE` spills 600 numbers starting from the largest value in the previous column's spill area, so each column should start 599 higher than the one before it. Column K starts at 1, J at 600, I at 1199, and so on; `A1` should be 5991 and `A600` should be 6590.

What GridCraft shows after a full recalculation instead:

| Cell | Expected | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| `A1` | 5991 | 4193 |
| `B1` | 5392 | 4193 |
| `C1` | 4793 | 4193 |
| `D1` | 4194 | 4194 |
| `A600` | 6590 | 4792 |

Columns D to K are right. Columns A, B and C are stale, three links short, and all three show the same number. Excel gives the expected values.

## Why it happens

Each formula reads the spill *area* of the one before it, not its anchor cell. When the workbook is calculated, those spilled cells are plain values, not formulas, so the engine has no way to calculate the previous column on demand while evaluating the next one. In row-major order `A1` is calculated first, when `B2:B600` still holds the old values, then `B1`, and so on down the chain. The write-back after a pass notices that a spill changed, queues the formulas that read its area, and …

title: Calc: a dynamic-array formula in a table column that returns one value shows #SPILL! (regression in 0.11.1)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.11.1 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 (de-DE). 0.10.0 calculates the same file correctly.

**Fixture:** [`gridcraft/gc_table_filter_da.xlsx`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/gridcraft/gc_table_filter_da.xlsx), written by [`make_gc_table_dynamic_array.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/gridcraft/make_gc_table_dynamic_array.py) (standard library only, hand-written SpreadsheetML, nothing created or saved by Excel). Table `T_Main` has a calculated column `Owner` with `=FILTER(T_Data[Owner],T_Data[Key]=[@Key])`, stored the way Excel 365 stores it: `calculatedColumnFormula array="1"`, every cell `cm="1"` with `t="array"` and a one-cell `ref`. Each row matches exactly one row of `T_Data`. Controls: the same `FILTER` outside the table (`Main!F2`) and a plain calculated column (`COUNTIF`) in the same table.

**Steps:** `gridcraft-cli check gc_table_filter_da.xlsx --json` (or open the file and recalculate).

**Expected** (Excel for Microsoft 365, full recalculation through COM): `Main!B2:B4` = South, East, North (`HasSpill` = false); `F2` = South; `C2:C4` = 1.

**Actual (0.11.1):** `B2:B4` = `#SPILL!` (check: 3 mismatches, signature `text → #SPILL!`). `F2` and the `COUNTIF` column are correct. 0.10.0: 0 mismatches.

**Likely cause:** since #1510 (the fix for #1491) a one-value result is recorded as a 1 × 1 spill range, and `spill_blocked` in `crates/calc/src/recalc.rs` treats every spill anchored in a table as blocked (`sh.tables.iter().any(|t| t.range.contains(anchor))`; the same condition is in `spills_as_before`). Excel refuses only results of more than one cell inside a table; a one-value result is shown. Keeping the table condition for arrays larger than 1 × 1 should restore 0.10.0's behaviour without undoing #1491.

**Impact:** in the 0.11.1 corpus rerun (to be posted on #891) seven real-world workbooks with this pattern gained between 3,500 and 6,200 formula mismatches each, almost all `#SPILL!`…

body:
Excel can't open an XLSX that GridCraft saved with a picture placed in a cell. Opening it with repair fails too. Checked on `main` at ac8da7d4 (0.11.1), Windows 11, Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0, build 20430) through COM, files opened read-only.

| Workbook saved by `gridcraft-cli run` | Excel |
|---|---|
| `=SEQUENCE(3)` in D1, no picture | opens |
| floating picture at E10 (`insert.picture` without `placement`) | opens |
| 40 × 20 px PNG in B2: `insert.picture={"placement":"cell","at":"B2","path":"red.png"}` | can't be opened, also not with repair (`CorruptLoad` = repair) |
| the same picture plus `=SEQUENCE(3)` in D1 | can't be opened, also not with repair |

#1533 (for #1429) changes the rich-value parts the writer adds ([richdata.rs#L309-L350](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/xlsx/src/richdata.rs#L309-L350): part content types, the `ext` URI and the `XLRICHVALUE` metadata type). With it the picture-only workbook opens in Excel, but a workbook with an in-cell picture and a dynamic-array formula still can't be opened (see the check of #1533 on #1429).

title: Calc: clearing a dynamic array leaves the array it blocked at #SPILL! until Calculate Now
author: iluebbe
body:
When a dynamic array that blocks another one is cleared or overwritten, the blocked array stays `#SPILL!` until the next full recalculation. Excel spills it at once. Checked on `main` at ac8da7d4 (0.11.1), Windows 11, `gridcraft-cli run`, compared with Excel for Microsoft 365 through COM (automatic calculation).

1. C14: `=SEQUENCE(1,7)`, which spills to C14:I14.
2. F13: `=SEQUENCE(5,2)`. Its area F13:G17 overlaps F14:G14, so it shows `#SPILL!`.
3. Clear C14 (`edit.clearContents`, the Delete key), or type `5` into C14.

| | GridCraft | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| after step 2 | F13 `#SPILL!` | F13 `#SPILL!` |
| C14 cleared | F13 stays `#SPILL!` | F13 spills to F13:G17 (1 … 10) |
| `5` typed into C14 | F13 stays `#SPILL!` | F13 spills |
| then Calculate Now (F9) | F13 spills | |

When the blocking array itself turns into `#SPILL!` because a value is typed into its area, the other array does spill (`a_spill_that_goes_away_unblocks_another`). Only clearing or overwriting the blocking formula is missed.

**Cause:** an edit re-evaluates `#SPILL!` anchors near the edited cells only ([recalc.rs#L983-L1014](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/calc/src/recalc.rs#L983-L1014)): anchors up to 64 rows and columns above and to the left of an edited cell, and, for an emptied cell, anchors above and to the left of it. The cells the old spill area frees (D14:I14 here) don't count as emptied, and F13 is to the right of C14, so F13 isn't re-evaluated. Treating the freed spill area of an anchor like emptied cells would cover this case.

title: AutoFilter: the filter range doesn't grow when data is entered in the row below it
author: iluebbe
body:
An AutoFilter range doesn't grow when data is typed in the row right below it, so the new rows stay outside the filter. In Excel the range grows. Checked on `main` at ac8da7d4 (0.11.1), Windows 11, `gridcraft-cli run`, compared with Excel for Microsoft 365 through COM.

A1:B5 holds the header Name / Qty and the rows d 4, b 2, a 1, c 3, with an AutoFilter on A1:B5.

| Step | GridCraft | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| AutoFilter on A1:B5 | range A1:B5 | range A1:B5 |
| `e` in A6, `5` in B6 | A1:B5 | A1:B6 (already after A6) |
| Reapply | A1:B5 | A1:B6 |
| filter Qty > 2, then `f` / `1` in row 7, Reapply | A1:B5; rows 3 and 4 hidden, row 7 shown | A1:B7; rows 3, 4 and 7 hidden |
| a row typed after a blank row (row 9), Reapply | | A1:B7, not grown |

Excel grows the range as soon as a value is entered in the row below (here set through COM); the new row is hidden by the next Reapply.

In GridCraft the range is set only by `data.filter` ([data.rs#L539-L553](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs#L539-L553)) and moved by row and column inserts and deletes. Cell entry never changes it. Everything else reads that stored range:
- filtering and Reapply ([`apply_filter`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs#L656-L659));
- the drop-down's value list ([`filter_values`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs#L766-L770));
- the saved file, which keeps `<autoFilter ref="A1:B5">`.

#1122 (for #1097) makes sorting use the stored range as well, so rows typed below would also be left out of a sort (see the check of #1122 on #1097).

title: Objects set to "Don't move or size with cells" move when rows above or columns to the left are resized
author: iluebbe
body:
Pictures, shapes and charts set to "Don't move or size with cells" move when a row above them or a column to their left changes size. In Excel they stay where they are. Checked on `main` at ac8da7d4 (0.11.1), Windows 11, `gridcraft-cli run`, Excel for Microsoft 365 through COM.

A 200 × 40 px picture inserted at E10 with `"mode": "absolute"`, then saved and opened in Excel:

| Change in GridCraft before saving | Picture in Excel (Left, Top in pt) |
|---|---|
| none | 204, 128.25 |
| row 1 height 60 pt (`home.rowHeight`) | 204, 174 |
| column A width 30 characters (`home.columnWidth`) | 325.9, 128.25 |

All three files store `<xdr:twoCellAnchor editAs="absolute">` with `from` at E10, so the picture follows the cell. For comparison, in Excel itself (Placement 3, at 192, 135 pt), setting row 1 to 60 pt and column A to 30 characters leaves the shape at 192, 135. A "Move but don't size" shape moves down 45.75 pt.

**Cause:** the model keeps every object as an anchor cell plus an offset ([`Anchor`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/model/src/features.rs#L384-L395)), absolute ones too. The reader turns an `absoluteAnchor` position into a cell and offset with the row heights it has at that point ([drawing.rs#L59-L73](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/ac8da7d49cbeb4be6aa1ad5869f3d29fe2da8cd9/crates/xlsx/src/drawing.rs#L59-L73)). Row-height and column-width changes don't adjust absolute anchors.

The same shows up on open: GridCraft makes default-height rows taller to fit a larger Normal font, and absolute objects below them move down. With Verdana 16, rows 1–3 went from 15 to 21.82 pt and an absolute picture moved from 135 to 155.5 pt (see the check of #1272 on #1271).

title: [Feature Request] Add "Print Selection" and "Set Print Area" features (similar to Office 365)
author: akhilmiles
body:
### **Feature Description**
Currently, when trying to print a spreadsheet layout, GridCraft defaults to formatting the entire active sheet. It is missing the native layout controls found in standard office software like Microsoft Office 365 (Excel) that let users isolate specific data ranges for printing.

### **Desired Behavior**
I would like to request two key printing features modeled after the Office 365 workflow:

1. **Print Selection Toggle:** Inside the standard print dialog (`Ctrl + P`), add a settings dropdown or radio button to switch from "Print Active Sheets" to **"Print Selection"**. When chosen, the print preview and output should dynamically isolate and render only the user's highlighted grid cells (e.g., A1:D15), hiding the rest of the canvas.
2. **Set Print Area option:** Add an option under a Page Layout menu to permanently "Set Print Area" for the sheet based on the active selection. 
3. **Scaling Controls:** Basic options to "Fit All Columns on One Page" or "Fit All Rows on One Page" when printing a selection so the text isn't cut off at the page margins.

### **Why this is needed**
For users transitioning from traditional office suites to the Craft ecosystem, being able to quickly print a small table or receipt block out of a larger data sheet without exporting it to a new file is essential for a standard desktop workflow.

title: Web embedding: host-controlled read-only session with editing blocked and Save disabled
author: gamma
body:
## Use case

An embedding application can grant a user permission to view a workbook without permission to modify it (for example, an attachment preview or a drive viewer). Rejecting saves in the host protects the stored file, but the editor still accepts changes and presents an active Save button. Users can spend time editing changes that cannot be persisted.

## Requested behavior

Add a host-controlled, session-level read-only mode for the web build:

- Let the trusted same-origin parent specify read-only when opening a workbook, before editing becomes possible. A proposed extension is `readOnly: true` on `gridcraft:open`; the exact protocol is open for discussion.
- Block document mutations at the command/input layer, including cell and formula edits, formatting, paste, cut, drag-and-drop, structural changes, and undo/redo that changes the workbook. Greying out the ribbon alone is insufficient.
- Disable Save and Save As in the ribbon, quick-access toolbar, menus, and keyboard shortcuts. Do not emit `gridcraft:save` in a read-only session.
- Keep scrolling, sheet navigation, zoom, find, selection, and copy available. Show a clear read-only indicator.
- Keep this separate from workbook/sheet protection: do not alter the workbook or save a protection setting into the file, and do not let an in-editor action lift the host-imposed restriction.
- Accept the setting only through the existing trusted host boundary. The host must continue enforcing write permissions on the server; this mode makes the UI match those permissions.

## Suggested acceptance checks

title: Charts: automatic axis step ignores the chart's size; Excel's interval limit grows with plot height (1 to 10)
author: bldred
body:
GridCraft's automatic value axis picks its major unit in `crates/chart/src/axis.rs` (`nice_steps`): the smallest step of 1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ that gives **at most 8 intervals**, whatever the chart's size. Excel uses the same steps, but the number of intervals it allows depends on how tall the plot is: from 1 on a very short chart, through 9 at the default 5 × 3 in, up to a ceiling of 10. So GridCraft gets the step wrong on default-size charts (95…100: Excel 92–101 by 1, GridCraft 92–102 by 2) and on small ones (Excel 90–110 by 10 at 2.5 × 1.5 in).

**Measured** black-box in Excel for Windows (Microsoft 365) over four rounds of synthetic workbooks written by GridCraft. These are column charts with a title, a bottom legend and no axis titles, on an automatic axis, read from Format Axis ▸ Bounds/Units or the axis labels. Chart heights are as Excel's Shape Height reported them.

| Chart height | Interval limit | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1.43 in | 1 | max 28 → 0–50 by 50; max 70 → 0–100 by 100 (both reject 2) |
| 1.5 in (2.5 in wide) | 2 | 95…100 → 90–110 by 10 (rejects 3); max 40 → 0–50 by 50 |
| 1.67 in | 2 | max 28 → 0–40 by 20 (rejects 3) |
| 1.91 in | 3 | max 28 → 0–30 by 10 (rejects 6); max 70 → 0–100 by 50 (rejects 4) |
| 2.38 in | 6–7 | max 28 → by 5 (6); max 70 → 0–80 by 20 (rejects 8) |
| 3 in (default) | 9 | max 40 → 0–45 by 5 (9); max 47.5 → 0–50 by 10 (rejects 10); 9.5M → by 2M (rejects 10) |
| 3.8–6.25 in | 10 | 2, 5, 9.5 → 0–10 by 1 (10); 10.4…13.3 → by 2 (reject 11–14) |

Other findings:
- Steps are 1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ only. A step of 2.5 (max 21) or 4 (max 33.3) is never used, even when it would fit.
- Decimals follow the same rule: 0.95…1.00 → 0.92–1.01 by 0.01.
- A horizontal value axis (bar chart, scatter X) at the default 5 in width allows 9: the stacked bar 45200… → 45180–45240 by 10 rejects 10. Other widths weren't measured.
- A scatter chart's Y axis pads differently (95…100 → 94–101, not 92), which is outside this issue.

title: File › Print: no orientation, paper size, margins or scaling choices (Windows)
author: tsuspe
body:
### Description
On Windows, File › Print only offers the printer settings, "Print Active Sheets / Entire Workbook", "Fit Sheet on One Page" and a "Page Setup…" link. Excel's Print view also has, next to the preview:
- Portrait / Landscape orientation
- Paper size
- Margins presets (Normal / Wide / Narrow / Custom)
- Scaling: No Scaling, Fit Sheet on One Page, Fit All Columns on One Page, Fit All Rows on One Page

Each of these updates the preview as soon as it changes. Today you have to leave the print view (Page Layout tab or Page Setup…) to change them, and you can't see the effect while choosing.

This is the "Portrait and landscape orientation missing from print options" point split out of #2105 (also mentioned in #1416). Column/row fitting is tracked in #2353, and Print Selection in #2351.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open an existing .xlsx that was made in Excel.
2. File › Print (Ctrl+P).

### Expected
The orientation, paper size, margins and scaling controls appear in the print view, using the sheet's current page setup (`sheet.print`). Changing one updates the preview and is saved to the sheet, as it is in Excel.

### Actual
None of these controls are in the print view. Only the margins can be reached, through Page Setup…, and the preview doesn't show the result while you are choosing.

GridCraft updated on 2026-10-22 through ArtCraft Launcher (v0.10.0 or v0.11.1), Windows. Still reproducible on `main` at ac8da7d: `backstage.rs` has no orientation, paper size, margins or scaling controls.

`crates/ui-egui/src/backstage.rs` `fn print`: the left column only renders `printing::show`, the scope combo, the fit-to-page checkbox and the Page Setup link. title: Ctrl+Alt+click follows a hyperlink; Auto Fill Options button uses unmirrored bounds on right-to-left sheets
author: xc4pr
body:
Two review points from #2314 and #2315 that are still open on `main` (both in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`).

### 1. Ctrl+Alt+click on a hyperlink's text follows the link

Steps to reproduce:
1. Put a hyperlink in B4 that points to F9 inside the workbook.
2. Select B2.
3. Ctrl+Alt+click (Cmd+Option on macOS) on B4's link text.

Expected: B4 is added to the selection (B2, B4), the same as Ctrl+Alt+click did before #2314 and as Ctrl+click beside the link text still does.
Actual: the link is followed and the selection jumps to F9.

Cause: the hyperlink condition in the Ctrl/Cmd click branch does not exclude Alt.

### 2. Auto Fill Options button on a right-to-left sheet is checked against the unmirrored cells area

Steps to reproduce:
1. Turn on Sheet Right-to-Left, type 1 and 2 in B1:B2 and drag the fill handle down a few rows. The Auto Fill Options button appears.
2. Scroll horizontally so the filled range sits at the left edge of the grid on screen: the button disappears, although it fits inside the cells.
3. Scroll the other way until the range's corner is just behind the row headings: the button is drawn on top of the row headings.

Expected: the button shows wherever it fits inside the visible cells, as on a left-to-right sheet, and never covers the headings.
Actual: see steps 2 and 3.

Cause: `fill_options_tag` mirrors the button into screen space and then checks it against `geo.cells`, which is in logical (unmirrored) coordinates.

The error-check tag (`error_check_tag`) compares its mirrored tag with `geo.cells` in the same way. It is only mentioned here; the fix for this issue does not change it.

Version/Commit: `main` at 168acc5
OS: Linux

title: Linux (Fedora 44/KDE Wayland): two-finger trackpad scrolling is very slow and has no momentum
author: ChristopheAwad
body:
## Summary

On Fedora 44 KDE Plasma (Wayland), GridCraft 0.11.1, two-finger scrolling on
the laptop trackpad has two problems:

1. Each swipe moves only a few rows, so moving through a sheet takes many
   swipes.
2. Scrolling stops immediately when I lift my fingers. There is no
   momentum/glide, which makes the short movement feel even worse.

Mouse pointer movement is normal. I have not tested a mouse wheel yet.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start GridCraft 0.11.1 in a Wayland session.
2. Open any workbook.
3. Two-finger scroll down, up, or sideways over the grid.

## Expected

One normal trackpad swipe should move a sensible number of rows, like it does
in other apps. Lifting the fingers should let the view glide briefly, as it
does in GTK/Qt apps.

## Actual

The sheet moves very little per swipe. Scrolling stops dead when the fingers
lift, so short swipes feel even shorter.

## Environment

- GridCraft 0.11.1
- Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`)
- Installed through the launcher (package type not recorded)
- Laptop trackpad (exact model not recorded)

## Analysis

### 1. Small scroll delta

GridCraft reads egui's `smooth_scroll_delta` at
`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` around line 612 and applies it directly around
line 643, divided only by the grid zoom. There is no touchpad-specific
multiplier and no scroll-speed setting.

egui's `line_scroll_speed` (default 40) only applies to
`MouseWheelUnit::Line`, which is what mouse wheels use. On Wayland, winit
reports touchpad scrolling as pixel deltas, which egui exposes as
`MouseWheelUnit::Point`. The 40-point setting therefore never reaches the
trackpad.

Upstream reports:

- emilk/egui#5342 - "Adjustable touchpad scroll speed" (open)
- emilk/egui#461 - "Scroll is too slow on Gnome/Wayland" (closed, but its

title: XLSX: accounting formats 42 and 44 are saved as bare built-in ids, so LibreOffice and non-US Excel show them differently
author: helenkwok
body:
**What happens:** the public [LCOH calculator](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7948769) (CC BY 4.0) declares accounting format 44 in `styles.xml` with its code, `_("$"* #,##0.00_);_("$"* \(#,##0.00\);_("$"* "-"??_);_(@_)`, and uses it on 11 cells. After `gridcraft-cli convert` (`main` b8771d51) the cells still point at id 44, but the `<numFmt numFmtId="44" …>` declaration is gone. Excel for Mac 16.114 (US) still shows `$ (0.14)`. LibreOffice 26.8 shows `- 0.14`: no currency, and the negative reads as a dash. The original file shows `$ (0.14)` in both.

**Cause:** `builtin_id` in `crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs` writes a code as a bare built-in id when it matches the en-US table, and already excludes 5–8 "because their meaning depends on the reader's locale". Accounting formats 42 and 44 contain `"$"` too, and readers resolve them by locale the same way, but they aren't excluded.

**Fix:** treat 42 and 44 like 5–8, so their code is written as a custom format (`matches!(i, 5..=8 | 42 | 44)`). A test can check that a workbook with a 44-formatted cell keeps the code in `<numFmts>` after a save.

**Why it matters beyond GridCraft:** this one only shows when the file leaves GridCraft. GridCraft and US Excel both display it correctly, so neither would catch it; LibreOffice, and Excel in a locale whose currency isn't `$`, show something else.

title: Web host mode: say whether gridcraft:save is a Save or a Save As
author: helenkwok
body:
In host mode (`?host=parent`), `gridcraft:save` is sent with `{ name, bytes }` for both Save and Save As ([`host.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/v0.11.1/apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs), v0.11.1 and current `main`). The parent can't tell whether to replace the file it handed over or keep a new one.

**What goes wrong.** A page that keeps saved files by id (the natural design: it opened the workbook with `gridcraft:open`, so a save should update that entry) can only guess from the name. A Save As to a new name looks like a rename, and a Save As that keeps the name is indistinguishable from Save, so the page either overwrites the original or never updates it. I hit this in a small page that embeds the four Craft web editors and stores files in IndexedDB; it now treats a changed name as Save As, which still gets the same-name case wrong.

**Suggestion.** Send what PdfCraft already sends in its host mode: `pdfcraft:save` carries `{ name, saveAs, bytes }` ([`main.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.13.0/apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs)). For GridCraft that means `saveAs: true` for Save As. It's additive, so existing parents keep working, and the same field name across the Craft web apps lets one embedding page handle them all. As far as I can see the `Services::download` hook doesn't know which command triggered it, so this needs that information passed down, not only a change in `host.rs`.

Export as PDF is split out to #2452, as the triage bot asked. Related: #1984 (`gridcraft:opened`), #1020 (save acknowledgement) and storytold/pdfcraft#422.

title: Formula language setting, independent of the interface language (e.g. Italian interface, English formulas)
author: carminezac
body:
## Proposal

Add a **Formula language** setting next to **View › Interface language**, so the language used to type and read formulas can differ from the interface language.

- **Formula language:** *Same as interface* (default) · *English* · *Italiano* · … (the languages that have a formula dialect)
- A command such as `app.formulaLanguage.set {"language": "en" | "same" | …}`, so the CLI, MCP and the control channel can set it too.
- Files, the API and XLSX keep canonical English formulas, as today. The setting only changes how formulas are typed and shown (formula bar, cell editor, Show Formulas, AutoComplete, Insert Function, dialogs with formula fields).

## Why

Today the formula language follows the interface language (Spanish now; Italian, German, Polish, French, Russian… in the open dialect PRs). That matches Excel, which offers no choice: with an Italian interface you must write `SOMMA`, not `SUM`.

Many users want the interface in their language but formulas in English:
- formulas copied from guides, forums, Stack Overflow and AI assistants are almost always English;
- teams with colleagues using English Excel share formulas in English;
- people who learned Excel in English know `VLOOKUP`, not `CERCA.VERT`.

LibreOffice Calc has this as **Tools › Options › Calc › Formula › Use English function names**. GridCraft can do better than Excel here at little cost, because the dialect work in #1522 already makes every formula language a data table, independent of the interface catalog.

## Open question: separators

Argument and decimal separators come with the dialect today. Excel takes them from the **regional format**, not from the language (that was #1398, now being split into smaller PRs). With *English* formulas and an Italian region:
1. `=SUM(A1;A2)` and `1,5` — separators follow the region, as in LibreOffice and as #1398 intended; or
2. `=SUM(A1,A2)` and `1.5` — choosing *English* also brings the en-US separators.

Option 1 is consistent with Excel's rule …

title: A new font derived from the theme body font loses `<scheme val="minor"/>`
author: Fubeo
body:
`write_styles` marks a font as following the theme's body font only when it is font 0:

```rust
// crates/xlsx/src/styles.rs
s.push_str(&font_xml(f, None, i == 0 && f.name == wb.theme.minor_font));
```

Any other font whose name is the theme's minor font is written without `<scheme val="minor"/>`. That happens to every font a formatting command derives from the default one (bold, a colour, a size), and to the fonts of a file that had the scheme on several of them. After a save those fonts stop following the theme's body font: changing the theme fonts in Excel then leaves them on the old typeface.

Proposal: keep the scheme on the model's `Font` when it is read (or derive it from the base font when a command creates a font), instead of deciding it from the index.

title: XLSX: a worksheet with more than about 500k cells is reported damaged since #2413
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- Regression from #2413: a worksheet with more than about 500,000 populated cells is reported damaged on open and cut off after a few thousand rows.
- Cause: the new per-part element cap also counts the cells of streamed rows, which never stay in memory.
- A fix with a regression test follows in a PR.

Since #2413 (`6fac430f`), opening a workbook whose worksheet part holds more than `MAX_XML_NODES` (1,000,000) XML elements stops after a few thousand rows:

```
sheet "VMS" is damaged (the file contains invalid XML: the part holds more than 1000000 elements); kept 6310 rows
```

The file is not damaged. It is a workbook from a generating library with one sheet of 12,274 rows by 103 columns, about 1.0 million populated cells, which is an ordinary size (Excel allows 1,048,576 rows). Each cell is a `c` element with a `v` child, so the part holds about 1.96 million elements, and the import gives up after 6,310 rows, which is where the count passes one million. Excel and the previous GridCraft build open it whole.

The cause is in `xml::parse_streaming` (`crates/xlsx/src/xml.rs`): `finish` counts every element it attaches to a parent, but a worksheet's cells are attached to their `row` while the row is still open, and the row is then handed to the callback and dropped. So the counter grows with every cell of the sheet although the tree never holds more than one row. The same applies to `sharedStrings.xml`, streamed by `si`: a table of about a million plain strings, or fewer rich-text ones, would be refused too.

Fix: count only elements that stay in the tree. When a split element is handed out, the count returns to its value when that element started, so a streamed part of any size passes while a part that keeps a million elements in its tree is still refused. PR to follow with a regression test (5,001 streamed rows of 100 cells pass; the same part kept whole is refused).

title: feat: support `Alt + Enter` shortcut for manual in-cell line breaks
author: NicChoo96
body:
### Summary
Add support for the industry-standard `Alt + Enter` (Windows/Linux/Web) and `Option + Return` (macOS) keyboard shortcuts to allow users to insert manual line breaks inside a cell while in edit mode.

### Current Behavior
Keystroke combinations inside an active cell do not capture manual line break commands. Users cannot break text into multiple lines within a single cell without typing the text in an external editor and pasting it back in.

### Expected Behavior
1. **Shortcut Capture:** Pressing `Alt + Enter` (or `Option + Return` on Mac) while editing a cell or the formula bar should insert a `\n` line break at the cursor position.
2. **Auto-Wrap Toggle:** Using this shortcut should automatically flag the cell's layout property to enable text wrapping so the multi-line layout renders immediately without cutting off text.

### Implementation Checklist Idea
- [ ] Intercept `Alt + Enter` / `Option + Return` events inside the active cell text input context.
- [ ] Inject a new line break token at the current cursor string index.
- [ ] Ensure the row height handles the text block expansion natively or toggles the text-wrap property.

### Context
This matches standard parity behavior seen across Excel, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice Calc, providing essential workflow continuity for manual layout control.

title: XLSX: cells with duplicate, out-of-order or wrong-row addresses are placed silently
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- The worksheet reader places every cell where its `r` attribute says, with no check that the address belongs to the enclosing `row`, follows the previous cell, or has not been used already.
- A later cell with a repeated address silently replaces an earlier one; an unaddressed cell after a stray address lands at an unrelated position. No import warning is produced in any of these cases.
- Excel never writes such rows and treats them as corruption to repair. Proposed: drop the offending cells with an import warning, keeping what was already read.

Observed on main (3099df93) with a one-sheet workbook whose first row is, in order: `A1`=1, `C1`=3, `B1`=2, `A1`=999, `D7`=7, then a cell without an `r` attribute holding 8, followed by a normal second row. Read with `read_xlsx`:

- A1 is 999: the later duplicate replaced the first value, silently.
- D7 is 7, although the cell sits in the row for row 1.
- The unaddressed cell landed in E1: the row's row number combined with the column after the stray `D7`.
- The report carries no warning about any of it.

Why this matters: the reader's one defence against malformed input in a row is the grid check (an address outside 1,048,576 × 16,384 is dropped and warned about). Everything inside the grid is trusted, so a damaged or badly generated file can quietly change values, move cells and shadow data, and the user sees a clean open. A file written by Excel has its cells in ascending column order with row numbers matching the enclosing row, so none of these shapes ever come from Excel; a generator that produces them is producing a file Excel itself would refuse to open without repair. GridCraft's rule for such input elsewhere is to drop it and say so, never to lose or alter data silently.

Proposed behaviour, in `read_row` (`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs`): a cell whose address names a different row than the enclosing `row`, or whose column is not after the previous cell's, is dropped and counted; the first value read …

title: Keyboard: Alt+numpad codes insert nothing in cells (Alt+0128 for € produces no character)
author: Hardt96
body:
## Summary

Typing a Windows Alt code on the numeric keypad inserts nothing in GridCraft. Holding Alt and
typing `0128` on the numpad, then releasing Alt, should insert `€` (U+20AC) into the active cell
like it does in Excel, but no character arrives at all. Every Alt code tried fails the same way
(`Alt+0128` → €, `Alt+0169` → ©, `Alt+236` → é). The numpad itself works normally: without Alt,
its digits enter values into cells correctly, so this is not #2243 (where numpad keys are ignored
entirely, reported on Linux).

## Steps to reproduce

On Windows, Num Lock on, numpad verified working:

1. Select any empty cell.
2. Hold Alt and type `0128` on the numeric keypad.
3. Release Alt.
4. Look at the cell and the formula bar.

Repeat with other codes, e.g. Alt+0169 (©) or Alt+236 (é).

## Expected behavior

The cell shows `€` when Alt is released, as in Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 and as in
standard Windows edit controls (Notepad, WordPad). Any legacy Alt+numpad decimal code produces
its character.

## Actual behavior

Nothing is inserted. The cell stays empty — not the € sign, and not even the stray digits
`0128`. The Alt+digit events seem to be consumed without the composed character ever reaching
the cell. Alt shortcuts themselves are handled (the key tips / Alt sequences work, cf. #1441),
so Alt-held key events do reach the app.

## Runtime or environment

- GridCraft version: 0.11.1
- OS: Windows
- Keyboard layout: standard layout with a working numeric keypad (digits enter values without Alt)

title: Save after an open that dropped or kept over-limit content should behave like Save As
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- When an open drops or alters content, or keeps content Excel would not accept, a plain Save writes that state over the original file; the only protection is the info-bar warning the user may not read.
- Proposed: a document flag set by lossy or over-limit opens that makes Save behave like Save As until the user chooses a name, the way Excel's repair dialog does.
- Scope: the engine's open and save commands and the UI's Save; the readers already produce the warnings that would set the flag.

Today the readers handle malformed or over-limit input by dropping it with an import warning (cells outside the grid, hyperlinks past a cap, damaged parts cut short) or, with #2532, by keeping content Excel would not accept (cell text longer than 32,767 characters) with a warning that Excel may refuse or repair the saved file. In both cases the warning reaches the user through `ReadReport::warnings` and the info bar, and nothing else happens: Save still writes the workbook as read over the file it came from. A user who opens a damaged file, does not notice the bar, and saves has replaced the original with GridCraft's reading of it. For dropped content that is a silent loss; for kept over-limit content it is a file Excel may not open.

Excel's own answer is the repair dialog: a file it had to repair opens with a report of what was removed, and saving it forces a new name so the original survives. GridCraft's equivalent would be a flag on the document, set when the open produced warnings of either kind, that makes the Save command behave like Save As until the user has chosen a path, and that the UI shows alongside the warning. The readers need no change: the warning kinds already exist, and the flag could be as coarse as "the open had warnings" to start, refined later if some warnings prove harmless.

Related: #2526 and #2527 (a sheet wrongly reported damaged and cut short, which this would also have protected against), #2531 (addresses placed silently, which produc…

author: iluebbe
body:
Excel starts the Text Import Wizard when a `.txt` file is opened, so the delimiter can be chosen. GridCraft splits a `.txt` at tabs only and offers no choice. The Data tab's **Get Data (Text/CSV)** button opens the same File › Open dialog. As a result, a `.txt` separated by `;`, `,`, `|` or any other character lands in one column.

A `.prn` (Excel's Formatted Text) is read like a `.csv`, with a detected delimiter. Commas inside its text therefore split the lines, and a German `1234,5` ends up as two cells. Saving as `.prn` is refused.

## Measured

`main` at 17b9f6ff, `gridcraft-cli` on Windows 11, against Excel for Microsoft 365 (de-DE UI). Excel was driven through `Workbooks.OpenText` (the wizard's settings), `Workbooks.Open` and `SaveAs`. Synthetic files, 5 rows × 4 columns, one per delimiter: `,` `;` tab, space, `|` `:` `=` `^` `~` `#` `/` `§` `¦` `•` `€`, U+001F, `||` and `#|#`.

| Case | Excel | GridCraft 17b9f6ff |
|---|---|---|
| Open a tab-separated `.txt` | wizard; Tab: 4 columns | 4 columns |
| Open a `.txt` with any of the other 17 delimiters | wizard; that delimiter as a check box or Other: 4 columns (`#\|#` with Other `#`: 7, as in Text to Columns) | 1 column; no way to choose |
| Open a `.prn` with the lines `plain     a,b       1234,5` and `r2        d2` | `Workbooks.Open`: each line stays in one cell | row 1 split at the commas: `plain     a` \| `b       1234` \| `5` (a number) |

Save as .xlsx, .csv, .tsv, .json or .html.` |

title: [macOS] ⌘Q exits immediately with unsaved changes without prompting to save
author: piyushgoel2808
body:
### Summary
On macOS, pressing **⌘Q** (or selecting Quit from the application menu) immediately terminates GridCraft and loses any unsaved changes in dirty workbooks.

In contrast, clicking the window close button (`X`) properly intercepts the close request, checks if any workbook is dirty, and prompts the user whether to save changes.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch GridCraft on macOS.
2. Create or open a workbook.
3. Make an edit in a cell so the workbook has unsaved modifications.
4. Press **⌘Q** on the keyboard (or choose Quit from the native application menu).
5. **Observed**: The application terminates immediately; unsaved changes are lost.
6. **Expected**: GridCraft should prompt the user to save changes (matching the close button behavior).

### Root Cause
`muda::PredefinedMenuItem::quit(None)` routes to `[NSApp terminate:]`, which causes `winit` to terminate the process directly, bypassing the viewport close request and unsaved changes confirmation dialog.

### Proposed Solution
Intercept Quit on macOS to send `egui::ViewportCommand::Close` (or route via guarded quit handler), allowing GridCraft's existing unsaved-changes check to prompt the user before exiting.

title: Keep cell images visible across scrolling and zoom changes by caching display-sized previews
author: ypple1-blip
body:
### Environment
GridCraft 0.12.1 on Windows; XLSX worksheet containing multiple high-resolution images placed in cells.

### Observed behavior
Some cell images are displayed normally, while others show only an image placeholder icon. After scrolling, switching worksheets, or changing zoom, the set of visible images can change: an image previously visible may become a placeholder, while another reappears.

### Reproduction scenario
1. Open an XLSX worksheet containing numerous high-resolution images in cells, displayed at relatively small cell sizes.
2. View several images together.
3. Scroll away and back, switch sheets and return, or change the zoom level.
4. Observe whether some images switch between rendered content and placeholder icons.

### Expected behavior
Images in visible cells should remain consistently displayed as the view changes.

### Suggested improvement
Please consider caching downscaled display previews rather than retaining every image at its full original resolution in the rendering cache. Size previews according to the cell's displayed dimensions, zoom level, and display density. Refresh or select a higher-resolution preview when zooming in, reuse suitable previews when possible, and prioritize visible cells within a bounded cache budget.

This may reduce cache pressure substantially when large source images are shown as small thumbnails. Cache pressure is a possible explanation to investigate, rather than a confirmed diagnosis of every instance. The original embedded images should remain unchanged for saving, exporting, and later enlargement.

title: CSV: use locale-aware rendering after #2263 to preserve custom-format literals
author: coderabbitai
body:
## Summary

After #2263 lands, switch semicolon CSV export to its locale-aware number-format renderer. Use `format_value_in` with `Locale { decimal, group }` configured for decimal commas and period grouping.

Requested by @carminezac.

## Rationale

The current exporter swaps every `.` and `,` in the final rendered text. This also changes punctuation in quoted custom-format literals. For example, the numeric value `12.34` with format `0.00"."` currently exports as `12,34,`, but must export as `12,34.`.

Reuse #2263's renderer instead of adding a second locale-rendering implementation. This follow-up keeps PR #2466 independent of #2263.

## Required changes

- In `crates/engine/src/io.rs`, replace the final rendered-text character swap in the decimal-comma CSV path with locale-aware rendering through `format_value_in`.
- Configure the locale with decimal `,` and group `.`.
- Convert only numeric decimal and grouping separators. Preserve quoted literals and all other displayed characters.
- Preserve the existing full-precision behavior for finite General numbers.
- Keep date/time output, default comma CSV behavior, delimiter selection, quoting, and UTF-8 BOM behavior unchanged.
- Add regression coverage in the engine CSV export tests (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs` or the CSV tests in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] #2263 has landed before this integration is implemented.
- [ ] Semicolon CSV uses `format_value_in` with a decimal-comma locale instead of swapping punctuation in final rendered text.
- [ ] A numeric cell containing `12.34` with custom format `0.00"."` exports the field `12,34.`.
- [ ] Regression coverage confirms quoted literal commas also remain unchanged.
- [ ] Existing General, fixed-decimal, grouping, percent, and currency export behavior remains correct.
- [ ] Date/time output and comma CSV behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Existing CSV delimiter, quoting, and BOM tests still pass.

title: Saving a file opened through a symlink replaces the symlink with a regular file (Linux)
author: StephLTG
body:
On Linux, when I open an .xlsx file through a symbolic link (e.g. a shortcut on the desktop pointing to the real file elsewhere) and save it, GridCraft replaces the symlink with a regular file instead of writing to the link’s target.

Steps to reproduce

ln -s /path/to/original/book.xlsx ~/Desktop/book.xlsx
Open ~/Desktop/book.xlsx in GridCraft
Edit a cell and save (Ctrl+S)

Expected: the original file /path/to/original/book.xlsx is updated and the symlink stays in place.

Actual: ~/Desktop/book.xlsx becomes a regular file containing the changes; the symlink is gone and the original file is left unchanged. This means users can silently end up editing a copy.

Likely cause: the atomic save (write to a temp file + rename) renames over the symlink path itself. Resolving the path first (e.g. std::fs::canonicalize) before writing the temp file next to the real target would fix it. This is how LibreOffice and most editors behave.

title: Web: host GridCraft in the page's own document (no iframe)
author: helenkwok
body:
The web app's host bridge (`?host=parent`, [`host.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/main/apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs)) only works inside an iframe: `Bridge::new()` returns `None` when the page isn't framed. A page that loads the wasm-bindgen module into its own document, with its own `<canvas id="gridcraft_canvas">` inside a component, can run GridCraft fine but has no way to hand it a workbook or receive its saves.

**Why it matters.** Embedding the editor as a component sized to a box, next to the page's own header and controls, is simpler than an iframe (one document, one style sheet, no cross-frame plumbing) and is how a React or plain-JS host usually wants it. I checked it with the v0.11.1 web build: the editor renders inside the box and keyboard focus stays separate from the page's own inputs; only the bridge is missing.

**Suggestion.** An opt-in page host mode with the same messages as `?host=parent`, carried as DOM `CustomEvent`s on the canvas instead of `postMessage`: `data-host="page"` on the canvas turns it on (the URL belongs to the host page, so a query flag doesn't fit), GridCraft dispatches `gridcraft:ready`, `gridcraft:save`, `gridcraft:dirty` and `gridcraft:failed` on the canvas with the message fields as `detail`, and the page dispatches `gridcraft:open` on the canvas. The events don't bubble, so nothing else on the page hears them. Unframed `?host=parent` keeps today's behaviour (the normal app with downloads), so no save can be posted to nobody.

I have a working implementation and would be glad to open a PR if this direction suits you. The same change is proposed for PdfCraft in storytold/pdfcraft#4731.

title: Cell text over 32,767 characters gets in through text files, cell.set and & and is saved to a .xlsx that Excel can't open
author: iluebbe
body:
**Summary**

- Text files, `cell.set` and the `&` operator can each put more than 32,767 characters into one cell.
- GridCraft saves such a cell to `.xlsx` without a warning, and Excel then can't open the file.
- Excel itself never lets a cell hold more than 32,767 characters.
- #2532 covers `.xlsx` files that already contain such text: the text is kept whole and a warning is shown. #2539 covers what Save should do after such an open. Neither covers the three ways listed here, which create the long text without any warning.

**Measured**

GridCraft at `main` f6b0cec6 (#2559 head 47e40a5f for the text-file row). Excel for Microsoft 365 16.0 build 20527 on Windows, German region.

| Way in | GridCraft | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| File › Open of a `.csv` with a 100,000-character field | one cell with 100,000 characters, no warning | splits the field over four rows (A2:A5), and the next field lands in B5 |
| `Workbooks.OpenText` of the same file | (same as above) | keeps the first 255 characters; the next field is dropped |
| `cell.set` / `Range.Value2` with 32,768 or 40,000 characters | keeps them all | cuts to 32,767 |
| `=REPT("x",20000)&REPT("x",20000)` | 40,000 characters | 32,767 characters, no error |

GridCraft's `CONCAT`, `TEXTJOIN`, `REPT` and `SUBSTITUTE` already return `#VALUE!` past the limit; only `&` lets the text through.

Opening the `.xlsx` that GridCraft saves (`Workbooks.Open`, alerts off):

| B2 length | Excel |
|---|---|
| 10 (control) | opens |
| 32,767 | opens, B2 has 32,767 characters |
| 32,768 | Open fails |
| 40,000 | Open fails |

**Steps**

```sh
# a 40,000-character field
{ printf 'id;text\r\n1;'; head -c 40000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x; printf '\r\n'; } > long.csv
gridcraft-cli convert long.csv long.xlsx
gridcraft-cli eval '=LEN(B2)' --in long.xlsx          # 40000

gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"B2","input":"=REPT(\"x\",20000)&REPT(\"x\",20000)"}' --out amp.xlsx
gridcraft-cli eval '=LEN(B2)' --in amp.xlsx           # 40000
```

title: Perf: lookups copy the whole key column or row on every call (VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, LOOKUP, MATCH, XLOOKUP, XMATCH)
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/functions` (checked against `main` at d8c5f588).

**Problem.** Every lookup call first copies its whole key column or row into a new `Vec<Value>`, and only then searches it. In `crates/functions/src/lookup.rs`: `vh_lookup` (VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP) calls `column()` / `row()`, `lookup` (LOOKUP) clones or copies, `match_fn` and `xmatch` call `vector()`, `xlookup` calls `vector()`. Each copy is O(rows) with one `Value` clone per cell, even when the answer is found in the first rows or by a binary search that touches about 17 entries of a 100,000-row range. So `VLOOKUP(x, table, 2, TRUE)`, `MATCH(x, range, 1)` and `XLOOKUP(..., 2)` (binary search) are linear per call instead of logarithmic, and a spilled lookup over many needles (`XLOOKUP(A2:A5000, ...)`) is quadratic.

**How measured.** A small probe through the public API (`gridcraft_functions::call`) with synthetic numbers, 100,000 rows, release build, pinned to one core with `taskset -c 3`, `perf stat -e instructions:u` (user instructions, setup subtracted; two runs agree to under 0.01%). Prototype of the fix below, results are identical:

| Call (100,000-row range) | Before (instructions) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2,000 x `VLOOKUP(500, A:B, 2, FALSE)` (hit in row 501) | 8.43 G | 0.040 G (210x) |
| 2,000 x `MATCH(70000, A:A, 1)` | 5.20 G | 0.0027 G (about 1,900x) |
| 2,000 x `XLOOKUP(70000, A:A, B:B, "nf", -1, 2)` (binary) | 5.20 G | 0.0028 G (about 1,800x) |
| 2,000 x `XLOOKUP(1500, A:A, B:B)` (hit in row 1001) | 5.26 G | 0.063 G (83x) |
| `VLOOKUP({5,000 needles}, 20,000-row table, 2, FALSE)` | 4.98 G | 0.98 G (5x; the rest is the scan itself) |

Wall time for the first row: 205 us per call down to about 1 us.

**Proposed fix.** Search a borrowed view instead of a copy: a small `Keys { data: &[Value], offset, stride, len }` (contiguous for a 1-D range and for a row, strided for the first column of a 2-D table), with `get(i)` and `iter()`. `find_exact`, `bsearch_last` and the `xsearch` he…

title: Perf: MEDIAN, PERCENTILE, QUARTILE, LARGE and SMALL fully sort the data to read one value
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/functions` (checked against `main` at d8c5f588).

**Problem.** MEDIAN, PERCENTILE(.INC/.EXC), QUARTILE(.INC/.EXC), LARGE and SMALL all call `sorted()` (`crates/functions/src/stat.rs`: `median`, `kth`, `percentile_inc`, `percentile_exc`), a full O(n log n) sort, to read one or two order statistics. A selection (`select_nth_unstable_by`) does the same job in O(n). The pattern `LARGE(range, SEQUENCE(300))` (a top-N list) repeats the full sort once per spilled cell.

**How measured.** Probe through the public API with synthetic numbers, release build, pinned with `taskset -c 3`, `perf stat -e instructions:u` (setup subtracted), plus wall time. Prototype of the fix below:

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `MEDIAN` of 1,000,000 numbers | 1.05 G instr, 33 ms | 0.18 G, 4 ms (about 6-8x) |
| `LARGE(1,000,000 numbers, 1)` | 19 ms | 2 ms (about 9x) |
| `LARGE(100,000 numbers, SEQUENCE(300))` | 9.0 G instr, 438 ms | 1.35 G, 66 ms (6.7x) |

PERCENTILE and QUARTILE sit in the same range as MEDIAN (the same sort dominates).

**Proposed fix.** `select_nth_unstable_by(idx, f64::total_cmp)` for the element at the needed index; for MEDIAN with an even count the lower middle is the maximum of the lower partition, and for PERCENTILE's interpolation the next order statistic is the minimum of the upper partition. The sort already uses `f64::total_cmp`, and a total order puts equal values at identical bit patterns, so the selected values equal the sorted ones bit for bit (including -0.0 before +0.0). The existing median and percentile tests pass on the prototype. PERCENTRANK and the other callers of `sorted()` that need the whole order stay as they are.

**Overlap.** #2657 touches `stat.rs` only in PERCENTRANK; `median`, `kth` and `percentile_*` are not in an open PR.

title: Perf: SUM, COUNT and AVERAGE over big ranges cost about 47 ns per cell, and every formula walks the same range again
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/calc` (upstream `main` at d8c5f588). Results are correct; only time is affected.

**Measured** (release build, one pinned core, 100% constants in column A; `recalc_all` or one edit that dirties every formula; two runs agree within 1%):

| Workbook | Cell visits | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 rows of `=A{r}/SUM(A$1:A$20000)` (percent of total) | 400 M | 19.0 s |
| 20,000 rows of `=SUM(A$1:A{r})` (running total) | 200 M | 9.4 s |
| 1,000 x `=SUM(A1:A50000)` | 50 M | 1.96 s |
| 1,000 x `=MAX(A1:A20000)` (range copied into a Vec first) | 20 M | 0.62 s |

That is 30 to 47 ns per cell, and the same editing cost on every edit that touches the column (editing one number in column A re-runs all of them).

**Where it goes.** `PassHost::visit_range` (`recalc.rs`) walks the range twice through `CellStore::iter_range` (once to calculate formula cells, once to fold), and `iter_range` opens a fresh `BTreeMap` range per row, so a one-column range pays a tree descent per cell. perf (instructions:u) puts 84% in `visit_range` and 13% in the flatten iterator.

**Proposed fix** (results bit-identical, same summation order):
1. Per pass, remember the (sum, count, first error) of a range whose cells are all constants (no formula, no spill), keyed by sheet and range. A second `SUM(A$1:A$20000)` in the same pass then costs a hash lookup. The percent-of-total case drops from 19 s to the cost of one walk (about 1 ms).
2. For a running total, extend the remembered result of the same-start range that is one or a few whole rows shorter instead of walking again: row-major left-to-right addition makes `sum(A1:A{r+1}) = sum(A1:A{r}) + A{r+1}` bit for bit. 9.4 s becomes linear (a few ms).
3. Walk once when the range holds no formula cell that is still pending (the first pass is only needed to calculate those).

Constant-only ranges cannot change inside a pass, so the memo needs no invalidation within a pass; it is dropped with the pass. Iterative calculation and ce…

title: Perf: any formula that uses a defined name or a table reference is recalculated on every edit, and a name's text is parsed again for every use
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/calc` (upstream `main` at d8c5f588). Results are correct; only time is affected.

**Cause.** `precedents()` in `eval.rs` sets `dynamic = true` for `Expr::Name` and `Expr::Struct`. `Calc::dirty_closure` adds every dynamic formula to the dirty set on every edit, whatever was edited. A name that points at `Sheet1!$H$1`, or `Table1[Price]`, has static precedents, so these formulas do not need to be "always dirty" (only OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile functions and names built from them do).

Second cost: `Evaluator::name` calls `parse_name` on the name's text on every use, so 100,000 uses parse 100,000 times.

**Measured** (release build, one pinned core). 100,000 rows of `=Rate*A{r}` where `Rate` is a defined name for `Sheet1!$H$1`, then a change to a cell nothing depends on:

| | Before |
|---|---|
| formulas recalculated by that edit | 100,000 (expected 0) |
| time of that edit | 105 ms |
| same, with a name whose body is `IF(Sheet1!$H$1>0,Sheet1!$H$1*1.19+Sheet1!$H$2,ROUND(Sheet1!$H$3,2))` | 259 ms, eval phase 230 ms vs 55 ms for a plain `=A*2` |

Expected after: edits that do not touch the name's cells recalculate nothing extra (about 0.1 ms), and the name text is parsed once per name per pass (eval phase of the second case back to about 70 ms).

**Proposed fix.**
1. In `precedents`, resolve a name to the precedents of its parsed body (nesting limited, cycles guarded), the same for a structured reference through the table's column range; stay `dynamic` if the body is dynamic (OFFSET, INDIRECT, volatile function, LAMBDA call, unknown name or table). Relative names stay dynamic or are resolved per cell offset.
2. Parse each name once per pass (cache by name and scope in the pass host) instead of per use.

Bit-identical results are checked by a test that compares incremental recalculation with a full recalculation after random edits of cells in, near and outside the names and tables, including renaming and redefining a name and resizing a …

title: Perf: with many dynamic-array results, every cell read and every range read scans all of them
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/calc` (upstream `main` at d8c5f588). Results are correct; only time is affected and it grows with (cells read) x (spill arrays).

**Cause** (`recalc.rs`, `PassHost`):
- `cell_value` loops over every spill computed so far in the pass for each plain constant cell it reads.
- `range_values` rebuilds a list of every cell of every spill array on the sheet for each range read (`self.spills.iter().flat_map(...)`), even when the range is far from all of them.
- `cells_changed` loops over all `spill_ranges` of the sheet for each changed cell (a paste of 20,000 cells with 2,000 spills on the sheet spends 54 ms there; with no spills the same loop costs nothing).

**Measured** (release build, one pinned core, `recalc_all`):

| Workbook | Time |
|---|---|
| 100,000 rows of `=A{r}*2` plus 5,000 `=SEQUENCE(5)` anchors (100,000 constant cells read) | 458 ms |
| same with 10,000 anchors and 200,000 rows | 1,612 ms (about 4x for 2x; the no-spill part is linear) |
| 20,000 rows of `=MAX(A{r}:B{r})`, no spills | eval 7.1 ms |
| same plus 2,000 `=SEQUENCE(50)` anchors (100,000 spilled cells) elsewhere on the sheet | eval 1,131 ms (160x) |

**Proposed fix** (identical results): index the pass's spill areas by sheet and rows (a map from covered cell to anchor, or an interval index by anchor row) so a cell lookup is O(1) and a range read only visits the spills that intersect it; in `cells_changed` look up the spills covering a changed cell through the same kind of index (or skip the loop when the sheet has no spill ranges). Expected: the 1,131 ms case back to about 10 ms, the 200,000-row case to about 300 ms.

**Overlap.** Open PRs #2483, #2490, #2308 and #1954 edit spill handling in `recalc.rs`, and #2319/#2122 the pass loop. I will keep the change to the lookup structure and rebase on whatever merges first.

title: Perf: clearing one cell scans every formula in the workbook, and each changed cell scans a 64x64 window
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/calc` (upstream `main` at d8c5f588). Results are correct; only time is affected.

**Cause.** In `Calc::cells_changed` (`recalc.rs`), when a changed cell is now empty, the "an emptied cell can unblock an anchor" step walks every key of `graph.nodes` and looks up each one's cached value (`sh.value(c) == #SPILL!`). The same loop runs in `run` for every area a formula stopped spilling over. In addition each changed cell scans a 64 x 64 window of stored cells for `#SPILL!` values, one tree descent per row.

**Measured** (release build, one pinned core): 100,000 formulas in column B, clearing one cell: 9.6 ms for that single clear, all of it the scan (nothing is recalculated). It grows linearly with formula count, so about 100 ms per Delete key press at a million formulas. Twenty thousand changed cells with no spills: 12 ms of window scanning on top of 10 ms of real recalc work.

**Proposed fix** (identical results): keep a small set of the cells whose value is `#SPILL!` (filled in write-back, and in `rebuild` the way `circ` is collected from cached `#CIRC!` values) and take the unblock candidates from that set; skip the 64 x 64 window and the loops entirely when the set and the sheet's `spill_ranges` are empty. Expected: 9.6 ms becomes under 0.1 ms; the window cost (about 0.6 us per changed cell) disappears for sheets without spills.

**Overlap.** Same region as #2483/#2490/#2340 (spill unblocking); the PR will keep their semantics and only change how candidates are found.

title: Perf: rebuilding the dependency graph deep-copies every formula's syntax tree
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a speed audit of `crates/calc` (upstream `main` at d8c5f588). Results are correct; only time is affected.

**Cause.** `Calc::rebuild` and `Calc::cells_changed` call `Formula::expr()`, which clones the whole `Expr` tree (`self.expr.as_deref().cloned()`), only to hand `&Expr` to `precedents`. `Formula::expr_arc()` returns the cached `Arc<Expr>` without copying (and `run` already uses it).

**Measured** (release build, one pinned core, 100,000 rows of `=IF(A{r}>B{r},A{r}*B{r}+ROUND(A{r}/3,2),MAX(A{r},B{r}))`, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, 20 rebuilds): 1.09 G instructions and 124 ms per rebuild. With `expr_arc()` in both places: 0.75 G (-31%) and 102 ms (-18%). `Expr::clone`, its drop and the `Vec<Expr>` clone were 19% of the profile. I tried the two-line change locally; the 90 `gridcraft-calc` tests pass (the graph is built from the same tree).

Every file open (`recalc_all` runs `rebuild`) and every undo/redo/structural edit pays this, so a million-formula workbook saves about 0.2 s per rebuild.

**Proposed fix.** Use `expr_arc()` in those two places; `precedents` already takes `&Expr`. It is small, so the PR can also pick up the remaining rebuild costs seen in the profile (a `HashSet` allocated per precedent cell in `Graph::cell_deps`).

title: refactor(cli): parse `gridcraft-cli` arguments with clap, following RFC-0012
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
Move `gridcraft-cli`'s argument parsing to [clap](https://docs.rs/clap) derive and [thiserror](https://docs.rs/thiserror), the way photocraft did, so it follows [RFC-0012: Command-line conventions](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18). Then every Craft CLI behaves the same: the same exit codes, help, errors, environment variables, completions and man pages.

## Reference

- **The rules:** [RFC-0012](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18).
- **The plan and decisions:** [photocraft#7071](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7071). It covers what was decided and why, such as rejecting repeated flags, `--version` with no `version` subcommand, and values that start with `-`.
- **The code:**
  - the port, merged as one PR: [photocraft#9167](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9167);
  - its review follow-up, typed usage errors: [photocraft#9194](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9194);
  - the ast-grep rules for the CLI code: [photocraft#9750](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9750), using craft-common-actions' [`ast-grep.yml`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/pull/80).
- **Files to read in photocraft:**
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/args.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/error.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs` (`run`)
  - `crates/automation/src/args.rs` (shared flags and environment variables)
  - `apps/photocraft/src/launch_args.rs` (the desktop app)
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/examples/man-and-completions.rs`
  - `lint/ast-grep/`

## Scope

- [ ] Parse every subcommand into clap derive types with typed values. Unknown or repeated flags, bad values and conflicting flags become usage errors (exit 2, on stderr) before any work starts.
- [ ] Use thiserror enums for errors, including the usage errors clap can't express itself. No `Result<_, String>` or `format!` messages.
- [ ] `main` passes `args_os()` to `run(args, out, err) -> exit code`, and the tests call `run` directly.

title: Web: workbook links open with window.opener intact (noopener passed as the window name)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

In the web app, the workbook-hyperlink opener means to open links with `noopener`, but the flag never takes effect. The opened page keeps `window.opener` and can navigate the GridCraft editor tab.

**Location:** `apps/gridcraft-web/src/web.rs:234`

```rust
let _ = w.open_with_url_and_target(&url, "_blank,noopener");
```

`web_sys::Window::open_with_url_and_target` is the 2-argument `window.open(url, target)`. So `"_blank,noopener"` becomes a literal window *name*, and no window features are passed. Unlike `<a target=_blank>`, `window.open` gets no implicit `noopener`. The sample `packaging/web/_headers` sets no `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`.

## Impact

The author of a workbook can attach a hyperlink to a page they control. If the user clicks it and confirms the Open Hyperlink dialog, that page can set `window.opener.location`. This replaces the editor tab with a look-alike page (reverse tabnabbing). Any unsaved workbook in that tab is lost without a prompt, and the referrer leaks the editor's origin.

Severity: low. It needs a click and a confirmation, and the attacker can't read the workbook.

## Reproduction

Reproduced in Chromium (Edge headless) on loopback with the exact JS call the binding makes:
- page A runs `window.open('http://127.0.0.1:8782/b.html', '_blank,noopener')`
- in page B, `window.opener` is non-null and `window.name === "_blank,noopener"`
- setting `opener.location` navigated A to another page

With `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`, the opener was `null` and nothing was navigated.

## Fix

```rust
let _ = w.open_with_url_and_target_and_features(&url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer");
```

PR to follow. As defence in depth, the sample `_headers` could also send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin-allow-popups` for standalone deployments.

title: Lifted lookups (XMATCH/MATCH/XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP over an array) have no total-work cap; a 1.6 KB workbook hangs on open
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

Lookups whose lookup value is an array (XMATCH, MATCH, XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, LOOKUP) do work proportional to needles × lookup vector, with no cap on the total. One small formula can keep recalculation busy for hours, and `file.open` recalculates synchronously.

**Location:** `crates/functions/src/lift.rs`, `call_lifted`. It checks only the output size (`rows * cols <= MAX_CELLS`), then calls the scalar lookup once per needle. Each call scans the whole lookup vector (`crates/functions/src/lookup.rs`, `find_exact`).

Every array is capped at `MAX_CELLS`, but their product isn't. Comparable code already caps total work: `MMULT` refuses past 2e9 work units (`crates/functions/src/math/matrix.rs:31`), and `LAMBDA_FUEL` exists "instead of squaring".

## Impact

A 1.6 KB `.xlsx` whose A1 holds

```
=ROWS(XMATCH(SEQUENCE(1048576),-SEQUENCE(1048576)))
```

hangs on open:
- `gridcraft-cli info` (killed after 120 s);
- the desktop app opened with the file (one core pinned, no window after 30 s);
- MCP or CLI pipelines that open it.

Measured cost on a release build of `main` (45f5ab18): about 8.4 ns per needle×entry, quadratic. That's about 2.6 h for this one cell and about a day for the `SEQUENCE(1000,10000)` needle form. The process has to be killed, which loses unsaved work in other documents open in the same session.

Severity: low, availability of the user's own process only. Opening the file is the only step needed.

Related: #2678 (each call copies the key vector). Fixing the copy reduces the constant factor, but an exact-match scan per needle stays quadratic, so the cap is still needed.

## Fix

Cap needles × lookup length for lifted lookups and return `#NUM!` past the cap, the same pattern as MMULT. PR to follow.

title: Control channel: pre-auth timeout is set on the wrong socket handle, and waiting connections are uncapped
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

With `--control`, a connection that hasn't sent the token is meant to be closed after 10 s (`AUTH_TIMEOUT`, `docs/control-protocol.md`). On Windows it never is. And there's still no cap on how many connections can be waiting to authenticate.

**Location:** `apps/gridcraft/src/control_server.rs`
- `serve` reads through `BufReader::new(stream.try_clone())`, but `authenticate` sets the timeout on `out`, the original stream (`out.set_read_timeout(Some(AUTH_TIMEOUT))`). On Windows the clone is a separate socket handle with its own timeout, so the auth read is unbounded.
- Even where the handles share a timeout (Unix), it's a per-read `SO_RCVTIMEO`. A peer sending one byte every few seconds resets it, up to `MAX_AUTH_LINE` reads.
- `serve_listener` spawns one thread per accepted connection with no cap. `incoming().flatten()` retries accept errors in a tight loop. The cap was recommended in #2174 but didn't land with #783.

## Impact

Any local process, including another OS user's, can open connections to the loopback port without the token. Each connection is held indefinitely and pins one thread and about 4 handles. It's resource accumulation that degrades the control channel and the app; there is no auth bypass.

Observed on a release build of `main` (45f5ab18) on Windows 11, with a dummy token:
- 200 silent connections: 200/200 still open after 11 s;
- a byte-at-a-time connection: still open at 58.7 s;
- threads/handles went from 19/583 to 219/1383, linear, with no cap;
- an authenticated client was still served.

Severity: low. `--control` is opt-in.

## Fix

- Set the timeout on the handle being read.
- Enforce one total deadline for the first line, shortening the timeout before each read.
- Cap concurrent pre-auth connections; close extra connections on accept.
- Back off on accept errors.

PR to follow.

title: Web host bridge: export and validate complete native JSON snapshots
author: Srbino
body:
The same-origin web host bridge can open native JSON workbooks, but its save callback always encodes XLSX. A host that stores the complete native document cannot request a native snapshot, validate a proposed snapshot through the engine, or preserve the local dirty state until durable storage acknowledges it.

Please expose a narrow, correlated native export request alongside the existing host open/save bridge. It should commit a pending cell edit before taking the snapshot, use the existing engine JSON encoder/decoder, return errors explicitly, and retain existing same-origin parent checks. This does not require collaboration or a new document model.

Reproducer: embed the v0.10.0 web release with ?host=parent, open a JSON workbook using gridcraft:open, edit a cell and use Save. gridcraft:save always contains a ZIP/XLSX payload; no inbound native-export request exists.
