title: Web host bridge: capability port transport for opaque sandboxed frames
author: Srbino
body:
A same-origin window bridge cannot serve a host that isolates its editor in an opaque iframe (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`, without `allow-same-origin`). Please add an opt-in capability MessagePort transport, preserving the existing window mode.

The public window channel should carry only a content-free protocol/bundle hello and a one-shot connect from the exact embedding parent and configured canonical parent origin, transferring exactly one port. Validate the pinned bundle on both handshake messages. All workbook bytes, state notifications and managed-save acknowledgements then travel only on that private port; ignore subsequent window messages. Native document messages should support complete ArrayBuffers up to 32 MiB rather than a small JSON-string envelope.

I am implementing this narrow transport on feat/host-capability-port, based on #2736 and #2737. A Chromium regression with a real opaque credentialless iframe starts the WASM editor but fails because no capability hello is emitted. Existing same-origin checks and legacy save behavior will remain unchanged.

title: Add opt-in native read-only host access without discarding drafts
author: Srbino
body:
A host that loses write access currently cannot put the native editor into a real viewing mode while preserving selection, scrolling, copy/find and unsaved cell/text-box buffers. Disabling the entire iframe also disables useful viewing.

Add an opt-in ephemeral read-only command guard and UI editing gate. A private capability-port host should boot read-only before any interactive frame, identify the access capability, and receive an acknowledgement only after a requested access state is actually applied. Native workbook protection and persisted data must remain unchanged. Legacy embedding keeps its current default behavior.

I am implementing this in `feat/host-read-only-access`, stacked on the native snapshot, managed ACK and capability-port work (#2736, #2737, #2744), with regressions first and actual opaque-frame browser verification.

title: Vietnamese alphabetical sorting is incorrect in v0.12.1
author: tanchanh
body:
# Vietnamese alphabetical sorting is incorrect in v0.12.1

## Summary

GridCraft v0.12.1 does not sort Vietnamese text according to Vietnamese alphabetical rules.

The problem is not limited to the letter **đ**. Vietnamese-specific letters and diacritics also appear to be affected, including:

- Vietnamese letters: **ă, â, đ, ê, ô, ơ, ư**
- Vietnamese tone marks: **acute (sắc), grave (huyền), hook above (hỏi), tilde (ngã), and dot below (nặng)**

The basic Latin letters, such as **d**, do not appear to be affected in the same way. The issue seems to occur when sorting requires proper handling of Vietnamese-specific letters and diacritics.

I tested the same type of data in Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, and ONLYOFFICE. These applications sort Vietnamese text correctly, whereas GridCraft produces an incorrect order.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open GridCraft v0.12.1.
2. Enter the following Vietnamese names into a single column, one name per row:

   ```text
   An
   Dung
   Khoa
   Kim
   Ăn
   Đang
   Ẩn
   ```

3. Sort the column in ascending alphabetical order.
4. Repeat the test using the `SORT` and `SORTBY` functions.
5. Compare the results with Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, or ONLYOFFICE using Vietnamese alphabetical sorting rules.

## Expected behavior

The names should be sorted according to Vietnamese alphabetical rules. The expected ascending order is:

```text
An
Ăn
Ẩn
Đang
Dung
Khoa
Kim
```

GridCraft should correctly handle the Vietnamese alphabet, including:

- **Ă** and **Â** as distinct letters following **A**
- **Đ** as a distinct letter following **D**
- Other Vietnamese vowel variants: **Ê, Ô, Ơ, Ư**
- Vietnamese tone marks when comparing words that otherwise contain the same letters

All sorting features should apply consistent Vietnamese locale-aware collation (`vi-VN`).

## Actual behavior

GridCraft v0.12.1 displays the following order when sorting the example names in ascending order:

```text
An
Dung
Khoa
Kim
Ăn
Đang
Ẩn
```

title: .xls open hangs: recalc_all spins in criteria::lookup_equal (UI never appears)
author: GaelDouay
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.12.1, macOS 26.7.1 and 26.6.2 (Apple silicon) — reproduced on two machines.

**What happens:** opening a real-world Excel 97-2003 `.xls` (BIFF8, 2.8 MB, 3 sheets of about 2,860 × 61, 2,871 × 59 and 7 × 17 cells, 327 XFs, 7 defined names) never shows the workbook. The window stays blank, the main thread sits at ~99–100 % CPU for 40+ seconds with flat memory (~55 MB), and the control channel's `ui.screenshot` times out. Waited over a minute on one run; it did not recover before I killed it.

**Where it spins** (`sample` of the main thread, 3 s):

```
gridcraft::main
 gridcraft_engine::cmd::file::open
  gridcraft_calc::recalc::Calc::recalc_all
   PassHost::calculate / compute
    Evaluator::eval → builtin → area_value
     Host::range_values → cell_value → compute → …
      gridcraft_functions::criteria::lookup_equal   ← most samples
       core::str::to_lowercase (char-by-char)
```

So it looks like the full recalc on open evaluates criteria functions (COUNTIF/MATCH-style equality over ranges) with no work budget, lowercasing every candidate string on every comparison. Not the same path as #2716 (lifted lookups over arrays): `lift` shows up in only one sample here.

**Expected:** open with cached values first (the file carries them) and recalc in the background or lazily, or cap the total work like other readers — at minimum, keep the UI responsive.

I can't share the file (client material), but I'm happy to run a build or a diagnostic command against it.

title: Wrapped text paints over the rows below when the row has a custom height (Excel clips it)
author: GaelDouay
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.12.1, macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon).

**What happens:** in a worksheet whose rows have an explicit height (`<row ht="57" customHeight="1">`) and cells with *Wrap text* on, a cell whose wrapped text needs more lines than the row height allows is drawn **past the bottom of its row**, over the cells of the rows below. Several rows in a column end up overlapping and unreadable.

**Expected (Excel):** with `customHeight="1"` the row keeps its height and the wrapped text is **clipped** to the cell; nothing paints over neighbouring rows.

**Repro shape:** `sheetFormatPr defaultRowHeight="16"`, rows 3–12 with `ht` between 47 and 101 and `customHeight="1"`, one column with 2–6 lines of wrapped text per cell, the next column narrower so its text needs more lines than the row height. Opening the file shows the text of each cell spilling into the next one or two rows.

This matters for translation workbooks (source / target columns side by side), where reviewers read long wrapped cells.

title: UI tests fail without CRAFT_FONTS_DIR: no glyph for ẞ and for Vietnamese ẻ
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Since egui 0.37 (#2543), kittest panics when it draws a character that no installed font has (`MissingGlyphPolicy::Panic`). Without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, the harness installs only egui's bundled faces, and `crates/ui-egui/tests/common/mod.rs` says the suite still passes then: the non-Latin language cases are skipped explicitly.

Two tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/interaction.rs` still draw characters the bundled faces lack. So `cargo test --workspace` fails on any checkout without the craft-fonts input:

| Test | Character | Panic |
|---|---|---|
| `column_autocomplete_folds_case_beyond_ascii` | `ẞ` (U+1E9E) in `STRAẞENBAHN` | `No glyph for "ẞ" (U+1E9E) in Name("cell")` |
| `language_switch_renders_the_ribbon_and_persists` | `ẻ` (U+1EBB) from the Vietnamese catalog (`i18n/vi.rs`) | `No glyph for "ẻ" (U+1EBB) in Name("ui")` |

Both panics list the same installed fonts: `Ubuntu-Light`, `egui-icons`, `NotoEmoji-Regular`, `emoji-icon-font` and `Hack`.

CI sets `craft-fonts-ref`, so CI passes. A local run without the fonts fails. The harness never uses the host's fonts, so this doesn't depend on the platform.

## Steps

1. Check out `main` at 45f5ab18 and leave `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` unset.
2. Run `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test it interaction::`.

## Expected

Both tests pass without the craft-fonts input, as the harness comment describes. Parts that need the fonts are skipped.

## Possible fix

- `language_switch_renders_the_ribbon_and_persists` leaves out Japanese, Korean and Chinese when craft-fonts aren't loaded. Vietnamese needs the same treatment. Alternatively, each catalog could be checked with `theme::craft_fonts_cover`.
- `column_autocomplete_folds_case_beyond_ascii` could run its `ẞ` case only when `theme::craft_fonts_loaded()`.

title: [Bug] UI lag after changing the row height for the entire worksheet
author: techunreal
body:
I'm using GridCraft 0.12.1 on Windows 11 and noticed some lag when scrolling, selecting cells, or moving the application window.

After a few tests, I managed to narrow down what's causing it.

### How to reproduce

1. Open a new, empty spreadsheet.
2. Click the top-left corner to select all cells.
3. Right-click the row 1 header and set the row height to 40.
4. Try scrolling or selecting different cells.

The interface becomes noticeably sluggish. If I undo the row height change, everything goes back to normal.

I also tried changing the height of just one row, then the first 1,000 rows, and finally the first 10,000 rows. None of these caused any lag.

Interestingly, changing the width of all columns to 20 works fine too. The problem only appeared when I changed the row height for the entire worksheet.

I initially thought it might be related to my GPU, but I tested both DirectX 12 and Vulkan, and the lag happens with both. GridCraft is running on my NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti.

I'm not sure what's happening internally, but it seems like changing the height of all rows at once causes some kind of performance issue.

Hopefully this helps narrow it down!

title: XLSX: new charts are saved with chart style 1, which Excel draws in grey
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

A chart inserted in GridCraft is blue in GridCraft but grey when the file is opened in Excel. A public review showed this: [GridCraft vs Excel, at 5:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=agfhH-wU-Bo&t=356).

The cause is the chart style number:
- `insert.chart` gives every new chart `style: 1` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert/chart.rs:261`).
- The writer saves that number as `<c:style val="1"/>` (`crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs:746`), and Excel draws chart style 1 in grey.
- GridCraft's renderer doesn't use the number, so GridCraft shows the chart in blue.

The reader already treats a missing `c:style` as 2 (`crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs:272`).

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0, build 20527) on Windows 11 opened the file through `Workbooks.Open`. The file is a column chart of four values, written by GridCraft 0.12.1. The two other rows are the same file with only `c:style` changed:

| `c:style` in `chart1.xml` | Excel's `Chart.ChartStyle` | Series fill |
|---|---|---|
| `1`, as GridCraft writes it | 1 | `#616161` (grey) |
| `2` | 2 | `#156082` (blue) |
| none | 2 | `#156082` (blue) |

## Steps

1. Run:
   ```
   gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1","values":[["Month","Spend"],["Jan",420],["Feb",380],["Mar",510],["Apr",465]]}' --cmd 'selection.set={"range":"A1:B5"}' --cmd 'insert.chart={"type":"column"}' --out chart.xlsx
   ```
2. Open `chart.xlsx` in Excel.

## Expected

The chart keeps its colours in Excel.

## Possible fix

- New charts get style 2, the value the reader assumes when the file has none. Alternatively, the writer leaves `c:style` out for a chart whose style was never chosen.
- `chart.set` accepts `style` (clamped to 1–16) and the writer saves it unchanged, so any chosen number becomes Excel's style of that number. Keeping a style read from a file is fine. A number picked in GridCraft needs to mean the same as in Excel, or be mapped before it's written.

title: PivotTable: with the active cell outside the data, use the sheet's only data block instead of "The reference isn't valid"
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

`insert.pivotTable` takes its source from the current region of the active cell. When the active cell is outside the data, Insert › PivotTable fails with:

> The reference isn't valid. Select a cell in a range with labeled columns, or pass `source`.

A public review ran into this. GridCraft needed a click into the data first, while Excel for the web filled in the range by itself: [GridCraft vs Excel, at 3:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=agfhH-wU-Bo&t=183).

## Measured

GridCraft 0.12.1 with 500 synthetic orders in `A1:F501` (Order, Region, Product, Units, Price, Revenue), using `insert.pivotTable {"rows":["Region"],"values":["Revenue"]}`:

| Active cell | Result |
|---|---|
| `A1` or `A2` | Source `sales!$A$1:$F$501`. Every region total matches `SUMIF`. |
| `J5` or `H1` | "The reference isn't valid." |
| `G1`, next to the data | "The PivotTable field name is not valid." The region takes in the empty column G. |

## Proposal

When the active cell's current region is empty and the sheet holds exactly one block of data with labeled columns, use that block as the source. If the sheet has no block or several, keep the error, which already says to pass `source`.

This goes beyond the current-region rule. It would apply alike to Insert › PivotTable and to `insert.pivotTable` without `source`.

title: CSV and text open: detect the date order per column, so 03/04/2026 next to 31/05/2026 is 3 April
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Opening a CSV reads dates with slashes month first, whatever the file holds and whatever the system region is. A file that writes dates day first, as the UK and most of Europe do, gets wrong dates without any notice. Day-first dates past the 12th of a month stay text in the same column.

A public review hit the same case on a US-format PC: [GridCraft vs Excel, at 4:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=agfhH-wU-Bo&t=256).

`customers.csv` (synthetic data, UTF-8, `,`-separated):

```
CustomerID,Name,City,SignupDate,RenewalDate,CardNumber,Balance
00123,Zoë Ångström,Malmö,03/04/2026,25/12/2026,4111111111111111,1234.50
00456,José Núñez,São Paulo,12/01/2026,01/02/2027,5500005555555559,99.90
00789,Françoise Lefèvre,Besançon,31/05/2026,30/11/2026,4012888888881881,0.00
01000,Jürgen Weiß,Köln,07/08/2026,13/09/2026,3530111333300000,-15.25
```

Windows 11 with German region settings, GridCraft 0.12.1. `main` at 45f5ab18 with #2559 gives the same:

| Cell | In the file | Read as |
|---|---|---|
| D2 | `03/04/2026` | 4 March 2026 |
| D3 | `12/01/2026` | 1 December 2026 |
| D4 | `31/05/2026` | text |
| E2 | `25/12/2026` | text |
| E3 | `01/02/2027` | 2 January 2027 |

So one column holds a mix of wrong dates and text, and nothing reports it.

## Proposal

#2559 chooses the decimal separator per column from values that read only one way. The date order could be chosen the same way:
- If a value in the column reads only day first (`31/05/2026`, `25/12/2026`), the column is day first. Its other values (`03/04/2026`) are then read day first too.
- If a value reads only month first (`12/31/2026`), the column is month first.
- If every value is ambiguous, keep today's rule. The open's warnings and the text report then say the order was guessed, as #2559 does for ambiguous numbers.
- If a column holds both kinds, it stays text.

The same applies to dates written with `-` and to two-digit years.

## Related

- #889, #361 and #2255: region settings for typing and coercion.
- #50…

title: XLSX open: a formula that calls a function GridCraft can't calculate loses the result saved in the file
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

GridCraft recalculates every formula when it opens a workbook. Some formulas call a function GridCraft doesn't have, or has only as a stub. Those get `#NAME?` or `#VALUE!` instead of the result saved in the file, and every formula that depends on them follows. Saving then writes the errors into the file as the saved results.

This affects the functions `docs/function-parity.md` lists as missing or stubbed:

| Result in GridCraft | Functions |
|---|---|
| `#NAME?` (missing) | GETPIVOTDATA, IMAGE, STOCKHISTORY, FIELDVALUE, RTD, TRANSLATE, DETECTLANGUAGE, COPILOT, PY |
| `#VALUE!` (stub) | FILTERXML, WEBSERVICE |
| `#N/A` (stub) | the seven CUBE functions |

A report built on GETPIVOTDATA or STOCKHISTORY opens as a sheet of errors, although the file holds every result.

## Measured

`unsupported.xlsx` was written by hand with saved results. The same happens on GridCraft 0.12.1 and on `main` at 45f5ab18:

| Cell | Formula in the file | Saved result | GridCraft shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `GETPIVOTDATA("Sum of Revenue",$A$1)` | 958237.75 | `#NAME?` |
| D2 | `_xlfn.FILTERXML("<r><v>7</v><v>9</v></r>","//v[2]")` | 9 | `#VALUE!` |
| D3 | `_xlfn.WEBSERVICE("https://example.com/rate")` | `"1.0825"` | `#VALUE!` |
| D4 | `_xlfn.STOCKHISTORY("MSFT",46023,46023,0,0,1)` | 512.5 | `#NAME?` |
| D5 | `_xlfn.IMAGE("https://example.com/logo.png","Logo")` | `#VALUE!` | `#NAME?` |
| D6 | `D1*2` | 1916475.5 | `#NAME?` |

- `gridcraft-cli check unsupported.xlsx` reports all six as mismatches.
- After `gridcraft-cli run --in unsupported.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A2","input":"5"}' --out saved.xlsx`, the file holds `<v>#NAME?</v>` and `<v>#VALUE!</v>` for these cells.

Excel 16.0 (build 20527) recalculates on open. A GridCraft-saved file with D2 as above and `=D2*2` showed 9 and 18 right after `Workbooks.Open`. Other readers of the saved results get the errors, such as viewers, scripts and other spreadsheet apps.

## Expected

The workbook shows what the file holds until …

title: FILTERXML is a #VALUE! stub; it needs no network and can be implemented on its own
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

FILTERXML gives `#VALUE!` for every input, because it is a stub (`docs/function-parity.md`). It only reads the XML text it is given, so unlike WEBSERVICE it needs no network.

Its only implementation is in #1203. That PR also adds Power Query, data connectors and WEBSERVICE, and it conflicts with `main`.

## Excel's behaviour (measured)

The measurements below come from Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527) on Windows 11, with German region settings (decimal separator `,`). Each formula was entered with `Range.Formula2` in a new workbook:

| Formula | Excel |
|---|---|
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>7</v><v>9</v></r>","//v")` | `{7;9}`, spilled down a column |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>7</v><v>9</v></r>","//v[2]")` | 9 |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>abc</v></r>","//v")` | `abc` (text) |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v a='5'/></r>","//v/@a")` | 5 |
| `=FILTERXML("<r xmlns='urn:x'><v>1</v></r>","//v")` | 1: the default namespace doesn't stop the match |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v> 3 </v></r>","//v")` | 3 |
| `=FILTERXML("<r>&lt;</r>","/r")` | `<` |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>TRUE</v></r>","//v")` | `TRUE` as text |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>1.5</v></r>","//v")` | 46143, the date 1 May 2026: read like input typed in the German region |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>1,5</v></r>","//v")` | 1.5 |
| `=FILTERXML("<r><v>2026-01-02</v></r>","//v")` | 46024, a date |
| no match (`//w`), an empty element, invalid XML, `""` as the XML or as the XPath | `#VALUE!` |
| `count(//v)`, `//v/text()` | `#VALUE!` |
| `//v` on `<v><w>1</w><w>2</w></v>`, an element with child elements | `#VALUE!` |

## Proposal

- Implement FILTERXML in `crates/functions` with an XML reader and the XPath subset these cases need: paths, `//`, attributes, and the predicates `[n]` and `[@a='x']`.
- Convert each result the way GridCraft converts typed input. Excel uses its region's rules, so a German Excel reads `1.5` as a date.
- Leave WEBSERVICE out. It fetches over the network and needs its own privacy decision.

title: XLSX save drops _xlfn. from STOCKHISTORY, TRANSLATE, DETECTLANGUAGE and COPILOT, so Excel no longer recognises them
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

A formula calling STOCKHISTORY, TRANSLATE, DETECTLANGUAGE or COPILOT loses the `_xlfn.` prefix when GridCraft saves the file. Excel then reads the call as an unknown name, so the formula is broken in Excel as well, even after a recalculation. The file Excel saved worked.

The writer adds `_xlfn.` only for the names in `FUTURE_FUNCTIONS` (`crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs:114`), and these four are missing from that list. GridCraft doesn't implement them, but it keeps their formulas. FIELDVALUE, IMAGE and FILTERXML, which GridCraft doesn't calculate either, are on the list and keep their prefix.

## Measured

`prefix.xlsx` was written by hand with each call spelled `_xlfn.NAME(…)`. It was opened and saved with GridCraft 0.12.1 (`gridcraft-cli run --in prefix.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"B1","input":"1"}' --out prefix_saved.xlsx`).

Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527, German) opened both files with calculation set to manual, so nothing was recalculated. A function Excel recognises shows its German name in `FormulaLocal`:

| Formula in `prefix.xlsx` | Saved by GridCraft as | Excel's `FormulaLocal`, original file | Excel's `FormulaLocal`, after the GridCraft save |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_xlfn.STOCKHISTORY("MSFT",46023)` | `STOCKHISTORY(…)` | `=BÖRSENHISTORIE("MSFT";46023)` | `=STOCKHISTORY("MSFT";46023)`, not recognised |
| `_xlfn.TRANSLATE("Hallo","de","en")` | `TRANSLATE(…)` | `=ÜBERSETZEN(…)` | `=TRANSLATE(…)`, not recognised |
| `_xlfn.DETECTLANGUAGE("Hallo")` | `DETECTLANGUAGE(…)` | `=SPRACHEERKENNEN(…)` | `=DETECTLANGUAGE(…)`, not recognised |
| `_xlfn.COPILOT("x")` | `COPILOT(…)` | `=_xlfn.COPILOT("x")`: this Excel build has no COPILOT | `=COPILOT("x")` |
| `_xlfn.FIELDVALUE(A1,"Population")` | `_xlfn.FIELDVALUE(…)` | `=FELDWERT(…)` | `=FELDWERT(…)` |
| `_xlfn.IMAGE(…)`, `_xlfn.FILTERXML(…)` | prefix kept | `=BILD(…)`, `=XMLFILTERN(…)` | the same |

## Expected

A formula GridCraft doesn't change is saved the way it was read, so Excel still recognises …

title: ECMA.CEILING is missing (#NAME?); Excel calculates it like CEILING
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

`=ECMA.CEILING(1.5,1)` gives `#NAME?` in GridCraft (0.12.1, and `main` at 11bb6738), while Excel calculates it.

`docs/function-parity.md` counts Excel's functions from Microsoft's alphabetical function list. ECMA.CEILING isn't on that list, so the parity table doesn't show this gap.

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527) on Windows 11, in a new workbook. Excel's ECMA.CEILING gives the same result as GridCraft's CEILING in every case:

| Arguments | Excel `ECMA.CEILING` | GridCraft `CEILING` | GridCraft `ECMA.CEILING` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1.5,1` | 2 | 2 | #NAME? |
| `-1.5,1` | -1 | -1 | #NAME? |
| `1.5,-1` | #NUM! | #NUM! | #NAME? |
| `-1.5,-1` | -2 | -2 | #NAME? |
| `2.5,2` | 4 | 4 | #NAME? |
| `-2.5,2` | -2 | -2 | #NAME? |
| `-2.5,-2` | -4 | -4 | #NAME? |
| `2.5,0` | 0 | 0 | #NAME? |
| `0,1` | 0 | 0 | #NAME? |
| `1.234,0.1` | 1.3 | 1.3 | #NAME? |
| `TRUE,1` | 1 | 1 | #NAME? |
| `1.5,"x"` | #VALUE! | #VALUE! | #NAME? |
| `1/0,1` | #DIV/0! | #DIV/0! | #NAME? |

For comparison, Excel's `CEILING.PRECISE(-2.5,-2)` and `ISO.CEILING(-2.5,-2)` give -2.

Excel also reads `ECMA.CEILING(…)` from a file without a prefix: a file saved by GridCraft shows it as `=ECMA.OBERGRENZE(1,5;1)` in a German Excel. So it doesn't need an entry in `FUTURE_FUNCTIONS`.

## Proposal

Add ECMA.CEILING to `crates/functions` as CEILING under a second name. List it as a Compatibility function, and add it to the Excel count in `docs/function-parity.md`.

title: FIELDVALUE and RTD give #NAME?; Excel gives #FIELD! without a data type and #N/A without an RTD server
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

GridCraft has neither FIELDVALUE nor RTD, so both give `#NAME?`. Excel gives `#FIELD!` for FIELDVALUE on a cell without a linked data type, and `#N/A` for RTD when no RTD server answers.

GridCraft doesn't have the `#FIELD!` error value at all: `docs/function-parity.md` lists it as missing.

The CUBE functions already match Excel here. They are stubs that give `#N/A`, which is also what Excel gives without a connection.

## Measured

Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527) on Windows 11, in a new workbook with no data types and no connections. A1 holds the text `Germany`, A2 holds 5 and B9 is empty:

| Formula | Excel | GridCraft 0.12.1 / `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `=FIELDVALUE(A1,"Population")` | #FIELD! | #NAME? |
| `=FIELDVALUE(A2,"Population")` | #FIELD! | #NAME? |
| `=FIELDVALUE(A1,"")` | #FIELD! | #NAME? |
| `=FIELDVALUE(B9,"x")` | #FIELD! | #NAME? |
| `=RTD("GridCraft.NoSuchServer",,"x")` | #N/A | #NAME? |
| `=RTD("",,"x")` | #N/A | #NAME? |
| `=CUBEVALUE("NoSuchConnection","[Measures].[x]")` and the other six CUBE functions | #N/A | #N/A |

## Proposal

- Add the `#FIELD!` error value. It needs to parse, display, compare and propagate like the other errors, and to work with `ERROR.TYPE`, `ISERROR` and `IFERROR`.
- FIELDVALUE returns `#FIELD!` for any cell without a data type. Until linked data types exist (#1957), that is every cell.
- RTD returns `#N/A` as a stub, like the CUBE functions. `docs/function-parity.md` already says GridCraft won't run COM servers.
- The formulas then read the same way they do in Excel. With #2770, the results a file saved for them would also stay.

title: commands --json: add a per-command `mutates` field
author: SANKKACHI
body:
## Problem

`gridcraft-cli commands --json` lists each command's `id`, `label`, `menu`, `shortcut`, and `params` (the parameters each command accepts), but it does not say whether a command changes the workbook. Automation tools that need this, for example to avoid running an edit by mistake, currently have to read the GridCraft source code and guess from how each command is written. That guess breaks when the way commands are defined in the source changes.

## Proposed behavior

Add a boolean field `mutates` to each entry in the `commands --json` output.

- `true` if running the command changes, or can change, the workbook: its cell contents, formulas, sheets (adding, deleting, or renaming a sheet; switching the active sheet does not count), formatting, tables, or charts, or if it writes a file to disk. The value describes what the command can do, not what one particular run happened to change. Example: `file.save`, which writes the workbook to a file.
- `false` if the command only reads the workbook or changes screen state, such as zoom, frozen panes, the selection cursor, or the active sheet. Example: `selection.move`, which moves the cell cursor; cell contents do not change.

This cannot be derived from the engine's existing internal flags, which are about undo and not about changes (see the pointers below). The GridCraft maintainers should decide the final name and definition.

## Pointers for maintainers (v0.12.1 tag)

- Output line: `apps/gridcraft-cli/src/main.rs:472`.
- Field type: `CommandInfo` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:51-60`).
- Value: `CommandSpec::info()` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:63-74`).
- The engine has two internal flags, `journal` (whether a command is recorded in the undo journal) and `undoable` (the undo policy), at `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:46-47`. They do not reliably indicate changes: `file.save` writes a file but is not undoable, and `selection.move` is journaled but changes no data. So they cannot stand in for `mutates`.

title: XLSX: a text box linked to a cell opens empty and loses its link and text on save
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

In Excel, a text box or shape can show a cell's value: select it and type `=$A$1` in the formula bar. The file stores the link as `textlink="$A$1"` on `xdr:sp`, and the current text in a field, `<a:fld type="TxLink">`.

GridCraft reads neither, so such a text box loses its content:
- It opens empty, because the reader takes text only from runs (`a:r`), not from fields ([drawing.rs#L225-L230](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/xlsx/src/drawing.rs#L225-L230)).
- The link is dropped, because the writer always writes `textlink=""` ([drawing.rs#L390](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/xlsx/src/drawing.rs#L390)).

Saving then writes an empty text box, so the link and the text are gone for Excel too.

GridCraft also can't create such a link: `insert.textBox` and `shape.setText` take only literal text.

## Measured

`textlink.xlsx` was written by hand: A1 = `hello`, and a text box over C3:F8 with `textlink="$A$1"` and the field text `hello`. It was saved with `gridcraft-cli run --in textlink.xlsx --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A2","input":"x"}' --out saved.xlsx`.

The two files were then opened in Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527) on Windows 11, through COM, reading `Shape.DrawingObject.Formula` and `Shape.TextFrame2.TextRange.Text`:

| File | Link | Text | After A1 = `changed` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `textlink.xlsx` | `$A$1` | `hello` | `changed` |
| `saved.xlsx` (GridCraft 0.12.1 and `main` at 45f5ab18) | none | empty | empty |

In `saved.xlsx` the shape is `<xdr:sp macro="" textlink="">` with no `xdr:txBody`. It is also renamed from `TextBox 1` to `Shape 1`.

## Expected

- An opened text box shows its text and keeps its link.
- The text follows the linked cell as the cell changes, as in Excel.
- Saving writes `textlink` and a `TxLink` field holding the current text, so other readers see it too.
- A link can be set: `=A1` typed in the formula bar…

title: Data validation: list sources that are formulas (OFFSET, INDIRECT, A1#) are read as typed lists
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

A list rule's source can be a formula that returns a reference:
- `=OFFSET($A$1,0,0,COUNTA($A:$A))` for a list that grows with its data;
- `=INDIRECT(B1)` for dependent dropdowns;
- `=$A$1#` for a spilled range.

GridCraft treats all of these as typed lists. `is_literal_list` counts every source that isn't a plain reference or a name, and has no `!` in it, as a literal list ([validation.rs#L127-L131](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/cmd/data/validation.rs#L127-L131)). `list_items` then splits the formula text at commas ([validation.rs#L146-L162](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/cmd/data/validation.rs#L146-L162)):
- `OFFSET($A$1,0,0,3)` gives the entries `OFFSET($A$1`, `0`, `0` and `3)`.
- `$A$1#` gives the single entry `$A$1#`.

Validation accepts these entries and refuses the real values. The in-cell dropdown takes its entries from the same function ([editor.rs#L128](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/ui-egui/src/grid/editor.rs#L128)).

Rules read from a file are affected the same way. Excel stores the source without `=` and quotes literal lists, so `<formula1>OFFSET($A$1,0,0,3)</formula1>` and `<formula1>INDIRECT("A1:A3")</formula1>` are formulas.

## Measured

Setup: A1 = `=SEQUENCE(3)`, which spills 1, 2, 3 into A1:A3, and B1:B2 = `x`, `y`. A list rule is put on one cell, then a value is entered there.

- GridCraft 0.12.1 and `main` at 45f5ab18: `data.validation`, then `data.validate`. A hand-written file with the OFFSET and INDIRECT sources above gives the same results.
- Excel for Microsoft 365 (16.0 build 20527), Windows 11, German region settings, through COM: `Validation.Add` (list), then `Validation.Value` after entering the value. `Validation.Add` takes the formula in the interface language, so the sources used `BEREICH.VERSCHIEBEN` and `INDIREKT`.

title: Custom Lists can't be defined, so AutoFill and Sort only know the built-in lists
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Excel's Custom Lists (File › Options › Advanced › Edit Custom Lists) hold the user's own series, such as `Low, Medium, High`, a list of branches or the fiscal months. AutoFill continues them, and Sort can order by them (Order › Custom List).

GridCraft has parts of this, but no way to define a list:
- AutoFill reads `Workbook::custom_lists` ([workbook.rs#L159-L160](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/model/src/workbook.rs#L159-L160), [fill.rs#L90](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/fill.rs#L90)), but nothing outside tests ever fills it. Only the built-in lists work: weekdays, months and `Q1`–`Q4` ([fill.rs#L63-L64](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/fill.rs#L63-L64)).
- `data.sort` takes a list per key as `customList` ([sort.rs#L64](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/cmd/data/sort.rs#L64)), but the Sort dialog has no Custom List order, and there are no saved lists to pick from.
- There is no command, option page or dialog to add, edit, import or delete a list.

## Excel

- The Custom Lists dialog shows the built-in lists, which can't be changed, and the user's own lists. A new list is typed one entry per line, or imported from a selected range.
- The lists belong to the application, not to a workbook, so every workbook can use them.
- AutoFill continues a list from any of its entries. Sort › Order › Custom List sorts by one, and PivotTables use them when sorting (PivotTable Options › Totals & Filters › Use Custom Lists when sorting).

## Proposal

- Commands to list, add, replace and delete custom lists, and to import one from a range, plus a dialog under File › Options › Advanced.
- Save the lists with the preferences (`Prefs`), so every workbook sees them, and fill `Workbook::custom_lists` from th…

title: Linked Picture (Paste › Linked Picture, Camera) is missing
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Excel can paste a range as a linked picture: Home › Paste › Linked Picture, or the Camera command. The picture shows the range as it looks on its sheet, with values, formats, borders and column widths, and it updates whenever the range changes. When the picture is selected, the formula bar shows its source (`=$A$1:$C$5`), which can be edited to point elsewhere. Dashboards use it to show ranges from several sheets side by side, scaled freely.

GridCraft has no such picture:
- Paste and Paste Special have no Linked Picture.
- There is no Camera command.
- `insert.picture` only takes image data.

## Proposal

- A picture whose source is a range reference. It is drawn with the grid renderer from that range and redrawn when the range changes.
- The reference follows sheet renames and inserted or deleted rows and columns, like any other reference.
- Commands: Paste › Linked Picture, and Camera (a picture of the selected range, placed with the next click). `insert.picture` could also take a `source` range.
- Selecting the picture shows its source in the formula bar, where it can be changed.
- XLSX: read and write linked pictures so they round-trip with Excel, with a snapshot image for readers that don't update them. How Excel stores them still needs to be observed.

title: R1C1 reference style option is missing
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Excel can show and take formulas in R1C1 notation (File › Options › Formulas › R1C1 reference style). With the option on:
- column headers are numbers;
- the Name Box shows `R2C3`;
- the formula bar shows `=R[-1]C+1`;
- typed formulas are read as R1C1.

GridCraft has some of the pieces, but not the option:
- `print_r1c1` prints a formula in R1C1 ([printer.rs#L226](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/formula/src/printer.rs#L226)), but only tests call it.
- `Prefs::r1c1` ([lib.rs#L364](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L364)) is saved with the preferences, but nothing reads it, and no command or option sets it.
- Typed R1C1 isn't read. `cell.set` with `=R[-1]C+1` fails with "There's a problem with this formula: unexpected Word("C")". Only INDIRECT's R1C1 mode converts R1C1 text (`r1c1_to_a1` in `crates/calc/src/eval/format.rs`).
- The file's reference style, `<calcPr refMode="R1C1"/>` in `workbook.xml` (ECMA-376), is neither read nor written ([read.rs#L231](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/xlsx/src/read.rs#L231), [write.rs#L365](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/blob/11bb67386c9bb19b0717e21e98adc608162ae2e5/crates/xlsx/src/write.rs#L365)).

`docs/function-parity.md` lists "A1 and R1C1 references" as done, and `docs/target-app-parity.md` mentions an A1/R1C1 parser. Only the printer exists.

## Proposal

- A checkbox under File › Options › Formulas, and a command that sets `Prefs::r1c1`.
- With the option on:
  - column headers show numbers;
  - the Name Box shows and takes `R2C3`;
  - the formula bar and the cell editor show `print_r1c1` relative to the cell;
  - typed formulas are parsed as R1C1 relative to the cell, and stored as A1.
- Read `calcPr refMode`, and write it when the option is on.
- Correct the two docs until the option exists.

title: Thai and Chinese functions give #NAME? (THAIYEAR, ROUNDBAHTUP, NUMBERSTRING, …)

title: Fill color applies to hidden (filtered-out) rows instead of only visible cells
author: petya8bachey
body:
When an AutoFilter is active and the user applies a background/fill color to a selection, the color is applied to the entire rectangular range — including rows that are currently hidden by the filter. After clearing the filter, those previously hidden rows appear colored, which is incorrect.
Expected behavior (same as Excel/LibreOffice): fill color should be applied only to currently visible (non-filtered) cells. Hidden rows must not be modified by formatting commands while a filter is active.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a sheet with some data and apply an AutoFilter.
2. Filter a column so that some rows become hidden.
3. Select a range of cells (e.g., a column or a rectangular area).
4. Apply a background/fill color to the selection (via toolbar or format menu).
5. Clear the AutoFilter (show all rows).
6. Observe: the hidden rows that were filtered out are now colored, even though they were not visible when the color was applied.

**Expected result**

Only the rows that were visible at the moment of formatting should receive the background color. Hidden (filtered-out) rows must retain their previous formatting.

**Actual result**

The fill color is applied to the full rectangular range, including all hidden rows within that range.

**Environment**

GridCraft 0.12.1
Windows (x86_64)

title: Recalc: a running COUNTIFS over a growing range ($B$2:B2) is 13-19x slower than Excel and grows faster
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** GridCraft 0.12.1 windows-x64 portable (`gridcraft-cli`), Windows 11 Pro, compared with Excel for Microsoft 365 on the same PC.

**What happens:** a running count, i.e. one `COUNTIFS` per row whose ranges grow down to the row itself (`$B$2:B2`, `$B$2:B3`, …), recalculates 13–20× slower than in Excel, and the gap widens with the row count. In a real-world ledger-style workbook of ours (about 5,500 rows, two running-count columns with 3–4 criteria pairs each), these formulas alone account for roughly 17 s of a 65 s `info` (Excel opens the same file in about 2 s).

**Steps:** generate the workbooks with the script below (openpyxl, synthetic data), then time `gridcraft-cli info <file> --json`. Column F of each row holds

```
=COUNTIFS($B$2:B<r>,B<r>,$C$2:C<r>,C<r>,$D$2:D<r>,"Rent*")
```

<details><summary>Generator (Python + openpyxl)</summary>

```python
import sys
from openpyxl import Workbook
for n in map(int, sys.argv[1:]):
    wb = Workbook(); ws = wb.active; ws.title = 'Data'
    ws.append(['id', 'unit', 'payer', 'text', 'amount', 'count'])
    for i in range(n):
        r = i + 2
        ws.cell(r, 1, i + 1); ws.cell(r, 2, 'U%02d' % (i % 80)); ws.cell(r, 3, 'P%03d' % (i % 120))
        ws.cell(r, 4, ('Rent %02d' % (i % 12 + 1)) if i % 5 else 'Service charge'); ws.cell(r, 5, 500 + i % 300)
        ws.cell(r, 6, '=COUNTIFS($B$2:B%d,B%d,$C$2:C%d,C%d,$D$2:D%d,"Rent*")' % (r, r, r, r, r))
    wb.save('gc_running_countifs_%d.xlsx' % n)
```
`python gen.py 1000 2000 4000 8000`
</details>

**Measured** (one run each, wall time; Excel = own hidden instance via COM, `Workbooks.Open` + `CalculateFull`):

| rows | GridCraft `info` | Excel open + full recalc | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 0.2 s | 0.17 s | ~1× |
| 2,000 | 0.5 s | 0.12 s | ~4× |
| 4,000 | 1.9 s | 0.15 s | ~13× |
| 8,000 | 7.4 s | 0.38 s | ~19× |

Results are right: `run --in … --out …` saves the same values as Excel (sum of column F = 28,288 at 4,000 rows and 109,888 at 8,000 rows; last row 17…

title: Editing a long number shows 1.23E+19 instead of its digits, and pressing Enter switches the cell to Scientific format
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

Type a 20-digit number, such as `12345678901234567890`, into a cell. The cell shows it as `1.23457E+19`. That part is fine.

Then edit the cell again with F2 or the formula bar. The editor shows `1.23456789012346E+19` where the digits should be. Press Enter without changing anything, and the cell's format switches from General to Scientific. It now shows `1.23E+19`, or `#######` if the column is narrow.

So just opening a cell to look at it and pressing Enter changes how the number is shown. Anyone working with long IDs, account numbers or big totals runs into this.

Excel shows the number as plain digits while editing (`12345678901234500000`, cut to 15 significant digits). The format stays General after Enter.

## Evidence

![Editing B2: the formula bar and the in-cell editor show 1.23456789012346E+19 instead of the digits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/gridcraft/1eb2ab0d3432df479e4c399102b5b213aab7fe25/evidence/large-number-edit/edit-shows-E-notation.png)

*Boxed: the formula bar and the in-cell editor while editing B2. Both show E notation, not digits.*

![After pressing Enter: the number format box now says Scientific and B2 shows #######](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/gridcraft/1eb2ab0d3432df479e4c399102b5b213aab7fe25/evidence/large-number-edit/after-enter-format-scientific.png)

*Boxed: after Enter, the format box reads Scientific (it was General), and B2 shows `#######`.*

The same thing through the control channel (`gridcraft --control 7982`):

```text
$ gridcraft-cli send 7982 engine.execute '{"command":"cell.get","params":{"cell":"B1"}}'   # after typing 12345678901234567890, Enter
  "input": "1.23456789012346E+19",
  "num_fmt": "General",
  "text": "1.23457E+19",

# F2, then Enter with no change
  "input": "1.23456789012346E+19",
  "num_fmt": "0.00E+00",
  "text": "1.23E+19",
```

## Details

title: `gridcraft --help` opens an empty window instead of showing help
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

Typing `gridcraft --help` in a terminal shows no help. It opens an empty spreadsheet window instead. `gridcraft -h` does the same.

This hits anyone who starts GridCraft from a terminal or a script. They can't find out which options the app takes, such as `--control <port>`. The help text is the only place these options could be listed.

`gridcraft-cli --help` works, but asking one of its commands for help fails. `gridcraft-cli run --help` says "unknown option" and exits with an error.

What should happen: `--help` and `-h` print the options and exit, without opening a window. This should work for `gridcraft`, `gridcraft-cli`, and each `gridcraft-cli` command.

## Evidence

![Terminal output: gridcraft --help and -h print only a log line, and gridcraft-cli run --help says unknown option](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nael-Nathanael/gridcraft/d2d915f2608ae0c306d25a5d7df01503b0bb2048/evidence/help-flag/gridcraft-help.png)

```
$ gridcraft --help
2026-10-28T12:05:02.526Z INFO  [main] gridcraft: GridCraft 0.12.1, log file ~/.config/gridcraft/logs/gridcraft.log
   (no usage text; an empty "Book1" window opens and the command keeps running)

$ gridcraft -h
2026-10-28T12:05:10.623Z INFO  [main] gridcraft: GridCraft 0.12.1, log file ~/.config/gridcraft/logs/gridcraft.log
   (same: no usage text, a second empty "Book1" window opens)

$ gridcraft-cli run --help
gridcraft-cli: unknown option --help
$ echo $?
1

$ gridcraft-cli convert --help
gridcraft-cli: unknown option --help

$ gridcraft-cli run -h
gridcraft-cli: unexpected argument `-h`
```

## Details

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `gridcraft --help` in a terminal.
2. Run `gridcraft-cli run --help`.

**Expected:** each prints usage text and exits with code 0. No window opens.

**Actual:** `gridcraft` logs one line, opens an empty "Book1" window and keeps running. `gridcraft-cli run --help` prints `unknown option --help` and exits with code 1.
